statement: Strengthened T-CHERI, pair invocation atomicity (idc_write_axiom / idc_write_prop): any instruction that may invoke a data capability either invokes none, or writes exactly the expected code cap to PCC and data cap to C29 (both from the invoked sets), or raises an exception without writing C29, or hits an assertion failure.

statement: Theorem 8.1 (address translation soundness): if InUserMode, NonSecure, MMUEnabled_EL01, VirtDisabled, HwUpdatesFlags, UsingAArch64, DebugDisabled hold of s and the pure characterisation 'translate_address(vaddr, acctype, iswrite, aligned, size, s) = r', then every successful outcome (Value r', s') of AArch64_TranslateAddress satisfies 'r' ≈det addrdesc(r)' and 's' = update_descriptor(r, acctype, iswrite, s)'.
assumptions: 64-bit EL0 user mode, non-secure, single-stage (no virtualisation), MMU on, hardware access/dirty-flag update on, debug disabled; successful translations only (faults not modelled); undefined fields ignored (≈det); sequential Sail model; ASL->Sail translation trusted
map_note: G-CF/A-6 - candidate discharge of the fixed-translation assumption in Morello monotonicity (Bauereiss-22 §5.1)

statement: MiniSail kernel calculus: type safety and decidability of type checking (SMT-fragment constraints recorded exactly, others propagated in A-normal form).
assumptions: Proved of the MiniSail core, not of the full Sail implementation; mechanisation not stated in the read passage
map_note: A-4 - partial foundation for the trusted specification toolchain

statement: Abstract capability model: a Cap is capSealed : option (Sentry + Key), capPerms (Exec/System/Load/Store/Cap/Sealing/Unsealing), capCanStore and capCanBeStored label sets (Local/NonLocal, modelling SL and GL), explicit sets of sealing and unsealing keys, capAddrs as an explicit address SET (not base/top), capKeep* attenuation masks (modelling LM/LG), and a capCursor that 'can be out of bounds w.r.t. capAddrs ... In the formal model, any address is representable'; sealing does not check the cursor is in bounds, so sentry in-boundsness must be checked explicitly.
assumptions: Compressed encoding, representable range, and rounding are abstracted away entirely; the address set is exact
map_note: A: RP2 (YBNDSRW rounding) is out of scope at this layer by construction; the model assumes an exact address set

statement: RestrictUnsealed y z: z is a restriction of unsealed y iff capSealed equal and capPerms, capCanStore, capCanBeStored, capSealingKeys, capUnsealingKeys, capAddrs, capKeepPerms, capKeepCanStore, capKeepCanBeStored of z are each subsets of y's; the cursor may change arbitrarily.
assumptions: Definition of the single-step derivation relation; instructions are assumed (WfNormalInst) to produce only ReachableCap results
map_note: RP2+RP3: the abstract statement that bounds (capAddrs) and permissions only shrink on unsealed derivation

statement: RestrictSealed y z: for sealed y, z must have equal seal, equal perms, canStore, keys, addrs, keep* sets and equal cursor; only capCanBeStored may shrink (GL may be cleared on a sealed cap). The source comment calls this 'a quirk of CHERIoT' and gives a concrete scenario where it is harmful.
assumptions: Models CHERIoT's rule that CAndPerm on a sealed cap may clear only GL
map_note: RP5: sealed capabilities (incl. sentries) are immutable except for GL

statement: Restrict y z := if y unsealed then RestrictUnsealed else RestrictSealed.
assumptions: none beyond P-A2-002/003
map_note: RP1: the per-step authority order

statement: LoadCap x y z: a cap y may be loaded through x only if x is unsealed with Load and Cap permission, from a capability-aligned address range inside x.capAddrs whose readCap is inl y (i.e., tagged), and the loaded value is z = attenuate x y.
assumptions: readCap returns inl only when the tag is set (P-A2-037)
map_note: RP4+RP3: a capability enters a register from memory only if tagged, and attenuated by the authorising cap

statement: attenuate loadAuth loaded: if loaded is unsealed, its perms, canStore, keepPerms, keepCanStore, keepCanBeStored are intersected with loadAuth's keep* masks; if sealed they are kept unchanged; capCanBeStored is intersected in BOTH cases (comment: 'also a quirk of CHERIoT ... Ideally, no attenuation (implicit or explicit) must happen under a seal'); keys, addrs, cursor, seal unchanged.
assumptions: Models LM (drop Store/keep-Store) and LG (drop NonLocal from canBeStored) load attenuation
map_note: RP3: load-time permission attenuation; RP5 caveat that GL is attenuated even under a seal

statement: Seal x y z: z = y sealed with key k only if k is in x.capSealingKeys and both x and y are unsealed. Unseal x y z: z = y unsealed only if y is sealed with k, k is in x.capUnsealingKeys, and x is unsealed.
assumptions: Keys are abstract; sentries (inl) are never produced by Seal, only by call/ret instructions
map_note: RP5: seal/unseal are key-mediated; sentries cannot be unsealed by Unseal

statement: ReachableCap mem origSet c: inductive closure of origSet under Restrict, LoadCap (through mem), Seal, and Unseal. ReachableAddr lifts this to (addr, size, perms, canStore, canBeStored) tuples via unsealed reachable caps; ReachableRead/Write/Exec/RW/RWXAddr select by permission.
assumptions: Authority of a thread is defined as this closure from its register file, pcc, mepcc, mtcc, and trusted-stack caps
map_note: RP1: the definition of 'authority' that monotonicity is stated over

statement: ValidMemCapUpdate mem caps mem': every capability-slot whose readCap changed and now holds a tagged cap stDataCap must satisfy (a) stDataCap is ReachableCap from caps, and (b) there is a reachable, unsealed stAddrCap with Store and Cap permission covering the slot, and (c) some label l is both in stAddrCap.capCanStore and stDataCap.capCanBeStored (SL/GL check). ValidMemTagRemoval: a tag can be cleared only via such a stAddrCap. ValidMemDataUpdate: a byte can change only via a reachable unsealed Store cap covering it. ValidMemUpdate is the conjunction.
assumptions: Imposed on every Ok instruction by WfNormalInst/WfSystemInst (hypotheses); revocation, MMIO and DMA writes are not modelled
map_note: RP4: a tagged capability can be written to memory only by a reachable cap with Store+Cap; tags are never set by data stores

statement: ReachableMemSame m1 m2 caps / UpdatedMemSame: two memories agree on all data and tags reachable from caps, and updates agree where either memory changed; used to state that instructions depend only on reachable memory (FuncNormal/FuncSystem/FuncCallSentry/FuncRetSentry/FuncExn).
assumptions: Noninterference framing only; no proof uses FuncNormal yet
map_note: G-CF: 'behaviour is a function of reachable state' is the shape of a confidentiality lemma; none

statement: FuncNormal as written compares normalInst (rf,pcc,m1) with normalInst (rf,pcc,m1) -- both branches use m1, not m2 -- so the definition is trivially satisfiable and does not actually state memory-independence (likely a typo; FuncSystem, FuncCallSentry, FuncRetSentry correctly use m2).
assumptions: Defect in the artifact; no downstream lemma depends on FuncNormal's content
map_note: none: review finding to report upstream before G-CF2 reuses the definition

statement: WfNormalInst normalInst: for every ValidRf rf, pcc, mem, if the instruction returns Ok (rf',pcc',mem') then pcc has Exec, ValidMemUpdate mem (pcc::capsOfRf rf) mem', every cap in pcc'::capsOfRf rf' is ReachableCap from pcc::capsOfRf rf, pcc' has Exec, and rf' is valid; exceptions impose nothing.
assumptions: This IS the per-instruction monotonicity obligation; it is assumed of every decoded instruction (carried as a proof field of Inst_General) and never discharged against the CHERIoT Sail or any concrete ISA
map_note: RP1 (per-instruction form) and RP2/RP3/RP4 jointly: the hypothesis AIVHAI must discharge against RVY instruction semantics

statement: WfSystemInst systemInst pcc: as WfNormalInst but the root set additionally includes mepcc, mtcc and the trusted-stack caps, and pcc must have both Exec and System permission. WfGeneralInst: if pcc lacks System permission the instruction coincides with some WfNormalInst and leaves the system context unchanged; if it has System permission it satisfies WfSystemInst.
assumptions: User-mode code cannot touch mepcc/mtcc/trusted stack; system registers are reachable only with System (ASR) permission
map_note: G-CF: user mode cannot alter switcher state; RP1 extended to system-register authority

statement: WfCallSentryInst callSentryInst src optLink: on Ok (pcc',rf',ints'), pcc has Exec; register src holds a cap src_cap with Exec whose seal is a forward sentry (CallEnableInterrupt sets ints'=enabled, CallDisableInterrupt sets disabled, CallInheritInterrupt or unsealed keeps ints) and pcc' = src_cap unsealed; if a link register is given, all other registers are unchanged and the link holds a cap that is a RestrictUnsealed of pcc, sealed as RetEnableInterrupt/RetDisableInterrupt according to the current interrupt status, with Exec; otherwise rf' = rf.
assumptions: Backward sentries into the trusted-stack/MTCC domain are modelled only as sealed pcc restrictions; cursor in-boundsness of the sentry is not checked here (see P-A2-001)
map_note: RP5: the only way to unseal a sentry is to jump through it; the link register receives a sealed, not raw, return cap

statement: WfRetSentryInst retSentryInst src: on Ok (pcc',ints'), pcc has Exec, register src holds an Exec cap sealed as RetEnableInterrupt or RetDisableInterrupt (any other seal, including unsealed, is excluded by False), ints' follows the sentry, and pcc' is the unsealed cap.
assumptions: Unsealed returns unsupported (TODO in source)
map_note: RP5: return sentries restore interrupt posture atomically with control transfer

statement: Inst: every decoded instruction constructor (Inst_General, Inst_Call, Inst_Ret, Inst_Exn) carries a proof of its Wf* obligation as a field; decode : list Byte -> Inst is a Context hypothesis. Hence the whole ISA is assumed well-formed and nothing in the development connects the abstract instructions to CHERIoT's Sail.
assumptions: The gap between this abstract spec and the ISA is the entire instruction level
map_note: G-c: for AIVHAI the Wf* fields are exactly the refinement obligations the RVY (Sail) semantics must discharge

statement: FetchAddrsOk fetchAddrs: there is a fixed function from address to fetched-address set such that fetchAddrs mem1 a = fetchAddrs mem2 a whenever the two memories agree on the bytes at those addresses (tags are not required to agree: TODO).
assumptions: Context hypothesis in SwitcherProperty only
map_note: none

statement: fetchAddrsInBounds / ThreadStep: a thread step either executes threadStepFunction when the fetched addresses are within pcc.capAddrs, the cursor is in bounds, pcc is unsealed and has Exec (GoodThreadStep), or raises an exception with pccNotInBounds (BadUserFetch). exceptionState: on any exception the register file is preserved, pcc := mtcc, mepcc := old pcc, exception info recorded, trusted stack and liveness unchanged, interrupt status unchanged.
assumptions: Exceptions always vector to mtcc; no interrupt-disable on trap is modelled
map_note: G-CF: trap entry hands control to the switcher's MTCC with user registers intact

statement: SameThreadStep / MachineStep: only the current thread, and only if ThreadAlive, takes a ThreadStep; all other threads' states are unchanged; a thread switch (Ev_SwitchThreads) is permitted only when interrupts are enabled and changes nothing but the current-thread index. Traces record Ev_General, Ev_Call, Ev_Ret, Ev_Exception, and switches.
assumptions: Interleaving semantics with atomic thread switch; the scheduler is not modelled
map_note: G-CF: the operational model G-CF2 is expected to follow

statement: CHERIoTValidation.cheriot_cap / mk_abstract_cap: a concrete CHERIoT capability (6 compressed-permission formats MemCapRW/RO/WO, MemDataOnly, Executable, Sealing; 3-bit otype; base, length, addr with a proof base <= addr < base+length) is mapped to the abstract Cap: otypes 1..5 on executable caps become the five sentries, 6 and 7 become unsealed (TODO), data otypes become key seals; sealing/unsealing key := [addr]; capAddrs := [base, base+length); keepPerms drops Store unless LM; keepCanBeStored drops NonLocal unless LG; canStore includes Local iff SL; canBeStored includes NonLocal iff GL.
assumptions: Validation mapping only; no lemma is proved about it, and the addrInBounds field excludes out-of-bounds cursors that the abstract Cap allows
map_note: G-c: the concrete-to-abstract cap map AIVHAI needs for 64-bit RVY caps; the two 'quirk' comments (P-A2-003, P-A2-006) are encoded here

statement: ISA_CAPSIZE_BYTES_NONZERO: 2^ISA_LG_CAPSIZE_BYTES > 0.
assumptions: none
map_note: none

statement: AttenuateRestrict: for all x y, Restrict y (attenuate x y) -- load-time attenuation is a Restrict step.
assumptions: none
map_note: RP3: LM/LG attenuation never grants

statement: Restrict c c' implies: sealing keys of c' subset of c's (RestrictCapSealingKeysSubset); unsealing keys subset (RestrictCapUnsealingKeysSubset); capSealed equal (RestrictSealedEq); capAddrs subset (RestrictCapAddrsSubset).
assumptions: none
map_note: RP2 (addrs never grow) and RP5 (seal state preserved, keys never grow) at the abstract level

statement: Restrict is a preorder compatible with unsealing: RestrictRefl, RestrictTrans, RestrictSetCapUnsealed (Restrict y z -> Restrict (unseal y) (unseal z)), RestrictUnsealedOk, setCapSealedNoneEq, setCapSealed_inv.
assumptions: none
map_note: RP1: transitivity is what turns per-step monotonicity into sequence monotonicity

statement: Reachability is monotone in the root set and composes: ReachableCapIncrease (Subset caps capss -> ReachableCap caps c -> ReachableCap capss c), ReachableCaps_app, ReachableCapSubsetImpliesReachableCap, ReachableAddrSubset, ReachableRWXAddrSubset, StPermForAddrSubset, StPermForCapSubset, ValidMemTagRemovalSubset, ValidMemDataUpdateSubset, ValidMemCapUpdateSubset, ValidMemUpdateSubset.
assumptions: none
map_note: RP1 plumbing

statement: LoadCapUpdate / LoadCapUpdate': if x is ReachableCap in mem from caps, mem' is a ValidMemCapUpdate (resp. ValidMemUpdate) of mem by caps, and LoadCap mem' x y z, then z is ReachableCap in mem from caps -- loading from validly updated memory yields nothing new.
assumptions: none
map_note: RP1: the memory half of the inductive step (store-then-load cannot amplify)

statement: ReachableCap_ValidUpdate (and ReachableAddr_, ReachableReadAddr_, ReachableWriteAddr_, ReachableRWAddr_, ReachableCaps_ValidUpdate, ReachableCapSubset_ValidUpdate): if mem' is a ValidMemUpdate of mem by caps and caps' are reachable from caps in mem, then anything reachable from caps' in mem' was already reachable from caps in mem; ReachableCapSubset is therefore preserved across valid updates.
assumptions: none
map_note: RP1: the sequence-level monotonicity engine, proved from the Wf* hypotheses

statement: readCapImpliesTag: readCap mem capa = inl cap implies readTag mem capa = true.
assumptions: bytesToCap returns inl only when tag && decode succeeds
map_note: RP4: untagged memory never yields a capability

statement: Separation lemmas: RWAddressesDisjoint is symmetric and implies WriteReadDisjoint; WriteReadDisjointImpliesFalse (no reachable unsealed Store cap of one set overlaps a reachable Load cap of the other); LoadCapUpdateDisjointUnchanged, ReachableCapDisjointUnchanged', Reachable{,Read,Write,RW}AddrDisjointUnchanged, ReachableCapSubsetDisjointUnchanged', ReachableCapSubsetUpdateDisjointUnchanged: a ValidMemUpdate by caps that are write/read-disjoint from t changes nothing t can reach; RWAddressDisjointUpdate and RWAddressDisjointUpdateUnchanged: pairwise RW-disjointness of thread root sets is preserved by a valid update of one of them.
assumptions: Isolation is stated as disjointness of reachable RW address sets, not of compartments
map_note: G-CF: thread non-interference via disjoint reachable address sets

statement: generalInstOkCommon: any WfGeneralInst that returns Ok performs a ValidMemUpdate relative to (user caps ++ system caps), yields caps reachable from them, and a ValidRf. callSentryOkCommon: any Ok WfCallSentryInst yields ValidRf rf' and Exec in pcc'. ValidRfUpdate, SubsetCapsOfUserTS, SameThreadStep_lengthThreads, SameThreadStep_curId are structural.
assumptions: Direct unfolding of the Wf* hypotheses
map_note: RP1: bridge from per-instruction hypotheses to the step relation

statement: Configuration records: a Compartment is a PCC (code + read-only data incl. import entries), optional CGP (None = library), import entries (sealed cap to an export entry, or sentry to a library function), error handlers (offset, Stackful|Stackless), export entries (offset, stack size, num args, interrupt status), export-table addresses, and sealing caps; a Config is compartments, initial thread metadata (CSP, compartment), initial memory, and a SwitcherConfig (compartment index, entry addresses for compartment_switcher_entry, exception_entry_asm, switcher_after_compartment_call, error_handler_return, and the switcher's exclusive key). MMIO and shared objects are TODO.
assumptions: Static linkage; no MMIO, no shared objects, no heap/allocator, no revoker
map_note: G-CF2: the configuration vocabulary AIVHAI's CF model will instantiate for a 64-bit application core

statement: Initial-reachability well-formedness predicates: InitialCompartmentAddressesOk (every RWX address reachable from a compartment's caps is in its footprint); AllReachableCaps (caps reachable from a compartment are reachable without loading from memory, i.e. memory holds no extra caps for it); SentriesOnlyFromImportTables and SealedDataCapsOnlyFromImportTables (every reachable sentry / switcher-sealed data cap is declared in the import table).
assumptions: Loader/linker obligations (the 'auditable' capability set); marked 'TODO: Not sufficient; need to include sealed caps'
map_note: G-CF: loader-established invariants; RP5 (sentries exist only where audited)

statement: ValidPCCPerms: PCC perms subset of {Exec, System, Load, Cap} (no Store, Sealing, Unsealing) and no SL. ValidCGPPerms: subset of {Exec, System, Load, Store, Cap} and no SL. ValidSealingCap: perms subset of {Sealing, Unsealing}. WFImportEntry: a library import is a forward sentry inside a library footprint with PCC perms; an export import is sealed with the switcher key, has no Store, and lies in an export-table footprint.
assumptions: W^X and no-SL-on-globals are configuration assumptions, not derived from the encoding
map_note: G-CF: code/global capability shape; RP3 (code is not writable, globals cannot store Local caps)

statement: WFCompartment: InitialCompartmentAddressesOk, AllReachableCaps, PCC unsealed with ValidPCCPerms, CGP (if any) unsealed with ValidCGPPerms, SentriesOnlyFromImportTables, SealedDataCapsOnlyFromImportTables, all import entries WF, all sealing caps ValidSealingCap, and no compartment sealing cap can seal with the switcher's key. WFSwitcher c := True (placeholder). WFConfig: ConfigFootprints (compartment footprints, stack footprints, export-table footprints) pairwise Separated; every compartment WFCompartment; the switcher compartment exists; only the switcher compartment holds a cap with the switcher key among its unsealing keys.
assumptions: The switcher itself is unconstrained (WFSwitcher = True); its code is not modelled
map_note: G-CF: the top-level configuration hypothesis of ThreadIsolatedMonotonicity and compartment isolation

statement: Memory-stability predicates: SwitcherCodeUnchanged, ReadOnlyMemUnchanged (all compartments' PCC ranges equal initial memory incl. tags), ExportTablesUnchanged, NonStackMemPreserved (everything outside the thread's stack unchanged between two memories), MemEquivalentAtAddr/AtThread. GlobalMemInvariants bundles ReadOnlyMemUnchanged and ExportTablesUnchanged but is commented out of GlobalInvariant with 'TODO: prove these'.
assumptions: Not proved inductive; the switcher contracts assume them via SwitcherMemEquivAtThread
map_note: G-CF: code and export tables immutable at runtime -- unproved in the pin

statement: GlobalInvariant config m: machine_curThreadId < length threads and Forall2 ThreadInv (ValidRf per thread). Proved: InvariantInitial (ValidInitialState -> GlobalInvariant), GlobalInvariantImpliesValidRf, ThreadStep_ThreadInv, SameThreadStep_ThreadInv, SameThreadStepOk, GlobalInvariantStep (GlobalInvariant is preserved by every MachineStep).
assumptions: The invariant is weak (index validity and register-file length only) because the memory invariants are deferred
map_note: G-CF2: inductive-invariant scaffolding

statement: WFLookupExportTableCompartmentId: if the static lookup maps a cap to (cid, eid) then compartment cid exists, the cap's addresses lie in its export table, and entry eid exists. Defined with the comment 'TODO: add a well-formedness condition as below' and never assumed by any theorem; LookupExportTableCompartmentId itself is an unconstrained Context parameter.
assumptions: An unconstrained oracle: proofs that mention export-table lookup are only as strong as this parameter
map_note: A: G-CF2 must constrain the lookup (or derive it from memory) before compartment identity carries weight

statement: ValidCSP / mkCSP: a valid stack capability is unsealed, perms exactly {Load, Store, Cap}, can store Local and NonLocal caps (SL), can itself be stored only in Local slots (not GL), carries no keys, keeps all permissions on load, and covers a contiguous range [base, base+len) with cursor inside. ValidTrustedStackFrame: the frame's callee cap maps by lookup to (cid, eid) and its CSP is a ValidCSP that is a Restrict of the thread's initial CSP. ValidTrustedStack: every frame's CSP is valid and its callee export entry belongs to a non-library compartment.
assumptions: Stack pointers are the unique SL authority and are always local
map_note: G-CF: stack-capability invariants of the switcher

statement: ValidInitialThread: every cap reachable from a thread's user state is reachable from its initial CSP plus its initial compartment's caps; the trusted stack holds exactly one valid frame for the initial compartment; all tags in the stack footprint are initially clear; the initial CSP is a ValidCSP. UserModeOk / UserModeInvariant: every thread without System permission in its PCC has mtcc = MTCC config (an unsealed exec PCC over the switcher footprint at exception_entry_asm). ValidInitialState: memory = configInitMemory, Forall2 ValidInitialThread, GlobalInvariant, UserModeInvariant.
assumptions: Boot-time state; nothing about the scheduler, allocator or revoker
map_note: G-CF: initial-state obligations on the loader

statement: uniqueInitialProvenance: under WFConfig, an address has at most one provenance (stack of thread tid, or compartment cid). threadInConfigFootprint / compartmentInConfigFootprint locate footprints in ConfigFootprints.
assumptions: WFConfig_footprintDisjoint
map_note: G-CF: memory partition is a partition

statement: SwitcherProperty module intent: pre/postconditions for the switcher's entry points compartment_switcher_entry and exception_entry_asm and its backward sentries switcher_after_compartment_call and error_handler_return; the switcher is required to touch only the register file, the thread's own stack, and read-only global memory, which gives atomicity-by-disjointness so that postconditions are functions of the state at entry even with interrupts enabled; the interrupt handler is modelled as an atomic thread switch; MTDC is modelled as the trusted stack; instructions that clobber MTDC/spill areas are to be treated as atomic with interrupts disabled.
assumptions: Switcher source (cheriot-rtos sdk/core/switcher/entry.S) is referenced, not modelled; the scheduler call from the switcher is acknowledged as outside the switcher's code region (TODO)
map_note: G-CF: the switcher contract style; A: switcher-only-touches-own-stack is an assumption on code, not a theorem

statement: In_Switcher_Invariant tid st_init st: while in the switcher, PCC has System permission, all PCC addresses are in the switcher footprint, and fetch succeeds (fetchAddrsInBounds). SwitcherEntry_Invariant: the invariant holds for every memory that agrees with the entry memory on the thread's stack and leaves switcher code and export tables equal to initial memory (SwitcherMemEquivAtThread).
assumptions: Fetch assumed to succeed on the exception path because MEPCC is clobbered there
map_note: G-CF: the 'in TCB' state predicate

statement: Post_UnwindStackBase (via unwindStackOk, PostRf_UnwindStack, PostRfSpec_UnwindStack): popping the top trusted-stack frame with CSP tcsp requires a second frame to exist; afterwards mtcc = MTCC, mepcc = new pcc (TODO relax), the trusted stack is the tail, interrupt status unchanged; memory from the stack base up to tcsp.cursor + SPILL_SLOT_SIZE is zeroed with tags cleared and all other memory unchanged, and the stack had Store authority over that range; PCC and ra, gp, s0, s1 are restored from the spill slots read through tcsp; sp = tcsp + SPILL_SLOT_SIZE; a0, a1 carry the return values (ret0/ret1); every other register is zeroBytes. Post_UnwindStackForced sets a0 = compartmentFailValue, a1 = 0; Post_UnwindStackReturnOk passes a0/a1 through.
assumptions: TODO: interrupt status, CSR_MSHWM (stack high-water mark) not modelled; stack zeroing is keyed on the trusted CSP, never on the untrusted one
map_note: G-CF: stack-clearing and register-clearing obligations on return (ephemeral delegation)

statement: ExceptionEntry_Pre: pcc = MTCC, ValidTrustedStack, and the entry invariant. ExceptionEntry_Post: back in user mode and one of (1) Stackful handler: untrusted csp from the register file is a ValidUntrustedCSP; a 16-slot spill frame (PCC=mepcc with tag cleared, 15 registers) is written below it and nothing else changes; interrupts enabled; error counter of the top frame incremented; PCC = compartment PCC + a declared Stackful handler offset; ra = IRQ-enabling backward sentry to error_handler_return; gp = pristine callee CGP; sp = a0 = csp - SPILL_FRAME_SIZE; a1 = mcause; a2 = mtval; others zero; (2) Stackless handler: memory unchanged, sp = tcsp restricted to addresses below its cursor and reset to its base (comment: 'NB!!: this means a compartment can regain stack caps after an exception!'), a0 = mcause, a1 = mtval, rest zero; (3) forced unwind (Post_UnwindStackForced); (4) thread dead; and in all cases only the thread's stack changed.
assumptions: Comments record that the real implementation clobbers mtdc and the trusted-stack spill context and reads/writes through an untrusted csp that might point to globals ('TODO: Here, we assume we checked the integrity of the csp'); case (3) 'Exit the thread? TODO'
map_note: G-CF: the error-handler contract; A: csp-integrity check is assumed

statement: ExceptionHandlerOk: for all tid and entry state satisfying ExceptionEntry_Pre, along every ThreadStep sequence the thread remains in system mode with the entry invariant UNTIL it is in user mode satisfying ExceptionEntry_Post (Combinators.until). No liveness ('TODO: liveness?'); not lifted from thread-local to the machine level ('TODO: lift thread-local property to machine').
assumptions: A specification of the switcher code, with no proof and no model of the code it specifies
map_note: G-CF2: the obligation AIVHAI's CF model must actually prove (the pin states it only)

statement: ExceptionReturn_Pre (pcc = ErrorHandlerReturnPCC, valid trusted stack, invariant) / ExceptionReturn_Post (user mode; forced unwind or thread dead; only stack changed) / ExceptionReturnOk (until-form). The install-context return path (a0 = 0: reload registers from the untrusted csp) is commented out pending cheriot-rtos issue 559 because the current switcher reads globals and needs interrupts disabled.
assumptions: Only the unwind outcome of error-handler return is specified
map_note: G-CF: error-handler return; A: install-context path excluded

statement: CompartmentCall_Pre (pcc = CompartmentCallPCC, valid trusted stack, invariant). CCall_Post_Ok: the initial sp holds a ValidCSP; t1 holds a cap sealed with the switcher key whose unsealing maps to (compartment, entry); a new trusted frame with CSP = init_csp with cursor - SPILL_SLOT_SIZE and the unsealed export cap is pushed; mepcc, liveness unchanged; mtcc = MTCC; interrupt status := the export entry's; pcc = compartment PCC + export offset; ra = backward sentry (RetEnable/RetDisable per the entry) to switcher_after_compartment_call; gp = callee CGP; sp = init_csp restricted to addresses below the new TCSP cursor minus STACK_ENTRY_RESERVED_SPACE; a0..a5, t0 preserved iff their index < numArgs else zeroed; every other register zero; the callee's stack region is zeroed with tags cleared. ('TODO: check for stack size'; spill of ra/gp/s0/s1 is defined in compartmentCallMemOk but CCall_Post_Ok uses only compartmentCalleeStackZeroed.)
assumptions: Stack-size check and alignment/underflow TODO; no MSHWM
map_note: G-CF: cross-compartment call contract (least privilege on entry); RP5 (export entries reachable only via switcher-sealed caps)

statement: CCall_Post_NotEnoughStack: system context unchanged except exception info, memory unchanged, pcc = the caller's ra, a0 = notEnoughStackValue, a1 = 0, all other registers unchanged. CompartmentCall_Post: user mode and (Ok | NotEnoughStack | forced unwind | thread dead) and only the stack changed. CompartmentCallOk: until-form from the precondition.
assumptions: As P-A2-045
map_note: G-CF

statement: CompartmentReturn_Pre (pcc = CompartmentCallPCC, valid trusted stack, call invariant) / CompartmentReturn_Post (user mode; Post_UnwindStackReturnOk with a0/a1 from the callee, or thread dead; only stack changed) / CompartmentReturnOk (until-form). The callee is responsible for zeroing unused return registers; the switcher zeroes the rest.
assumptions: Precondition reuses the call entry PCC rather than the switcher_after_compartment_call address
map_note: G-CF: return contract

statement: UserModeInvariants (mepcc = MTCC, valid trusted stack), ThreadInv' (ValidRf and, when not in system mode, UserModeInvariants), GlobalInvariants (GlobalMemInvariants and Forall2 ThreadInv'): marked 'TODO: move these under Configuration and prove they are inductively preserved'.
assumptions: Not used by any theorem
map_note: G-CF2: the intended strengthened invariant, unproved

statement: ReachableCompartment (audit graph): c1 -> c2 and c2 -> c1 if c1 imports a switcher-sealed cap into c2's footprint; c1 -> l if c1 imports a sentry into l's footprint (directed); reflexive on valid indices; transitive. MutuallyIsolatedCompartment idx1 idx2: both are non-library compartments and idx1 cannot reach idx2.
assumptions: Libraries may be shared without connecting their clients (C1 -> L <- C2 does not connect C1 and C2)
map_note: G-CF: the static isolation relation the loader audit is supposed to establish

statement: IsolatedFromCompartment mem srcCaps cid := no RWX address reachable from srcCaps lies in compartment cid; no reachable sentry points into cid; no reachable cap sealed with the switcher key points into cid. CompartmentIsolation m: for every pair of mutually isolated compartments, c1's initial caps are IsolatedFromCompartment idx2 in m's memory. CompartmentIsolatedThreads m: every thread currently in user compartment idx1 (no System perm, top trusted frame maps to idx1) has user-state caps IsolatedFromCompartment idx2. InitialProperty := GlobalInvariant and UserModeInvariant and CompartmentIsolation and CompartmentIsolatedThreads.
assumptions: Isolation is about addresses, sentries, and switcher-sealed caps only; data-sealed caps with other keys and MMIO are not covered
map_note: G-CF: the isolation property statement

statement: ExceptionStepOk__User: if the current thread is in user mode and takes an exception step (memory unchanged; pcc := mtcc; mepcc := pcc; other threads unchanged) and GlobalInvariant holds before and after, then InitialProperty' (UserModeInvariant, CompartmentIsolation, CompartmentIsolatedThreads) is preserved -- because the trapped thread leaves user mode and the others are untouched.
assumptions: The only step kind for which isolation preservation is proved
map_note: G-CF: trap preserves isolation (one case of the missing inductive step)

statement: ReachableViaCallRet caps caps' and WfCallSentryInst_CapsReached: after an Ok call-sentry instruction from a ValidRf with unsealed pcc, every cap in pcc'::rf' is either an old cap, or the sealing (as a sentry) of a RestrictUnsealed of an old unsealed cap (the link), or the unsealing of an old sentry (the target).
assumptions: WfCallSentryInst hypothesis
map_note: RP5+RP1: a sentry call changes authority only by sealing a restriction of pcc and unsealing the invoked sentry

statement: AddressesInitiallyIsolated and PCompartmentIsolation_InitCompartments: in any ValidInitialState of a WFConfig, distinct compartments' initial caps reach no RWX address of each other, and mutually isolated compartments share no sentries or switcher-sealed caps (CompartmentIsolation holds initially). Subset lemmas (AddrsIsolatedFromCompartmentSubset, SentriesIsolatedFromCompartmentSubset, SealedDataCapsIsolatedFromCompartmentSubset, IsolatedFromCompartmentSubset) are antitone in the source set.
assumptions: WFConfig, ValidInitialState
map_note: G-CF: initial compartment isolation follows from footprint separation and audited imports

statement: ReachableCapRestrictCSP: adding an unsealed, keyless cap x whose covered memory is entirely untagged to a root set adds no reachable cap other than restrictions of x itself. InitialThreadCapSubset, IsolatedFromCompartmentInitialThread, ValidInitialThreadImpliesCompartment, PCompartmentIsolation_InitThreads: hence an initial thread in compartment idx1, whose stack is untagged, is isolated from every compartment idx1 cannot reach.
assumptions: Stack initially untagged (ValidInitialThread_stackUntagged)
map_note: G-CF: a fresh stack capability confers no cross-compartment authority

statement: InitialPropertyHolds: ValidInitialState config m -> InitialProperty (m, []). The module comment states its scope: 'This module just validates the initial configuration setup'; there is no lemma that InitialProperty (or CompartmentIsolation) is preserved by MachineStep in general (only the exception case, P-A2-053).
assumptions: Initial state only; compartment isolation over execution is NOT proved in the pin
map_note: G-CF: initial-state half of compartment isolation; the inductive half is open

statement: SameDomainEvent / SameDomainTrace: a trace is same-domain iff every event is a thread switch or Ev_SameThread _ Ev_General; any Ev_Call, Ev_Ret or Ev_Exception makes the trace non-same-domain. ThreadReachableCapSubset m_init m_cur t_init t_cur := everything reachable from capsOfThread t_cur in m_cur was reachable from capsOfThread t_init in m_init. IsolatedThreads m := pairwise RWAddressesDisjoint over threads' cap sets. ValidInitialMachine := ValidInitialState and IsolatedThreads. IsolatedMonotonicity m := Forall2 ThreadReachableCapSubset from the initial machine. PThreadIsolatedMonotonicity (m, tr) := SameDomainTrace tr -> IsolatedMonotonicity m.
assumptions: 'Same-domain' = sentry-free and trap-free; cross-domain steps are excluded by making the property vacuous on such traces
map_note: RP1: this is RP1's exact statement shape ('no sentry-free, trap-free sequence increases authority'), at the whole-thread level

statement: SameDomainStepOk: given GlobalInvariant before and after, Invariant' (IsolatedThreads and IsolatedMonotonicity) and a same-domain SameThreadStep, Invariant' holds after: the stepping thread's reachable set shrinks (ReachableCapSubset_ValidUpdate) and the others' are unchanged because its writes are disjoint from their reads (ReachableCapSubsetUpdateDisjointUnchanged); pairwise disjointness is preserved (RWAddressDisjointUpdate*).
assumptions: generalInstOkCommon (hence WfGeneralInst); IsolatedThreads
map_note: RP1: the inductive step

statement: InvariantInitial, GlobalInvariant_length, InvariantImpliesThreadReachableCapSubset, IsolatedImpliesWriteReadDisjoint, InvariantStep (Invariant preserved by every MachineStep, where Invariant := GlobalInvariant and (SameDomainTrace -> Invariant')), InvariantUse (Invariant -> PThreadIsolatedMonotonicity).
assumptions: none beyond module context
map_note: RP1

statement: Theorem ThreadIsolatedMonotonicity: for every config and initial_machine, WFConfig config -> ValidInitialMachine config initial_machine -> Combinators.always MachineStep (PThreadIsolatedMonotonicity initial_machine) (initial_machine, []): along every execution, as long as the trace contains only general instructions and thread switches (no sentry calls/returns, no exceptions), each thread's reachable capability set in the current memory is a subset of what it could reach in the initial state, and threads' RW address sets stay pairwise disjoint. Proved by Establish/Preserve/Use with Invariant; Qed; no Admitted, Axiom, Hypothesis or Parameter anywhere in the development (grep: 0 hits); 34 Qed in Properties.v, 53 in SpecLemmas.v.
assumptions: Section hypotheses: fetchAddrs, decode producing Wf*-certified instructions (the whole ISA level), pccNotInBounds, an unconstrained LookupExportTableCompartmentId; WFConfig (loader); IsolatedThreads initially (pairwise RW-disjoint threads, i.e. no shared writable memory at all); memory invariants (read-only code, export tables) not proved; property is vacuous on traces with calls, returns or traps
map_note: RP1: the closest mechanized precedent for RP1, but at the abstract-model level with the per-instruction obligations assumed; also G-CF (thread isolation) in the sentry-free fragment

statement: Combinators.always step P initial: exists invariant with Establish (invariant initial), Preserve (invariant s -> step s t -> invariant t), Use (invariant s -> P s). Combinators.until step P Q initial: Q initial, or P initial and until holds after every step. (eventually is commented out.)
assumptions: Inductive definitions; until has no liveness content (vacuous on stuck states)
map_note: G-CF2: the proof-rule shape to reuse

statement: encodableCap c (definition): the two inferred MSBs of T equal the MSBs of B plus the internal-exponent length bit plus the carry from Tbot < Bbot; internal_E or E = 0; and if internal_E then the low internal_E_take_bits of B and T are zero. validBounds c (definition): E <= cap_max_E; at E = cap_max_E, Tmsb = 0 and the top two bits of B are 00; at E = cap_max_E - 1, Bmsb = 0.
assumptions: Definitions used as hypotheses of the properties below; the Capability record carries derived fields (inferred T MSBs, separate E) that the in-memory format does not
map_note: RP2 support: the canonical-encoding invariant AIVHAI must carry as a global invariant for RVY (RVY's analogue is capIsMalformed, P-A2-110)

statement: propEncodableCorrect: encodableCap c <-> memBitsToCapability(c.tag, capToMemBits(c)) == c (a Capability record is encodable iff the memory round-trip is the identity).
assumptions: Checked for the 128-bit CHERI Concentrate encoding (MW=14) of sail-cheri-riscv circa 2021; the register entry notes the repository is unmaintained since 2022 and partly bit-rotted, so 'checked' is as of the pin, not re-run
map_note: RP4 support (bit-exact decode/encode); exact precedent for an RVY round-trip property, which RVY currently only asserts (P-A2-108)

statement: propDecodeEncodable: for all capBits and tag, encodableCap(memBitsToCapability(tag, capBits)).
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: RP4 support: every bit pattern decodes to an encodable record

statement: propDefaultCapEncodable / propNullCapEncodable: default_cap and null_cap are encodable.
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: none: root/null well-formedness

statement: propSetBoundsEncodable: if c is encodable and reqBase <= reqTop then setCapBounds(c, reqBase, reqTop) is encodable. propSealEncodable: sealing with otype <= cap_max_otype preserves encodability. propUnsealEncodable: unsealing preserves encodability. Comment: other manipulations do not change bounds or otype and trivially preserve it.
assumptions: as P-A2-064; closure of the encodable set under the three bounds/otype-changing helpers
map_note: RP2 support: the inductive closure of canonical encoding under YBNDSRW/seal/unseal

statement: propSetBoundsValid: if reqBase <= reqTop <= 2^64 then setCapBounds(c, reqBase, reqTop) has validBounds. propSetBoundsInstrValid: the instruction form (base = c.address, top = base + len) yields validBounds whenever top <= 2^64. Comment: 'for any (encodable) capability ultimately derived from the initial capability in a monotonic way, base <= top should hold'.
assumptions: Top at or below 2^64 (the initial capability's top); reachable-capability hypothesis stated in prose only
map_note: RP2 support: setCapBounds never produces the high-exponent degenerate encodings

statement: propBaseLeqTop: encodableCap(c) and validBounds(c) imply base <= top for (base, top) = getCapBounds(c).
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: RP2 support: non-negative length for canonical caps (RVY asserts this inside getCapLength instead, P-A2-106)

statement: propBuildCapValidEq: for encodable c with validBounds and an encodable, tagged, unsealed auth, re-deriving c via setCapBounds(auth, base(c), top(c)), setCapOffset, setCapPerms, setCapFlags yields exactly unsealCap(c) with tag = true and auth's reserved bits (CBuildCap recreates the bit pattern modulo reserved bits).
assumptions: No check that c's bounds/perms are within auth's; that is CBuildCap's instruction-level check
map_note: RP4 adjacent: tag re-derivation is exact only within an authorising cap (YBLD in RVY)

statement: propSetBounds: for (exact, newCap) = setCapBounds(c, reqBase, reqTop): (reqBase <= reqTop) -> (exact <-> newBase = reqBase and newTop = reqTop); and if c encodable, reqBase <= reqTop <= 2^64, and origBase <= reqBase and reqTop <= origTop (request monotonic) then newBase <= reqBase and reqTop <= newTop (request satisfied) and origBase <= newBase and newTop <= origTop (bounds monotonic) and, if validBounds(c), E does not increase.
assumptions: Preconditions 'corresponding to the checks performed by the CSetBounds instructions'; reachable caps with top <= 2^64
map_note: RP2: THE exact precedent for 'bounds never widen under rounding' (YBNDSRW); covers rounding-down of base and rounding-up of top simultaneously, plus exactness-flag correctness and exponent monotonicity

statement: propSetOffset / propIncOffset: if setCapOffset (resp. incCapOffset) reports representable, the decoded bounds are unchanged.
assumptions: Only the representable => bounds-unchanged direction; the converse (representable range characterisation) is the commented-out counterexample P-A2-079
map_note: RP2: address mutation (YADDRW/YADDIW analogue) cannot move bounds when the representability check passes

statement: propSetLSBs: changing the low MW-3 bits of the address never changes the decoded bounds (always representable).
assumptions: MW = cap_mantissa_width (14 for 128-bit caps)
map_note: RP2 support: fast-path representability

statement: propSetBoundsSmallExact: setting bounds from c.address with length < 2^(MW-2) is always exact with the requested base and top.
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: RP2 support: exactness envelope (RVY: lengths below 2^(MW-2) exact; CHERIoT analogue is 511 bytes)

statement: propRepresentableSetBoundsExact: if c.address is aligned to CRAM(len) and len = CRRL(len) then setCapBounds from c.address with len is exact. propPowerOfTwoRepresentable: naturally aligned power-of-two-length bounds are always exact. propZeroLenRepresentable: zero-length bounds are exact for any base.
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: none: allocator-support soundness (CRRL/CRAM), feeds exact-bounds obligations rather than RP2 itself

statement: propRepresentableBoundsMono: if the unaligned request (reqBase, reqBase+reqLen) is within c's bounds, c is encodable, and CRRL does not overflow to zero, then the CRAM/CRRL-aligned request (reqBase & mask, + repLen) is also within c's bounds.
assumptions: noLenOverflow: CRRL returns 0 when the representable length would round to 2^64
map_note: RP2: aligning a monotonic request stays monotonic

statement: propRepresentableLengthIdempotent: CRRL(CRRL(len)) = CRRL(len). propRepresentableMaskLengthAbsorb: CRAM(CRRL(len)) = CRAM(len) unless CRRL overflows to zero.
assumptions: as P-A2-064
map_note: none: CRRL/CRAM algebra

statement: propSetCurrentBoundsExact: for encodable c0 with validBounds, CSetOffset to 0 then CSetBoundsExact with the current length is representable, exact, and returns c1 unchanged (setting a capability's bounds to its own bounds is the identity). Note: length computed in bitvector arithmetic because integer modulo is unsupported in the SMT backend.
assumptions: Canonical encoding assumed to rule out negative lengths
map_note: RP2 support: idempotence of bounds-setting

statement: $counterexample propSetOffset (COMMENTED OUT, 'TODO: Elaborate on the representable range, as in this earlier attempt'): intended to characterise the representable range as (-len, 6*len) around the bounds and to show representable <-> bounds unchanged; not active.
assumptions: Not checked; the only $counterexample in the file and it is disabled
map_note: RP2: an open precedent for a full representable-range characterisation AIVHAI could complete for RVY

statement: propSpecifiedRequiredAlignment: the 'CHERI Concentrate Alignment Requirements' as documented in the ISA (no alignment when I_E = 0; otherwise base and top aligned to 2^(E+3+C) with E = 52 - clz(l[64:13]) and carry C) are exactly ~CRAM(length) + 1, i.e. the documented rule is necessary and sufficient.
assumptions: MW = 14, 64-bit addresses
map_note: none: spec-prose vs model consistency check; a template for checking RVY's documented alignment rule against the Sail

statement: forallBaseAndLen / forallCap (quantification helpers): properties are stated over capabilities obtained as setAddr(setBounds(setAddr(almightyCap, base), len), addr) when both calls are exact, treating (base = 0, len = all-ones) as the almighty capability; the file states as an ASSUMPTION that every valid capability is reachable this way 'ignoring those calls that return capabilities with inexact bounds', justified by prop_unique and prop_exact.
assumptions: Only bounds and addresses are covered ('Only caring about bounds and addresses of capabilities here'); permissions, otype, flags, tag-clearing are out of scope
map_note: A: a reachability-from-root assumption that an RTL-level RP2 proof must either adopt or discharge

statement: prop_unique: two successive exact setBounds calls from almighty (base,len) then (newBase,newLen), with newBase >= base and newBase+newLen <= base+len and the result valid, yield the same in-memory bits as a single exact setBounds(almighty, newBase, newLen) -- chains of setBounds collapse to one.
assumptions: Exactness of all intermediate calls; checking harness not in the file
map_note: RP2 support: canonicity of derived encodings (the CHERIoT spec's 'canonical encoding' hypothesis, stated here for cheri-cap-lib)

statement: prop_exact: if setBounds(setAddr(almighty, base), len) is inexact, then setBounds from the resulting base with the resulting length is exact (every inexact result is some exact result), provided the resulting length is not all-ones.
assumptions: as P-A2-081
map_note: RP2 support: justifies quantifying over exact results only

statement: prop_exactConditions: with (mask, length) from setBoundsCombined(nullCap, len), setBounds(setAddr(almighty, base & mask), length) is exact (CRAM/CRRL-aligned requests are exact).
assumptions: as P-A2-081
map_note: none: BSV counterpart of propRepresentableSetBoundsExact (P-A2-075)

statement: prop_getBase / prop_getTop / prop_getLength: for every capability obtained from almighty by exact setBounds(base, len) and any exact setAddr, getBase = base, getTop = base + len (or 2^64 for almighty), getLength = len.
assumptions: as P-A2-081
map_note: G-c: decoder correctness of the RTL library (getBase/getTop/getLength agree with the request)

statement: prop_setAddr: for any address within [base - 32, base + len + 32], setAddr is exact and getAddr returns it (a minimum 32-byte representable slack on either side of the bounds).
assumptions: 'How far out-of-bounds can we go in general?' -- tolerance 32 is a chosen test bound, not the full representable range
map_note: none: usability (no spurious tag loss); contrast CHERIoT, whose representable range may equal the bounds (P-A2-096)

statement: prop_isInBounds: provided base + len does not wrap, isInBounds(cap, False) <-> getAddr >= getBase and getAddr < getTop. Comment: 'TODO: the nowrap condition is required (but probably should not be)'.
assumptions: Wrap-around at 2^64 excluded, flagged as a probable library defect
map_note: G-c: bounds-check predicate agrees with decoded bounds; A: the no-wrap caveat is an open RTL-library concern for CVA6-CHERI

statement: prop_fromToMem: pack(toMem(fromMem(unpack(in)))) == in for every 128-bit in-memory pattern (memory round-trip identity).
assumptions: Untagged bit patterns included
map_note: RP4 support (bit-exact copy); BSV counterpart of propEncodableCorrect/propDecodeEncodable

statement: prop_setBounds: for every reachable capability cap and any new_len, if setBounds(cap, new_len).value is a valid (tagged) capability then getBase(cap) <= getBase(new_cap) and getTop(cap) >= getTop(new_cap) -- bounds never widen.
assumptions: Stated over the library's CapPipe type used by CVA6-CHERI/Flute/Toooba; relies on the tag-clearing inside setBounds; exactness not required
map_note: RP2: the RTL-library statement of bounds monotonicity; the G-c refinement target for YBNDSRW on CVA6-CHERI

statement: Guarded manipulation (CHERI inheritance): 'the bounds may be narrowed, but neither widened nor displaced; permissions may be shed but not regained; and tag bits may be cleared but never set'; each memory access must be authorised by a valid capability in a register cited by the instruction, in bounds and permitted.
assumptions: Paper-level claim; the checked properties are deferred to the Sail/SMT (P-A2-097)
map_note: RP2+RP3+RP4: the informal statement of all three

statement: Compartmentalised memory safety (eight obligations): for any object owned by compartment A, compartment B must not be able to (1) access it unless passed a pointer, (2) access outside its bounds, (3) access it after free, (4) hold a pointer to an on-stack object after the call, (5) hold a temporarily delegated pointer beyond a single call, (6) modify an object passed by immutable reference, (7) modify anything reachable from a deeply immutable reference, (8) tamper with an opaque (sealed) reference; guaranteed for static data, stack and heap, and enforced only across compartments.
assumptions: Heap guarantees hold for all code outside the allocator compartment; intra-compartment safety is a compiler matter
map_note: G-CF: the informal top-level isolation goal; (8) is RP5 in prose

statement: Permission ontology and W^X: 12 architectural permissions (GL, LD, SD, MC, SL, LG, LM, EX, SR, SE, US, U0); 'Capabilities may not simultaneously permit execution and stores, guaranteeing W^X at the hardware level'; sealing permissions are separated because their bounds name otypes; three capability roots (writable memory, executable memory, sealing) present at reset and expected to be erased by early boot.
assumptions: W^X is a property of the 6-bit compressed formats (Figure 2), not an additional check
map_note: RP3: permission lattice structure; G-CF: three roots at reset

statement: Load Global (LG) acts recursively: capabilities loaded via a cap without LG have LG cleared and are marked local; Load Mutable (LM) clears LM and store permissions on loaded capabilities (read-only sharing of a whole data structure).
assumptions: Combined with stack zeroing on return to make delegated caps ephemeral
map_note: RP3: transitive load attenuation (modelled by capKeep* in P-A2-006)

statement: Sentries for interrupt control: three forward sentry types (enable, disable, inherit interrupts), unsealed automatically only when used as a jump target and otherwise unusable; on jump-and-link the link register is written with the sentry type that restores the current posture; two further otypes reserved for return sentries of each posture. Hence a compartment can be granted the right to call a function with interrupts disabled without being able to disable interrupts arbitrarily.
assumptions: Later revisions distinguish forward/backward arcs (footnote 4)
map_note: RP5: sentry opacity and posture atomicity, informal; mechanized counterpart P-A2-014/015

statement: Encoding: 64-bit capability = R(1) | p(6) | o(3) | E(4) | B(9) | T(9) | a(32); six compressed permission formats; two disjoint sets of 7 otypes selected by EX (0 = unsealed), five executable otypes for sentries; bounds decode by inserting B and T at bit e of a with corrections c_b, c_t in {-1, 0, 1} from a_mid < B and T < B (Figure 3); E = 0xf encodes exponent 24; objects up to 511 bytes always exact; larger objects aligned per e.
assumptions: 32-bit addresses; one spare bit
map_note: RP2 context: the compressed encoding whose rounding RP2 is about (for RVY the fields differ: see P-A2-109)

statement: Representable range trade-off: 'the CHERIoT encoding has no such guarantee: in the worst case the representable range is equal to the object bounds, and in all cases addresses below the base are invalid'; moving the address outside the representable range invalidates the capability.
assumptions: Accepted compatibility cost; hypothesised that embedded code is careful with pointer arithmetic
map_note: RP2: address mutation outside the range clears the tag rather than moving bounds

statement: 'we implemented encoding and decoding in Sail and used its SMT solver backend to check some important properties of the encoding scheme. For brevity, we do not elaborate further here.' -- the paper names no property; the checked set lives in the CHERIoT ISA specification Appendix B.1 (prop_decEnc, prop_andperms, prop_setbounds, prop_setbounds_monotonic, prop_setaddr, prop_repbounds, prop_repbounds_c, prop_crrl_cram, root/null properties; census B8).
assumptions: Claim only; properties not enumerated in this source
map_note: RP2/RP3: pointer to the CHERIoT SMT precedents catalogued under B8

statement: Hardware load filter invariant: 'no capabilities that point to freed memory can be loaded into registers' -- on every capability load the base of the loaded cap indexes a revocation bit and, if set, the tag is cleared before writeback; footnote 6: this relies on tags identifying pointers precisely, on monotonicity of capability bounds, and on correctness of the bounds set by the allocator.
assumptions: Spatial safety (allocator bounds), heap-only revocation bits, 8-byte granules
map_note: none directly (temporal safety is outside AIVHAI's RP set) but it is stated as a consequence of RP2+RP4

statement: Background revoker race: a store from the main pipeline to an address held in flight by the revoker must be detected and the word reloaded, else the revoker's write-back of an invalidated word clobbers the new store; multi-core systems would need the revoker to snoop all memory traffic.
assumptions: Single-core; software revoker avoids the race by disabling interrupts
map_note: none: microarchitectural atomicity obligation relevant to a DMA-capable (NPU) design

statement: Temporal safety claim: memory chunks return to free lists only after a full revocation cycle, so 'it is impossible for allocations to temporally alias'; because the load filter consults quarantine bits, 'UAF accesses in general are impossible as soon as free() has returned'.
assumptions: Allocator compartment trusted; epochs; sweep completes
map_note: none

statement: Scoped delegation via local/global: compartment global pointers have SL cleared; the switcher's provided stack is the only SL storage, so caller arguments stripped of G cannot be stored outside the callee's stack; the stack is zeroed by the switcher on return, destroying delegated references; stack high-water mark CSRs (SR-protected) bound the zeroing cost.
assumptions: Code capability read-only; CGP has no SL
map_note: G-CF: ephemeral delegation (mechanized as capCanStore/capCanBeStored plus stack zeroing in P-A2-043/047)

statement: Unforgeability and monotonicity (section 5.3): 'a pointer is unforgeable and can only decrease rights ... CHERI instructions can only increase the base, decrease the top or remove permissions. As a result, a pointer pointing to freed memory must have a base field pointing to revocation bits that have been set'.
assumptions: Informal; no proof artifact in the paper
map_note: RP1+RP2+RP3+RP4 in one sentence; the paper's only monotonicity statement

statement: No $property or $counterexample exists anywhere in the pinned RVY Sail model: grep over every *.sail in CHERI-Alliance/sail-cheri-riscv (commit 71610658, 2026-10-06) and its sail-riscv submodule (395f655, zcheri-0.9.3-12) returns nothing; no properties/, verif/ or SMT directory exists; the Makefile's only SMT line (435) is commented out.
assumptions: The model implements the riscv-cheri (RVY) specification, not CHERI ISAv9; README notes the code is 'a bit messy' after extraction from Codasip's internal fork
map_note: RP2/RP3/RP4: there is NO upstream encoding property for RVY; everything AIVHAI needs must be ported from P-A2-063..080 or written fresh

statement: assert(E >= 0, 'Cap is malformed if E<0') in getCapBoundsBits, after an early return None() for malformed caps: bounds are decoded only for non-malformed capabilities and the exponent is then non-negative.
assumptions: Runtime assertion in the executable model; not proved
map_note: RP2 support: the decoder's precondition (analogue of validBounds)

statement: getCapBoundsBits: base = (a_top + (bHi - aHi)) @ B @ 0^E, top = (a_top + (tHi - aHi)) @ T @ 0^E with R = B - 2^(MW-2) deciding the region corrections; if E < cap_max_E - 1 and top2 - base2 > 1 the MSB of top is inverted ('corrects for errors that happen when the representable space wraps the address space'); a commented-out alternative correction 'was thought to be equivalent ... but differs at least in some cases where E >= cap_max_E - 1'.
assumptions: Decoder definition with an acknowledged equivalence uncertainty at high exponents
map_note: RP2: the decoder whose base <= top and monotonicity AIVHAI must prove; A: high-exponent corner is a flagged risk

statement: assert(top >= base) inside getCapLength for every non-malformed capability: decoded top is never below decoded base.
assumptions: Executed only when getCapLength is called; equivalent to propBaseLeqTop's conclusion but asserted rather than checked for all inputs
map_note: RP2: RVY's base <= top invariant, currently an assertion -- direct port target for propBaseLeqTop (P-A2-069)

statement: assert(e >= 0) in getRepresentableAlignmentMask with comment 'setCapBounds will never make a malformed cap with E < 0': CRAM is computed by running setCapBounds(root_cap, 0, len) and reading its exponent.
assumptions: Claim about setCapBounds stated as an assertion
map_note: RP2 support: port target for propSetBoundsValid (P-A2-068) and the CRRL/CRAM properties (P-A2-075,077)

statement: assert(bitsToCap(cap.tag, capToMetadataBits(cap).bits @ cap.address) == cap) on every capability store, with the comment 'Assume that conversion to bits and back does not change the capability. TODO: State closed-form normalised-ness criterion that implies this, and prove it as an invariant of capabilities in the system.'
assumptions: The round-trip identity (encodability) is assumed of every capability reaching memory; the normalised-ness criterion is explicitly missing
map_note: RP4: the encodability invariant RVY lacks; exact port target for propEncodableCorrect/propDecodeEncodable (P-A2-064/065) and the 'canonical encoding' global invariant

statement: RVY 64-bit-address encoding parameters (cheri_prelude_128.sail): cap_mantissa_width = 14, cap_E_width = 6, cap_use_L8 = false; 32-bit-address variant (cheri_prelude_64.sail): mantissa 10, E width 5, cap_use_L8 = true, with EncMetadata fields SDP(2), AP_P(5), GL, reserved, CT, EF, L8, Tm, TE, Bm, BE; permissions are a 5-bit AP_P encoding decoded by the ap_p_encdec mapping into (R, W, C, LM, EL, SL, X, ASR) plus mode, with comments that forward match failures mean YHIW-written bits and backward failures must be prevented by legalizeFields.
assumptions: Field layout differs from both CHERIoT (P-A2-095) and CHERI Concentrate (P-A2-063): internal-exponent EF/L8 scheme, no otype field (sealed is a single CT bit), quadrant-based permission encoding
map_note: RP2/RP3: the concrete field model AIVHAI's 64-bit lemmas quantify over

statement: Malformedness predicates: boundsMalformed (with internal exponent: E = cap_max_E with B != 0, or E = cap_max_E - 1 with B's MSB set, or E < 0, or (L8 in use and E = 0)); permsMalformed (AP_P pattern with no forward decoding); capReservedValid (reserved fields zero); capIsMalformed is the disjunction; capTaggedAndNotMalformed. getCapBoundsBits, getArchPerms etc. return None for malformed caps; loads optionally legalise malformed permissions (sys_legalize_malformed_permission_on_load).
assumptions: Definitions only; no property states that tagged capabilities are never malformed
map_note: RP2/RP4: RVY's 'validBounds + encodable' analogue; the global invariant 'tagged implies not malformed' is the RVY form of the canonical-encoding hypothesis

statement: setCapBounds (described as 'An ideal version of setCapBounds as described in paper'): chooses e = cap_max_E - clz(length[addr_width .. MW-1]), uses the internal exponent iff e != 0 (or the implied length bit when L8 is unused), truncates B/T losing e + cap_xe_width bits, increments T when top bits were lost, and if the length overflows increments E and recomputes; returns (exact, newCap) with exact = no significant bits lost. Comment on the E increment: 'TODO: E can overflow here. The previous code silently wrapped so I've copied that but I'm not sure it's correct.'
assumptions: Definition only; the overflow wrap is an acknowledged uncertainty
map_note: RP2: the function AIVHAI's YBNDSRW rounding proof is about; A: E-overflow wrap is a flagged risk to resolve before proving

statement: Representability on address change: setCapAddrChecked clears the tag if the new address is not representable, or the cap is sealed (unless allowSealedUnchanged and the address is unchanged), or the cap is malformed; incCapAddrChecked likewise; clearTagIf/clearTag are the only tag-clearing primitives.
assumptions: Definitions; no property that representable implies bounds unchanged
map_note: RP2+RP5: port target for propSetOffset/propIncOffset (P-A2-072) and for 'sealed caps lose their tag on address change'

statement: Guru CHERIoT parameter invariants (the only four theorems that unfold SpecDefines): CapBSz = CapcTSz + 1; 2^ExpSz = AddrSz; 2 < CapBSz < AddrSz; Emax = 2^ExpSz - CapcTSz; with concrete values CapcTSz = 8, CapBSz = 9, ExpSz = LgAddrSz = 5, CapPermSz = 6, CapcOTypeSz = 3. 'Every other property in the entire codebase is derived purely from them.'
assumptions: Parameter-level; Qed by reflexivity/lia
map_note: none directly; the parameterisation discipline AIVHAI's 64-bit datapath proofs should copy (AddrSz = 64 would need ExpSz = 6)

statement: Theorem BoundsMonotonic: for any capability cap and address addr, let ecap = DecodeCap cap addr and bounds = Bounds isRoundDown base length (the hardware bounds-setting functional unit); if base >= ecap.base and base + length <= ecap.top then bounds.base >= ecap.base and bounds.top <= ecap.top. Proved for both round-up and round-down modes by showing the new exponent is at most the decoded cap's corrected exponent and the decoded base/top are multiples of 2^e.
assumptions: About the Guru circuit description of the Bounds and DecodeCap units (Guru expressions evaluated by evalLetExpr), i.e. the implementation's datapath, not the Sail; Print Assumptions is invoked at BoundsMonotonic.v:5167 but its output is not recorded in the tree; no Admitted anywhere in cheriot/*.v
map_note: RP2 and G-c: a mechanized, RTL-level bounds-never-widen theorem for the CHERIoT datapath -- the closest existing artifact to what AIVHAI needs for RVY's YBNDSRW at the hardware-refinement layer

statement: Theorem BoundsRoundUpProperties (Bounds false): outBase = floor(base / 2^e) * 2^e <= base; outLength = m * 2^e; outBase + outLength >= base + length (covering); outBase + (m-1) * 2^e < base + length (minimality: the length is the smallest multiple that covers); and e > 0 implies 2^(CapBSz-1) <= m (mantissa MSB set unless e = 0).
assumptions: as P-A2-114
map_note: RP2: exactness and minimal-rounding of CSetBounds in hardware; port target is the same theorem for RVY's setCapBounds

statement: Theorem BoundsRoundDownProperties (Bounds true): outBase = base exactly; outLength = m * 2^e with outLength <= length; e > 0 implies 2^(CapBSz-1) <= m.
assumptions: as P-A2-114; corresponds to CSetBoundsRoundDown (shrink-only)
map_note: RP2: shrink-only bounds derivation proved at the datapath

statement: Supporting Guru lemmas (160 Lemma/Theorem declarations in BoundsMonotonic.v): decode_base_top / base_top_shape (decoded base and top are 2^E-aligned around the address), ecap_base_multiple, ecap_top_multiple, ecap_E_nonneg, ECorrected_le_Emax, bounds_E_nonneg, bounds_E_le_Emax, bounds_E_le_ecap_ECorrected, bounds_base_math, bounds_top_math, bounds_top_eq, bounds_base_le, bounds_length_m_e, bounds_roundUp_min, bounds_roundUp_covering, bounds_roundDown_base_eq, bounds_roundDown_length_le, countLeadingZeros/countTrailingZeros loop characterisations, cE_decode_id.
assumptions: as P-A2-114
map_note: RP2: reusable arithmetic lemma library for a 64-bit port

statement: Other Guru proof artifacts in the tree are infrastructure, not capability properties: Impl/ImplStaged.v (31 theorems about the staged-pipeline combinators: Iter_Enq_Step0, Iter_Step_Inductive, Iter_First_Spec, Pipe_Enq_Stage0, Pipe_Step_Adjacent_Inductive, Pipe_First_Spec, Pipe_Deq_LastStage, ...), Impl/ImplMulDivProof.v (88 lemmas on the multiplier/divider), BankedMem.v (4), SpecRevoker.v revokerBaseAlignedLemma, Clut/Clut.v dmaCanAccessKind, SpecDevice.v (3 list lemmas).
assumptions: No theorem relates Impl/ to Spec.v in the pin
map_note: G-c: pipeline-staging lemmas are the building blocks of the (absent) refinement proof

statement: README refinement theorem: 'Theorem pipeline_refines_spec : forall (p : Program) (result : FinalState), ValidProgram p -> Pipeline_Exec p result -> Spec_Exec p result.' where ValidProgram means all traces on the atomic specification satisfy the FENCE rule and the FENCE.I rule. The identifiers pipeline_refines_spec, Pipeline_Exec, Spec_Exec and ValidProgram do not occur in any .v file in the pin (grep: 0 hits).
assumptions: Stated in prose only; the spec is 'an atomic, 1-step interleaved transition system on shared memory (specMemTree)'
source: cheriot/README.md (section 'Multi-Core Memory Consistency & Pipeline Refinement Specification', subsection 3)
map_note: G-c: the intended top-level hardware-refinement statement for the Guru CHERIoT core; not yet an artifact

statement: Multi-core program validity contract (FENCE): a trace is valid iff for any two cores where core 1 does access1(A) then Store(B), core 2 does Load(B) observing that store then access2(A), and the A accesses conflict, there is an appropriate FENCE (R,W or W,W) or a True Dependency between access1(A) and Store(B), and a FENCE (R,W or R,R) or a True Dependency between Load(B) and access2(A); True Dependency is defined semantically (varying the loaded value changes the later address or store data; y = x*0 is not a dependency). FENCE.I contract: any Store(A) followed by Fetch(A) must have a FENCE.I between them.
assumptions: Side condition of the refinement theorem; programs violating it get no guarantee
map_note: G-c: memory-model hypothesis under which hardware refinement is claimed; A: software (CF) must obey it

statement: ISA deviation 1 (deferred jump faults, MePrevPcc SCR 27): CJALR/CJAL/branches never fault synchronously; an invalid target or sentry clears PCC.tag and the exception is raised at the next instruction fetch; MePrevPcc records the PCC of every committed, non-trapping instruction and is read-only (a CSpecialRW write is decoded as illegal), so on a deferred fault MePcc holds the fetch PCC and MePrevPcc the jump's PCC.
assumptions: Deviation from cheriot-sail; attribution correctness is stated, not proved
map_note: RP5: an invalid sentry jump yields an untagged PCC rather than a trap -- changes the trap-free/sentry-free boundary RP1 is stated against; A: G-CF2 must model deferred faults if it follows this core

statement: ISA deviation 2 (5-bit cE encoding): cE is 5 bits, cT 8 bits, B 9 bits, p 6 bits; the property M_msb = (cE != 0) is leveraged so that cE = 0x1F (all ones) encodes E = 0 with M_msb = 1, 'allowing exact 32-bit representation of decompressed bounds'; get_E_from_cE maps all-ones to 0 and get_cE_from_E_T_B maps (E = 0, Mmsb = 1) to -1.
assumptions: Differs from CHERIoT's 4-bit E with 0xf = 24 (P-A2-095); cE_decode_id (BoundsMonotonic.v:504) is the proved decode/encode identity for this field
map_note: RP2 context: a non-standard exponent encoding whose monotonicity proof (P-A2-114) does not transfer verbatim to CHERIoT-Ibex or to RVY

statement: ISA deviations 3-9: ScrSanitizer checks only LSB = 0 for MePcc/Mtcc and clears the tag instead of faulting; all exceptions set MTVAL in the CHERI {S, RegIdx, Cause} format; MMIO register decode ignores the low 2 bits; revoker interrupt is W1C; timer compare is exposed as CSRs mtimecmp/mtimecmph (Sstc addresses 0x14D/0x15D, ASR-gated) with a sticky core-side mtip latch cleared only by writing them; mip is virtual (MEIP combinational from PLIC); writes to read-only registers (MePrevPcc, mip) raise IllegalInst; WFI is decoded as ECALL so the idle thread yields to the scheduler.
assumptions: Documented divergences from cheriot-sail; 'CHERIoT has no privilege hierarchy: isolation derives from capabilities and the ASR permission'
map_note: G-CF: ASR-gated system state; none for RP1-RP5

statement: Observational correctness: the execution pipeline produces an infinite stream of memory interactions (address, byte enables, write-enable, write data, or 'no event') identical to that of the iterated Sail specification when both start in the same initial state, up to microarchitecturally defined timings (Realise/Check) and against the tightened specification CSpec = clear o Spec
assumptions: default config CHERIoTEn, RV32E, RV32BNone, pure-capability mode, temporal safety; memory grants/responses within 10 cycles; WFI wake within bounded cycles; interrupts stay active until cleared by a memory op; no debug-mode entry; no bus errors; M-type instructions excluded; unknown-CSR accesses unchecked; MSHWM/MSHWMB, debug CSRs, perf counters unchecked; spec is a modified Sail fork; Realise and Check are hand-written SV regarded as part of the statement; base case abs(en(s)0)=a0 unproven; all SVA proofs unbounded (k-induction)
source: Ploix-25 Sec. I.A lines 44-46; Sec. III item 2 line 134; Sec. VIII.C lines 425-461; Sec. X lines 521-533
map_note: G-c; this is the archetype of 'implementation refines the Sail ISA model' that AIVHAI must reproduce for CVA6-CHERI against RVY

statement: Liveness: spec_en (instruction EX->WB transition or interrupt handled) is always eventually fired; a weak but finite upper bound on cycles between successive spec_en states is proved by bounding edges of the microarchitectural state path and summing
assumptions: memory response bound of 10 cycles; processor sleep after WFI is always awoken in bounded time; bounds are 'low enough to be tractable, high enough to cover any stall'
source: Ploix-25 Sec. III item 6 line 142; Sec. VII lines 277-281; Sec. VIII.B lines 337-339
map_note: G-c; liveness is a required companion to any refinement claim for CVA6-CHERI

statement: Instruction fetch correctness: if an instruction enters the fetch FIFO with a given address then, if it later leaves the FIFO, it leaves with the same address (fetch verified separately because Sail does not model an instruction cache/FIFO)
assumptions: structural decomposition: fetch and execution pipeline verified independently; the 'input ports' of the execution pipeline include the instruction bits delivered by fetch to the RVC decoder
source: Ploix-25 Sec. III item 1 line 132; Sec. VIII.B lines 379; Sec. X line 535
map_note: G-c; CVA6's frontend (branch predictor, I-cache) will need the same out-of-model treatment

statement: State matching: for all n >= 0, abs(en(s)_n) = a_n, i.e. the abstraction of the microarchitectural state at every spec_en sample equals the n-th iterate of the (tightened) Sail specification; proved by induction on n using the continuity properties as the inductive step
assumptions: the induction is an informal pen-and-paper argument over mechanically proved SVA lemmas (the authors state the notation 'is not defined mathematically or formally'); base case abs(en(s)0)=a0 is an unproven assumption; relies on liveness of spec_en
map_note: G-c; the glue argument between per-instruction lemmas and the top-level claim

statement: Continuity properties: each time the Sail specification is queried (spec_en), the new inputs abstracted from the RTL state equal the outputs stored from the previous query (or are at least as strict, for capability tags); hence the state one instruction finishes in is the state the next begins with, closing pipeline-control and forwarding gaps left by end-to-end checks
assumptions: uses end-to-end instruction correctness properties as lemmas; helper invariants; the pipeline follower is stepped by the RTL's own stall/flush control signals rather than independent logic
source: Ploix-25 Sec. III items 3-4 lines 136-138; Sec. VI.A line 259; Sec. VIII.A lines 319-329
map_note: G-c; required to turn per-instruction checks into a refinement for a pipelined CVA6

statement: End-to-end instruction correctness: a case split over instruction types (illegal instruction being one type) establishing that each instruction entering the pipeline mutates the ISA architectural state (register file at WB, CSRs at end of EX, PC) exactly as one iteration of the Sail main loop specifies, from immediately after fetch to the last effect; covers all instructions, interrupts, fetch errors and exceptions
assumptions: spec evaluated on the abstract pre-state at the EX->WB boundary and carried in a pipeline follower; excludes M-type instructions, debug mode, bus errors, unknown CSRs, MSHWM/MSHWMB, debug CSRs, perf counters; requires DTI and other helper invariants; multiple instructions in flight allowed (no Burch-Dill single-instruction flushing)
source: Ploix-25 Sec. III item 7 line 144; Sec. VI lines 228-259; Sec. X lines 531-533
map_note: G-c; the per-instruction obligation set for CVA6-CHERI vs RVY

statement: M-type (multiply/divide) data-path instructions conform to Sail: NOT proved; the authors did not attempt conclusive proofs and expect symbolic trajectory evaluation to be needed
assumptions: explicitly excluded from coverage
map_note: none; a coverage gap to avoid repeating, not a property

statement: State abstraction API: the observed initial state of an instruction accounts for register forwarding vs register-file reads; post-update state is taken at the time each piece of architectural state changes; capabilities are mapped from the RTL representation into the Sail capability type
assumptions: abs is derived from internal RTL signals; limited internal RVFI signals used but the RVFI interface as a whole is not (it gives too limited a view of CSR mutation)
map_note: G-c; an abstraction function for CVA6-CHERI's 128-bit capability register file is the analogue

statement: Global data-type invariant (DTI): every compressed capability stored in any stateful block (EX, CSR blocks incl. MTCC) always carries cached correction fields top_cor (2 bits) and base_cor (1 bit) equal to the values the Sail bounds-decompression algorithm computes from (a, B, T, E)
assumptions: proved by assume-guarantee decomposition with k-induction at k=1-2; longest block (MTCC CSR) about two minutes; later extended with the memory well-formedness constraint
source: Ploix-25 Sec. II.A lines 100-114; Sec. V lines 198-226
map_note: G-c; CVA6-CHERI's capability register representation will need an equivalent representation invariant

statement: DTI decomposition lemmas: (1) capabilities at reset satisfy the DTI; (2) for stateful blocks, DTI on state and inputs implies DTI on outputs; (3) DTI on state and inputs implies DTI on next-cycle state; (4) for stateless blocks DTI on inputs implies DTI on outputs; (5) by k-induction from 1-4, all stored capabilities always satisfy the DTI
assumptions: per-block case split; CSR block split per CSR; steps 1-4 independent, 5 by k-induction
map_note: G-c; reusable proof structure for a block-decomposed CVA6 invariant

statement: DTI strengthening with the memory constraint: every tagged capability inside the processor satisfies the well-formedness constraint imposed on loadable capabilities (e.g. no tagged capability with top > 2^32); hence every tagged capability written to memory satisfies it, validating the load-side assumption
assumptions: closes the loop only for capabilities the core itself writes; does not cover DMA or other cores
source: Ploix-25 Sec. V line 226; Sec. VII.B lines 307-313
map_note: G-c5; tag-and-representation integrity of capabilities round-tripping through memory

statement: Assumption on capabilities from memory: every capability loaded from memory with its tag bit set is well-formed (representable; top <= 2^32); the constraint is applied only to tag-set capabilities, and some CHERIoT-Ibex microarchitectural optimisations are unsound without it
assumptions: assumed, not proved; explicitly 'a faulty DMA device or additional less well behaved cores may invalidate our assumption, but that is beyond the scope'
map_note: G-c5; precisely the assumption the Coral NPU DMA path can violate, so AIVHAI must discharge it rather than assume it

statement: Memory-bus protocol assumptions: a response cannot arrive in the same cycle as its grant; grants occur only when a request is being sent; a response cannot arrive unless a request is outstanding
assumptions: SystemVerilog assumptions on the Ibex instruction and data memory ports per the Ibex verification docs
map_note: none; environment constraint, though CVA6's AXI/cache interfaces will need their own

statement: Bounded memory latency: grants and responses are returned within 10 cycles (the protocol itself allows unbounded delay)
assumptions: assumption introduced for tractability of liveness and of helper properties by unrolling
source: Ploix-25 Sec. VII lines 277-281; Sec. X line 523
