statement: 'When an object is allocated with an explicit capability, it may be freed only by presenting the same capability. This means that if you pass a heap-allocated buffer to another compartment, that compartment cannot free it unless you also pass the authorising capability.' 'the deallocation API will always make progress. The allocator uses a priority-inheriting lock, which is dropped while blocking.'
assumptions: none stated
map_note: G-CF — allocator ownership and free-path liveness

statement: Scheduler fault tolerance: 'the scheduler ensures that its data structures are in a consistent state before performing any operations on user-provided data that may trap. As such, it can unwind to the caller and, at worst, leak memory owned by the caller.'
assumptions: none stated
source: Chisnall-26, 9.8 Ensuring that heap objects are not deallocated, approx line 4511
map_note: G-CF — scheduler integrity under malicious-caller faults

statement: Claims: 'While you have a claim on an object, that object counts towards your quota ... your claim will cover the entire object because you cannot free part of an object.' heap_claim_ephemeral: 'If this function returns zero then the heap pointers are guaranteed not to become invalid until either the next cross-compartment call or the next call to this function.' Hazard slots 'are cleared on every cross-compartment call'; 'If a pointer passed to heap_free is present in the allocator, the allocator will defer freeing the object.' 'In the case of failure, neither pointer will have been claimed.'
artifact: none (API contract; hazard-pointer epoch protocol described at 8.7 line ~3831 and 12.5 line ~5467)
assumptions: 'Any claim applied with heap_claim_ephemeral is lost on any cross-compartment call. This includes any blocking operation'
map_note: G-CF — allocator/switcher cooperative lifetime guarantee across mutual distrust

statement: MMIO read side effects (caveat stated as a rule): 'A read-only capability to a device's MMIO region may convey more rights than you expect ... don't assume that read-only means may-not-affect-device-state when providing capabilities to device memory.'
assumptions: device-specific
source: Chisnall-26, 11.1 What is a device?, approx line 4877
map_note: none — explicit scoping of what load permission means for devices; relevant to the NPU MMIO/DMA shim where read-only delegation may still have effects

statement: No ISRs: 'CHERIoT RTOS does not allow this because ISRs run with access to the state of the interrupted thread ... on RISC-V all registers of the interrupted thread are visible. This means that an ISR runs with access to the thread and compartment that are interrupted. Not only would this potentially break compartment isolation, it would be difficult to use safely'. Interrupts are instead 'mapped onto events that threads can wait on'; 'this kind of mechanism would violate the CHERIoT security model and is not provided'.
assumptions: interrupt latency ~1,000 cycles on Ibex accepted as cost
source: Chisnall-26, 11.6 Waiting for an interrupt approx lines 5015-5023; 15.4 approx line 6678
map_note: G-c and G-CF — only the switcher ever sees an interrupted context; a design invariant AIVHAI's CF must preserve on 64-bit cores

statement: Interrupt capabilities and futexes: handling an interrupt requires 'a software capability ... that authorises access to the interrupt' (waiting and/or acknowledging, each a separate boolean, auditable in the report). The interrupt futex 'is now a read-only capability (attempting to store through it will trap)'. 'external interrupts are not delivered on a particular channel unless the preceding one has been acknowledged.' The PLIC records interrupts while deferred and 'ensures that they are not lost'.
assumptions: edge-triggered interrupts are auto-completed by the scheduler (14.3)
source: Chisnall-26, 11.5 approx lines 4963-5011; 11.6 approx line 5033; 11.7 approx line 5053
map_note: G-CF — interrupt authority is a sealed software capability; scheduler mediates all interrupt handling

statement: Device exclusivity: 'the scheduler is the only component that has direct access to the interrupt controller, whereas the memory allocator is the only component that has full access to the revoker.' The RTOS Rego policy enforces: 'Only the allocator may access the revoker', 'Only the scheduler may access the interrupt controllers' (clint, plic).
artifact: cheriot-audit Rego policy (rtos.valid) — a link-time policy check, not SMT; closest category
assumptions: policy is run; MMIO regions correctly named in the board file
map_note: G-CF — device-authority confinement is link-time checkable; AIVHAI's NPU/DMA shim authority would be auditable the same way
correction: Codex review of PR #246, Cycle 1: the source describes a cheriot-audit Rego link-time policy check of the firmware image, not an SMT check (Chisnall-26 §11.8, §12.5).

statement: Fail-closed authority: 'Any access outside of this region requires an explicit capability to be provided to the compartment's import table by the loader. The loader, in turn, will provide such a capability if, and only if, the linker has created metadata instructing it to. This means that the system fails closed.' 'even if the compartment gains knowledge of some address, it does not gain rights to access any memory ... hiding things from the audit report does not result in increased rights (failing closed).'
assumptions: linker/loader correctness; audit report completeness
source: Chisnall-26, 12 Auditing firmware images, approx lines 5113-5123
map_note: G-c — the no-ambient-authority principle in auditing form; a direct consequence of RP1/RP4 (addresses are not rights)

statement: Hazard list and epoch protocol: 'The allocator is the only thing that should have access to [the hazard-pointer list] (the switcher also exposes a write-only view of a part of it for the current thread). Concurrent access to this is mediated via a 32-bit epoch variable that is incremented when the allocator starts and finishes reading the list. This means that it is safe to write to if the value is even, and that value is safely stored if the epoch is unchanged before and after writing. This is safe for anything to read, but only the allocator should write to it.' Sizes: two hazard pointers per thread, 4-byte epoch.

statement: Stack-derived buffers are automatically local: 'the on-stack buffer (the single byte local variable) is derived from our stack pointer and so is automatically local. This ensures that the TCP/IP compartment cannot capture it.' TLS does the same deliberately: 'Removing the global permission protects the TLS stack from time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) attacks by guaranteeing that the TCP/IP compartment cannot capture the buffer for longer than the duration of the call. Similarly, removing permissions and bounding the pointers to the buffers ensures that no data can leak to the TCP/IP compartment and it cannot overwrite anything.'
assumptions: callee cannot store non-global caps anywhere but its (truncated) stack, which is zeroed on return
map_note: G-c — no-capture of delegated buffers is derived from RP3 (global stripping) + stack confinement

statement: TLS flow isolation: 'the TLS compartment has no global state. All state associated with a TLS connection is stored in the connection object, exposed as a sealed capability. This means that two concurrent calls into the TLS compartment for different TLS connections have no shared state, giving flow isolation. An attacker who compromises one TLS connection cannot use this to attack another.' And 'it is impossible for the caller to accidentally send data over the socket unencrypted' because TLS owns the socket.
assumptions: TLS compartment 'implicitly trusts the caller for availability'; crashing it 'you can only attack yourself'

statement: Issue stage holds an issue queue, a scoreboard and a small ROB; an instruction issues once all operands are ready; dependencies are tracked in the scoreboard and operands forwarded from the ROB
assumptions: 8 ROB entries in the silicon instance
source: ZarubaBenini-19, section II item 4 and II-F, lines 96, 163-167, 199
map_note: G-c; in-order issue is the key hypothesis for relating pipeline state to ISA state

statement: 'Instructions can retire out-of-order from the functional units. Write-back conflicts are resolved through the ROB'; the commit stage 'commits all instructions in program order' and can commit two per cycle
assumptions: fixed-latency ALU/mul/CSR units; variable-latency FPU and LSU
map_note: G-c; out-of-order writeback with in-order commit is the pipeline invariant a refinement must carry

statement: 'Stores and atomic memory operations are held in a store buffer until the commit stage confirms their architectural commit'
assumptions: variable-size store buffer in the store unit
map_note: G-c; no speculative memory write becomes visible before commit

statement: Precise exceptions: an exception is linked to its instruction, auxiliary information saved, and 'When the excepting instruction finally retires the commit stage redirects the instruction frontend to the exception handler'
assumptions: exceptions from PTW on fetch, decode (illegal instruction), and LSU (translation or access faults)
map_note: G-c; precise exceptions are what let a trap in the Sail model correspond to one in RTL

statement: Interrupts are synchronised to a retiring instruction; 'Atomic memory operations must not be interrupted', so no interrupt is taken when retiring an atomic instruction, and likewise for atomic CSR instructions
assumptions: none stated
map_note: G-c; atomicity of AMO and CSR instructions relative to interrupts

statement: Access to supervisor-view and machine CSRs 'is restricted to the same or a higher privilege level'
assumptions: base supervisor ISA
map_note: G-c; privilege check the model and RTL must agree on

statement: 'CSR accesses are executed in the commit stage and are never done speculatively'; because a CSR write can affect already-speculated instructions (e.g. address translation), the pipeline is completely flushed on such accesses
assumptions: none stated
source: ZarubaBenini-19, section II-D and II-G item 5, lines 149, 187
map_note: G-c; non-speculative CSR effects simplify the refinement relation for privileged state

statement: Privileged instructions (WFI, environment call, return) 'are only executed non-speculatively in the commit stage' because they alter CSR state and privilege level
assumptions: none stated
map_note: G-c; privilege-level changes occur only at commit

statement: MMU with separate, configurable, fully set-associative flip-flop instruction and data TLBs (16 entries each in silicon), checked on every access; on a miss a hardware PTW walks main memory; pseudo-LRU replacement; a TLB miss stalls the cache pipeline until translation is valid
assumptions: SV39; no PMP is mentioned anywhere in the paper
map_note: G-c; address-translation structures the RVY Sv39 model must be refined by

statement: Flip-flop TLBs 'can be efficiently flushed in a single cycle'; for the separate instruction, data and translation memory streams, caches 'are either coherent or need to be entirely flushed' under fences
assumptions: RISC-V fence semantics
map_note: G-c; fence and flush semantics

statement: WAW hazards in the scoreboard are resolved by a light-weight renaming that adds one bit to the logical register address space and toggles the MSB per issued destination
assumptions: none stated
map_note: G-c; register-mapping detail of the scoreboard

statement: Both L1 caches are virtually indexed, physically tagged, with an extra output pipeline stage; the data cache is a parameterisable write-back cache with hit-under-miss across three master ports (PTW, load unit, store unit); single AXI5 master port arbitrated among fetch, refill/writeback and uncached accesses
assumptions: 16 kB 4-way I-cache, 32 kB 8-way D-cache, 3-cycle D-cache latency in silicon
map_note: G-c; memory-subsystem structure

statement: The FPU is 'IEEE compliant' with custom trans-precision extensions
assumptions: no compliance test is cited
map_note: none; FP is out of AIVHAI's capability scope

statement: Ariane 'contains a RISC-V compliant debug interface' using an execution-based approach (debug RAM, one extra instruction dret)
assumptions: RISC-V External Debug 0.13.1
map_note: none; debug is outside the proof boundary

statement: 'We support extensive tracing in RTL simulation. All register and memory access are traced together with their (physical and virtual) addresses and current values'; no PC tracing in hardware
assumptions: the trace is a capability of the simulator; the paper does not report comparing it against any oracle
map_note: G-c; the RTL trace is the implementation-side input a model-vs-RTL comparison would consume

statement: 'We provide support for Verilator- and QuestaSim-based RTL simulation as well as a ready-to-go FPGA bitstream'
assumptions: infrastructure availability, not a validation result
map_note: G-c; the simulation and FPGA substrates AIVHAI testing would run on

statement: Silicon was measured on an ADVANTEST 93000 ASIC tester using assembly-level tests exercising ALU, multiplier, divider, loads/stores with and without virtual memory (TLBs regularly flushed to exercise the PTW), and an IGEMM mixed workload; tests were run on silicon and the post-layout netlist, and 'Post-layout and silicon measurements lie within a 10 % error margin'
assumptions: tests are for power/energy characterisation, not functional verification; calibration factor applied to post-layout estimates
map_note: none; energy characterisation, not correctness

statement: Performance: up to 1.65 DMIPS/MHz; on Dhrystone a 5.77% mispredict rate with 128-entry BHT and 64-entry BTB, IPC 0.82; silicon runs 220 MHz to 1.7 GHz across 0.5-1.15 V; signed off at 902 MHz worst case
assumptions: GlobalFoundries 22FDX, 3x3 mm die
map_note: none; performance figures

statement: Design goal and claim: critical path under 30 NAND gate equivalents, with the most critical paths around the 8-way data cache
assumptions: synthesis-driven design
map_note: none; timing

statement: Branch prediction uses a 2-bit saturating-counter BHT, a BTB and a RAS with RISC-V static prediction (backward taken, forward not taken) as fallback; mispredict flush costs at least five cycles
assumptions: 8-entry BHT/BTB in silicon
map_note: G-c; speculative fetch that a refinement must show is architecturally invisible

statement: Single-bit tag (SBT) per word held in a table in DRAM with one bit per word, managed by a tag controller with a tag cache next to the DRAM controller; one bit is 'the minimum metadata needed to distinguish between an untyped data word and any number of new hardware-enforced types'
assumptions: 64-bit words in the gem5 study, 256-bit capability words in the CHERI FPGA study
source: JoannouWoodruffKovacsicsEtAl-17, Abstract, sections III and V, lines 28, 42, 80-88, 127
map_note: G-c5; the in-DRAM tag-table design is the tag-storage substrate whose integrity G-c5 concerns

statement: Tags in a shadowspace 'cannot be named by instructions from the host architecture and is therefore naturally protected from tampering without impeding program execution'
assumptions: shadowspace hidden from the host ISA
map_note: G-c5; non-addressability of tag storage is the core integrity argument

statement: With embedded metadata protected by an SBT, 'Hardware will then naturally propagate the M-bit tag with the word, and can prevent these tag bits from being overwritten by legacy operations if the SBT is set'
assumptions: embedded-tag architectures (CHERI, M-Machine, Low-fat pointers)
map_note: G-c5; tag preservation through data movement and clearing on legacy writes

statement: In a split tag/data cache hierarchy 'Consistency between tag and data becomes a problem when the two exist in separate cache lines', with no obvious efficient solution and page-granularity false sharing
assumptions: survey of FlexiTaint, MemTracker and related
map_note: G-c5; identifies the tag/data consistency hazard that a merged hierarchy avoids

statement: Merged-cache hierarchy: 'As tagged memory logically extends each memory word', caches should be widened throughout the hierarchy, 'storing tags alongside the metadata already held for coherence'; recommended for all SBT systems
assumptions: caches are not commodity parts and can be widened
map_note: G-c5; tag travels in the same line as its data through every cache level

statement: Tagging physical rather than virtual memory limits tag metadata to a fixed proportion of memory, yields a static table, merges with the physically-indexed cache hierarchy, and 'enable[s] memory clients that do not support translation to correctly handle tagged memory'
assumptions: the paper does not state how such clients (e.g. DMA masters) treat tags; it does not say non-tag-aware masters clear tags
map_note: G-c5; the only statement in the paper bearing on non-CPU memory masters

statement: 'CHERI introduces a dedicated tag cache next to the DRAM controller to more efficiently emulate a wider physical memory'; adopted by lowRISC and HDFI
assumptions: HDFI's 1 KiB tag cache showed 37.9-373% overhead, attributed to its tiny design
map_note: G-c5; tag-cache placement at the memory controller

statement: 'For a given word width, this caching behavior is identical for any SBT scheme as all schemes simply emulate a memory that is wider by one bit'
assumptions: DRAM trace of unmodified applications implies the tag-table trace
map_note: none; modelling assumption of the evaluation

statement: Evaluation methodology: gem5 instrumented to trace all DRAM accesses on two ARMv8 systems (small: one core, 256 KiB L2; big: four cores, 8 MiB L3 with prefetching), replayed against simulated 8-way physically-indexed tag caches; workloads Earley-Boyer under V8 (three instances on big) and FFMPEG
assumptions: 64-bit tag granule, amplification factor 64
map_note: none; performance methodology

statement: A 128 KiB tag cache covering the same data as the 8 MiB L3 it serves hits over 90%, inflating DRAM accesses by under 10%; at a 5% overhead threshold the small system needs a 32 KiB and the big system a 256 KiB tag cache (Earley-Boyer/FFMPEG: 4.91%/1.31% small, 3.72%/0.50% big)
assumptions: 64-byte tag lines, 8-way
map_note: none; overhead result

statement: The high hit rate is due to spatial locality at page granularity: a 64-byte tag line of 512 tags covers a 4 KiB page, and spatial hits grow until lines of about 4096 tags; this reduces the expected 50% DRAM traffic overhead to under 5%
assumptions: Earley-Boyer big, 256 KiB 8-way tag cache
map_note: none; explanatory result

statement: Silent-write elimination in the simulated tag cache (dropping writes of unchanged tags) reduces dirty lines from 80% to 4% for FFMPEG and 60% to about 30% for Earley-Boyer, making writeback traffic depend on tag values; not evaluated in hardware
assumptions: FPGA tag controller uses a standard cache without this feature
map_note: none; optimisation

statement: Hardware implementation: the tag controller of the open-source CHERI processor (bericpu.org) was rebuilt with performance counters; CHERI has 32 KiB L1s and a 256 KiB L2, 4-way, 128-byte lines, one tag per 256-bit word (amplification 256); the controller has a 32 KiB 4-way tag cache with 128-byte lines matching the burst size, each line providing tags for 32 KiB of data
assumptions: standard cache instantiation; no silent-write elimination or empty-line fabrication in hardware
map_note: G-c5; the concrete CHERI tag-controller design

statement: FPGA, uncompressed table: 'DRAM overhead was below 3% for programs with data sets contained in the multi-megabyte reach of the tag cache'; Splay with a working set over 100 MB stayed under 8%; benchmarks compiled with 256-bit capabilities for all pointers
assumptions: Octane under Duktape and MiBench natively
source: JoannouWoodruffKovacsicsEtAl-17, section V-B and VII, lines 158-160, 231
map_note: none; overhead result on CHERI hardware

statement: Hierarchical tag table invariant: a bit in the root level indicates whether any bit in its leaf group is set; a clear root bit means the leaf group is all zero and 'need not be accessed on a read or on a write of zero'; 'Each time we clear a tag bit in the leaf level, we must check whether the rest of the tags in the group are zero, clearing the bit in the root level if this is the case'; on boot clearing only the root level clears all tags
assumptions: fully hardware-managed; emulates a flat tag space; parameterised for arbitrary levels and grouping factors
map_note: G-c5; a stated structural invariant of hierarchical tag storage that must hold for tags to be correctly reported

statement: Empty-line fabrication: the simulated controller fabricates a tag-cache line when a leaf group first becomes non-zero and destroys it without writeback when it returns to all-zero; reduces fills by 0.5-75% depending on pointer density; requires groups to align with cache lines; not implemented on FPGA
assumptions: line-group principle
map_note: none; optimisation

statement: Static core-dump analysis (x86-64 FreeBSD, pointers identified by matching words against allocated addresses) finds that for many C applications fewer than 10% of tag groups contain pointers even at large grouping factors, while JavaScript/C++ applications reach about 25% pointer density with over 75% of large groups containing pointers; pointers cluster more than a 1% random distribution
assumptions: upper bound on pointer count; rare false positives
map_note: none; workload characterisation

statement: Dynamic hierarchical study (GF 512): FFMPEG pointer-tag misses collapse to near zero; code-pointer-only tagging eliminates further leaf groups with overhead collapsing in all but Earley-Boyer big; tagging zeroed lines costs under 0.2% traffic while zeroed lines are 1.5-2.5% of DRAM traffic
assumptions: pointers in DRAM traffic identified from TLB-miss-derived address lists, slightly overestimating density
map_note: none; compression result

statement: Line-group principle: 'The optimal grouping factor (GF) will almost always be equal to the cache line size', since no group smaller than a line can be usefully omitted from the cache
assumptions: Earley-Boyer big sweep of GF 8-2048
map_note: none; design rule

statement: The FPGA implementation uses a grouping factor equal to the cache word size (256 bits) rather than the line size (1024 bits) so that 'we [can] check if a leaf group is zero in a single cycle when a tag is cleared' and clear the parent bit
assumptions: two-level table
map_note: G-c5; how the hierarchical invariant (P-B-B098) is maintained in hardware

statement: FPGA with a two-level hierarchical table (GF 256) and all pointers tagged: for MiBench the tag working set fits the table cache and 'overheads entirely collapse' (amplified reach over 160 MiB); for JavaScript benchmarks 'the miss rate is at least halved'
assumptions: 32 KiB tag cache; Splay and Earley-Boyer chosen as hard cases
map_note: none; overhead result on CHERI hardware

statement: The hierarchical tag controller on FPGA 'consumed 15.4% more logic elements than the flat instantiation, averaged across 10 builds', with identical memory resources
assumptions: FPGA logic cost not representative of ASIC
map_note: none; area cost

statement: 'Benchmarks run on our FPGA implementation confirm the simulation results, and demonstrate that an SBT memory can be implemented using commodity memory at near-zero performance cost'; overall under 8% DRAM traffic overhead measured on FPGA, under 1% common case with compression
assumptions: performance, not functional, confirmation
map_note: none; cross-validation of simulation by FPGA measurement

statement: Tagged memory is claimed to enable 'non-bypassable security properties' and to provide integrity for metadata because the shadowspace is unaddressable
assumptions: no proof or test of non-bypassability is offered
map_note: G-c5; the informal integrity claim AIVHAI must turn into an argued property

statement: A basic VME matmul operation takes two vector registers, computes the outer product of these operands, and accumulates the results into a large matrix accumulator (N^2 multiply-accumulates from the two N-element vector operand registers).
assumptions: VME TG charter v9 (2025-08-03); scope statement, not a normative ISA text
map_note: A-1; the ISA model's VME arithmetic must realise the outer-product-accumulate shape the charter fixes

statement: VME depends on and remains closely coupled to a hart and its RVV implementation (reading vector registers for source operands and leveraging RVV for surrounding computation), but has a new accumulator regfile into which matmul results are accumulated; it requires no special new 2D matrix load/store instructions or major new CSRs.
assumptions: Charter v9; later superseded in detail by Zvt v0.4, which does add tile load/store (vtle/vtse) and one CSR (mtype)
map_note: G-c; the architecture decision that matrix state is per-hart and coupled to RVV, which the CVA6-CHERI refinement must respect

statement: VME will be matrix-dimension agnostic, similar to RVV being vector-length agnostic, using similar 'vsetvl and vl' mechanisms, so that implementations may choose max matmul dimensions, MAC datapath size, and accumulator regfile size freely.
assumptions: Charter v9
map_note: A-1; the model must be parameterised in the implementation dimension (TE) rather than fixing it

statement: Data movement into and out of accumulator registers is provided in both accumulator row-major and column-major manners, giving 'free' matrix transpose.
assumptions: Charter v9
map_note: A-1; row and column access paths to the same state are both architectural

statement: Exclusion: the larger 'HPC' FP data types will not be supported by VME (an add-on extension is possible); DSP-oriented add-on extensions are likewise out of scope for the TG.
assumptions: Charter v9; justified by HPC gravitating to IME with 4Kb+ VLEN
map_note: none; a scope boundary, not a verifiable property

statement: Zvt adds new architectural state to each hart in the form of square matrix tiles; computational instructions source operands from vector registers and accumulate into the tiles. Input width is SEW; accumulator width is TEW = SEW*TWIDEN with TWIDEN in {1,2,4} depending on the instruction.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft (riscv-isa-manual PR #2997 head 31a7666, 2026-09-21); not ratified
map_note: A-1; defines the state and width relation an ISA model must carry

statement: The computational instructions perform C[M,N] += A[K,M]^T * B[K,N] with C in tile state; each row of A and B is held in a separate vector register group; the inner dimension K has a maximum KMAX of 1, 2, or 4 depending on the data type of A and B.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; the arithmetic shape the model must implement

statement: Zvtbase provides the tile state and the configuration, move, load, store and context-manipulation instructions; in the base, the move, load and store instructions support a tile EEW (TEW) of 32 only, and other TEWs are reserved for these instructions. Moves, loads and stores for other TEWs are provided by Zvt8e, Zvt16e, Zvt64e.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; note internal tension with ll.556-558 which say vtle/vtse support all SEW settings 8..ELEN (that sentence presupposes the e-extensions)
map_note: A-1; a model must reserve non-32 TEW transfers unless the matching e-extension is enabled

statement: Extension dependencies: Zvtbase requires Zve32x; Zvt8e and Zvt16e require Zvtbase; Zvt64e requires Zvtbase and Zve64x. Hence VME requires at least the Zve32x subset of the vector extension.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: G-c; the CVA6-CHERI configuration must include Zve32x (and Zve64x for TEW=64) before Zvt is meaningful

statement: The Zvt extensions are compatible with the RV32E, RV32I, RV64E and RV64I base ISAs.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: none; portability statement

statement: Computational extensions and their dependencies: Zvti8i32mm (Zvtbase_Zvt8e; [U]Int8 -> Int32), Zvtofp8fmm (Zvtbase_Zvt8e_Zve32f; OCP FP8 -> FP32), Zvtfp16fmm (Zvtbase_Zvt16e_Zve32f; FP16 -> FP32), Zvtbf16fmm (Zvtbase_Zvt16e_Zve32f; BF16 -> FP32), Zvtfmm (Zvtbase_Zve32f; FP32 -> FP32), Zvtdmm (Zvtbase_Zvt64e_Zve64d; FP64 -> FP64).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft. DIFFERENCE: 26a names the FP8 multiplicand type 'OCP MX FP8'; 26b names it 'OCP FP8' (and the FP8 NOTE at 26b l.716 drops 'MX' relative to 26a l.570)
map_note: A-1; extension gating of each arithmetic instruction

statement: Each computational extension requires that the moves, loads and stores of both the multiplicand width and the accumulator width be supported.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; implied extension closure the model's configuration must enforce

statement: The matrix state is organised into matrix tiles, each a separately addressable two-dimensional square matrix; the fixed matrix state is viewed as a different number of tiles depending on TEW.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; one physical state with TEW-dependent views

statement: When TEW=32 the tiles are TExTE elements; TE is an implementation parameter constrained to be a power of 2 with VLEN/4 >= TE >= 4. The upper bound follows from the requirement that a tile row or column must fit within a single vector register group (VLEN*8 bits). Implementations may choose less than the maximum TE.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: G-c; a configuration invariant (VLEN/TE relation) the CVA6-CHERI parameterisation must satisfy

statement: The ISA fixes the number of TEW=32 tiles at four: mt0, mt4, mt8, mt12.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; fixed state size 16*TE*TE bytes

statement: Tile views by TEW: TEW=8 gives 16 tiles TExTE (mt0..mt15); TEW=16 gives 8 tiles TExTE (even specifiers mt0,mt2,...,mt14); TEW=32 gives 4 tiles TExTE (mt0,mt4,mt8,mt12); TEW=64 gives 8 tiles of (TE/2)x(TE/2) (even specifiers).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; table the model must reproduce

statement: For TEW<32 the tile dimensions stay TExTE; every halving of TEW halves the state per tile and doubles the number of tiles: the storage of each TEW=32 tile is divided to form two TEW=16 tiles (mt0 -> mt0 and mt2), and each TEW=16 tile into two TEW=8 tiles (mt0 -> mt0 and mt1).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; aliasing invariant across TEW views

statement: For TEW=64 the tile dimensions are reduced by a factor of 2 in each dimension (TE/2 x TE/2) while the number of tiles increases to 8; the storage of each TEW=32 tile is divided to form two TEW=64 tiles (mt0 -> mt0 and mt2).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; aliasing invariant for the 64-bit view

statement: ETE (effective tile edge) is defined as ETE = TEW < 64 ? TE : TE/2.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; definitional function used by every body/tail bound

statement: The Zvt<N>t extension name asserts TE >= N (e.g. Zvt32t indicates TE is at least 32); TE may be discovered dynamically with msettn.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; discoverability of the implementation parameter

statement: Tile punning: the tile state is reshaped for each supported TEW so that tiles combine to support wider accumulators (e.g. four TEW=8 tiles mt0..3 form one TEW=32 tile mt0); the punning scheme is architecturally fixed so that context switch, debug, and migration between harts see one layout. Architectural per-byte type tags were considered and rejected as impractically expensive.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the 'tag' here is a type tag, not a CHERI capability tag
map_note: A-1; the one-layout invariant is what makes context save/restore at TEW=32 correct for state written at any TEW

statement: Viewing the tile state as a linearized buffer of 16*TE*TE bytes, the byte position of element (tile,row,col) at width tew is given by the punning() function: per-TEW ptile, minor_offset and major_offset formulas (TEW=8: ptile=tile, minor=(row%4)*4+(col%4), major=(row/4)*(TE/4)+(col/4); TEW=16: ptile=tile+((row&2)>>1), minor=(row%2)*4+(col%2)*2+((col/2)%2)*8, major=(row/4)*(TE/4)+(col/4); TEW=32: ptile=tile+2*(row/(TE/2))+((col&2)>>1), minor=(row%2)*8+(col%2)*4, major=((row/2)%(TE/4))*(TE/4)+(col/4); TEW=64: ptile=tile+(row/(TE/4)), minor=(col%2)*8, major=(row%(TE/4))*(TE/4)+(col/2)); offset = ptile*TE*TE + major_offset*16 + minor_offset.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; given as C pseudo-code, no proof of bijectivity offered
map_note: A-1; an executable specification of the state layout that a Sail model can transcribe directly and that an RTL refinement must match byte-for-byte

statement: Zvtbase adds an unprivileged read-only CSR mtype at address 0xC23 with fields: bits XLEN-1:24 reserved; 23:10 tm[13:0]; 9:8 reserved; 7:5 tk[2:0]; 4:2 reserved; 1:0 mtwiden[1:0].
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; CSR layout

statement: mtype.tm can hold values 0..TE inclusive; mtype.tk can hold values 0..4 inclusive; if mtwiden=0 the matrix unit is not configured.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; CSR range invariants

statement: The width of the tm field constrains TE to be at most 8192.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft. DIFFERENCE: present only in 26b (PR text); absent from 26a (Internal Review PDF)
map_note: A-1; an upper bound on the implementation parameter the model's type must respect

statement: General matrix-multiply form C[tm,tn] += A[tk,tm]^T * B[tk,tn]: A and B from vector register groups, C in a matrix tile, all three named by register specifier fields; tm and tk are mtype fields and tn = min(vl, ETE).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; the operational definition of tn

statement: Each vector-register-group input has tk rows; each row is held in one or more vector registers; the total number of vector registers fits in one eight-register group; each row fits within an aligned power-of-2 vector register group and the collection of rows fits in a (potentially larger) group; KMAX depends on element widths with maximum 4.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; operand layout constraint

statement: Successive matrix rows in a vector register group are separated by 8/KMAX vector registers (e.g. KMAX=4, LMUL=2: v8..v9, v10..v11, v12..v13, v14..v15; KMAX=4, LMUL=1: v8, v10, v12, v14 with odd registers skipped).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; row-stride rule for operand decode

statement: Vector register specifiers of matrix operands must be divisible by LMUL (KMAX=4, LMUL=2: v8 valid, v9 not; LMUL=1: both valid, v9 denoting the odd registers v9..v15).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; operand-validity check (consequence of violation is not stated here; see P-B-G049 'unsupported settings are reserved')

statement: Vector register specifiers, taken modulo 8, must be less than 8/KMAX (e.g. KMAX=4: v10 is invalid); this prevents register groups spanning EMUL=8 group boundaries.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; operand-validity check

statement: As with the vset family, the matrix configuration instructions do not raise illegal-instruction exceptions as a consequence of vtype.vill holding 1.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; exception behaviour of configuration instructions

statement: Encoding of configuration instructions (opcode 1010111, funct3 111, bits 31:29 = 100): msettn (bits 27:25=100, 24:23=00, 22:20=000, rs1, rd); msettm (22:20=001); msettk (22:20=010); msetmtypei (bit 28=altfmt, 27:25=100, 24:23=vsew, 22:20=100, 19:17=000, 16:15=mtwiden, rd=00000); msetmtype (27:25=010, rs2, rs1, rd=00000).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; 26a's rendering of the same table is line-broken by transliteration (ll.263-270) but carries the same bits
map_note: A-1; decoder table

statement: The existing vset[i]vl[i] instructions write zero to the mtype CSR.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; modifies the semantics of pre-existing V instructions
map_note: A-1; cross-extension side effect a model of V must be updated for

statement: msetmtype writes mtype and vtype from rs1 and rs2: first vl is written 0 and mtype with rs1; then vtype with rs2 as though by vsetvl; then if the new mtype.mtwiden != 0, vma and vta are set to 1, vill is set if the resulting TEW is unsupported, and vlmul is set by the formula below. msetmtypei is the same except mtwiden, vsew and altfmt come from immediates and all other fields are zero.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; CSR write semantics

statement: msetmtype[i] pseudo-code: vl=0; (mtype,vtype from immediates or rs1,rs2); if vtype invalid per vsetvl semantics then vill=1; if mtwiden != 0: TWIDEN = 1 << (mtwiden-1); TEW = SEW*TWIDEN; ETE = TEW<64 ? TE : TE/2; EVE = VLEN/SEW; vtype.vlmul = log2(min(8/KMAX, 8/TWIDEN, ceil(ETE/EVE))); vma=1; vta=1; vill |= (SEW*TWIDEN > ELEN); mtype.tk = min(mtype.tk, KMAX); mtype.tm = min(mtype.tm, LMUL*EVE, ETE); if vill or mtwiden==0 then mtype=0; if vill then vtype=0 and vill=1.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; pseudo-code is the normative statement
map_note: A-1; directly transcribable into a Sail function and the first place an ISA-vs-RTL divergence on vlmul derivation would show

statement: msettn sets tn/vl to rs1 constrained by the matrix configuration: if mtwiden==0 then rd = vl = rs1 following vsetvl semantics with the current vtype; else rd = vl = min(rs1, LMUL*EVE, ETE). msetmtype and msettn degenerate to vsetvl when the unit is unconfigured, so context-switch code can use them unconditionally.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; vl-write semantics

statement: msettm: rd = tm = min(rs1, LMUL*EVE, ETE); msettk: rd = tk = min(rs1, KMAX). If the matrix unit has not been configured (mtwiden=0) the new tm or tk value is 0; the same section also states that msettm and msettk raise an illegal-instruction exception when mtwiden=0.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the two sentences about mtwiden=0 (value becomes 0 vs. illegal-instruction trap) are in tension in both 26a and 26b and a model must pick one; the text does not resolve it
map_note: A-1; an unresolved ambiguity to raise with the spec authors before modelling

statement: Unlike the vsetvl family, msettn, msettm and msettk are not special-cased when rd and/or rs1 is x0.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; a deliberate departure from V semantics that a copied vsetvl model would get wrong

statement: KMAX is fixed by SEW and TWIDEN: TEW=8: SEW8/TWIDEN1 -> KMAX 4; TEW=16: SEW8/TW2 -> 4, SEW16/TW1 -> 2; TEW=32: SEW8/TW4 -> 4, SEW16/TW2 -> 2, SEW32/TW1 -> 1; TEW=64: SEW16/TW4 -> 2, SEW32/TW2 -> 1, SEW64/TW1 -> 1.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; lookup table used by msetmtype, msettk and operand decode

statement: Tile Subset Specifier (TSS), a scalar: bits XLEN-1:31 reserved; 30:27 tile specifier (0-15); 26:24 pattern (0=row, 1=col, >1 reserved); 23:0 index within pattern.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; operand format for all move/load/store

statement: When there are fewer than 16 tiles at the selected TEW, the log2(16/NTiles) LSBs of the TSS tile-specifier field are ignored, so the field always refers to a valid tile.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; tile-specifier normalisation

statement: For row and column patterns the TSS index is an unsigned one-dimensional row/column index; indices >= ETE are reserved, and pattern values >1 are reserved. (Expected implementation behaviour: ignore reserved bits, take pattern mod 2 and index mod ETE.)
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the mod-ETE behaviour is an expectation in a NOTE, not a requirement
map_note: A-1; reserved-value handling the model must leave UNSPECIFIED or pin as the NOTE suggests

statement: vtle<EEW>/vtse<EEW> transfer matrix tile subsets between tile state and memory and support TEW values corresponding to all supported SEW settings (8..ELEN); implementations must provide vector loads and stores with EEWs corresponding to all supported SEW settings (8..ELEN).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; see tension with the Zvtbase TEW=32-only statement (P-B-G008)
map_note: G-c4; these are the only VME instructions that touch memory, so the per-access checking goal attaches here

statement: Encoding of vtle/vtse: vector load opcode 0000111 (load tile) and store opcode 0100111 (store tile); nf field = eee selecting EEW (000=8, 001=16, 010=32, 011=64, 1xx reserved); mew=1; mop=00; vm=1; rs2 = TSS; rs1 = base address; width=111; vd/vs3=0.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; uses the mew=1 space of the vector load/store opcodes
map_note: A-1; decoder table

statement: rs1 holds the base address in memory and rs2 holds the TSS; vtle/vtse do not support masks; EEW is statically encoded in the instruction.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: G-c4; defines the address operand and rules out masked (skipped) elements

statement: vtle/vtse always load and store the tile subset to a contiguous region of memory; for the row and column patterns the elements are stored in increasing index order in memory.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the footprint is therefore (number of body elements)*EEW/8 contiguous bytes from the base, element i at base + i*EEW/8 (the latter is the natural reading; the text does not write the address formula)
map_note: G-c4; the set of addresses accessed, which is what a per-access check must range over

statement: For vtle/vtse the body elements are those with indices in [vstart, min(vl, ETE) - 1] and the tail elements are those with indices >= min(vl, ETE); since vl=tn is the row length, column transfers may need an extra msettn to set vl to the column length.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: G-c4; bounds the element range (and hence the byte range) any access check must cover

statement: For the purposes of exception handling, vtle/vtse are considered to access memory in ascending order beginning at the byte determined by a function of the base address in rs1, the vstart value, and the instruction EEW; no memory is accessed below the elements specified by the vstart value.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the function of (rs1, vstart, EEW) is not written out; nothing is said about address translation, PMP/PMA, or page-fault granularity per element, nor that accesses are 'treated as scalar accesses'
map_note: G-c4; the only ordering/resumption statement, and the one AIVHAI would have to strengthen to 'each element is checked as a scalar access of EEW bytes'

statement: The matrix extension follows the precise exception model of the vector extension, allowing memory to be updated past the element indicated by vstart on a trap.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; inherits the V-extension trap model by reference only; which parts of V's per-element protection/translation rules carry over is not restated
map_note: G-c4; on a trap mid-transfer, elements beyond vstart may already have been written, so a capability/PMP violation on element i does not imply elements > i were not stored

statement: Misaligned element addresses raise either a load/store address-misaligned exception or a load/store access-fault exception; that is, unlike the vector extension, Zvt does not permit misaligned element accesses (rationale: new software with natural-alignment ABIs; simplifies implementations and detects programming errors).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the choice between the two exception codes is implementation-defined
map_note: G-c4; alignment is checked per element, and the natural-alignment requirement means an element never straddles a page or a cache line (helpful for per-element capability bounds checking)

statement: If mtwiden=0, the vtle/vtse instructions are reserved.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; no memory access can occur while the unit is unconfigured

statement: vtmv.v.t vd, rs1 moves a tile subset (TSS in rs1) to vector register group vd using TEW=SEW; vtmv.t.v rs1, vs2 moves vector register group vs2 to the tile subset; both support TEW for all supported SEW (8..ELEN). Encoding: opcode 1010111, funct3 110, vm=1; vtmv.v.t funct6 010000 with rs2 field 11111; vtmv.t.v funct6 010111 with vd field 0.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; register-to-tile transfer semantics and decode; no memory involved

statement: For vtmv the body elements are indices [vstart, min(vl, ETE) - 1] and tail elements are indices >= min(vl, ETE); if mtwiden=0 the instructions are reserved.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; tail policy for the vector destination is not restated here (vta is forced to 1 by msetmtype)
map_note: A-1; body/tail bound

statement: Matrix arithmetic instructions have the form C += A^T * B with C in a tile and A, B in vector register groups; unsupported vtype or mtype settings are reserved; an illegal-instruction exception is raised if vstart is nonzero.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; 'reserved' leaves the behaviour on bad settings unspecified rather than mandating a trap
map_note: A-1; precondition set of the arithmetic instructions

statement: Operand datatype selection: the datatype of vs2 is given by opcode and SEW; of vs1 by altfmt and SEW; of mtd by opcode, SEW and TWIDEN. Instruction table: vtfmm.tvv (SEW8/TW4/alt0 E4M3xE4M3->FP32; SEW8/TW4/alt1 E4M3xE5M2->FP32; SEW16/TW2/alt0 FP16xFP16->FP32; SEW32/TW1 FP32->FP32; SEW64/TW1 FP64->FP64), vtfmm.alt.tvv (SEW8/alt0 E5M2xE4M3; SEW8/alt1 E5M2xE5M2; SEW16/alt1 BF16xBF16->FP32), vtmmu.tvv (uint8 x uint8 -> int32; alt1: uint8 x int8), vtmms.tvv (int8 x uint8 -> int32; alt1: int8 x int8).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the mixed-signedness and mixed-FP8 cases are the 'mixed-precision widening' rules; TWIDEN is always 4 for 8-bit and 2 for 16-bit inputs, so the accumulator is 32-bit for every sub-32-bit multiplicand
map_note: A-1; type-dispatch table for the arithmetic

statement: The arithmetic instructions use tm, tn and tk to determine the computation; if any of these is zero, no computation is performed and no state is updated.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; 'no state is updated' presumably includes fflags, though that is not spelled out
map_note: A-1; zero-dimension no-op property

statement: Any tile elements outside [0, tm-1] x [0, tn-1] are tail elements and are handled with a tail-agnostic policy (for matrix arithmetic and for vtzero).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; tail-agnostic means the model must treat those elements as UNSPECIFIED after the instruction
map_note: A-1; nondeterminism the ISA model must expose rather than pin (a refinement-check hazard if the RTL is checked against one pinned value)

statement: The invalid (NV) and overflow (OF) scalar floating-point exception flags are updated by the results of floating-point matrix operations; the inexact, underflow and divide-by-zero flags are not updated, nor is the fixed-point saturation flag (vxsat).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; fflags side-effect contract

statement: For SEW <= 16, floating-point products are bulk-normalised and accumulated in fixed-point arithmetic, then converted to FP32 with rounding to odd per the RVBNA Algorithm, then added to the accumulator in IEEE 754 arithmetic with rounding to odd as described in RVBNA Rounding to Odd.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; defers the exact reduction order and rounding to the RVBNA chapter. DIFFERENCE: 26b pins the RVBNA references to riscv-isa-manual commit a38e1213 (src/unpriv/rvbna.adoc); 26a cites 'RVBNA Algorithm' by name only
map_note: A-1; the dot-product numerics the model must implement bit-exactly, and which must be fetched from RVBNA (not in this share)

statement: For SEW >= 32, floating-point products are computed in IEEE 754 arithmetic, rounded to a TEW-bit value using the rounding mode in frm, then added to the accumulator in IEEE 754 arithmetic using the same rounding mode (product rounded before accumulation; not fused).
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; with KMAX=1 at SEW>=32 (except SEW32/TW2 at TEW=64 where KMAX=1 too) there is one product per accumulate, so no reduction-order question arises at these widths
map_note: A-1; rounding contract

statement: If Zvtbf16fmm is implemented, the implementation must support selecting altfmt=1 when SEW=16; if Zvti8i32mm or Zvtofp8fmm is implemented, it must support selecting altfmt=1 when SEW=8.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; couples Zvt to the altfmt bit of vtype
map_note: A-1; a vtype legality rule conditioned on which Zvt extensions are present

statement: Matrix arithmetic encoding: OP-VE major opcode 1110111, funct6 111100, vm=1, vs2, vs1; funct3 001 for vtfmm.tvv (rd[0]=0) and vtfmm.alt.tvv (rd[0]=1); funct3 000 for vtmmu.tvv (rd[0]=0) and vtmms.tvv (rd[0]=1); rd[4:2] = t[3:1] tile number. Tile-selection bits are allocated from the MSB of rd; bits not present are defined zero; if t modulo (16/NTiles) is nonzero the instruction is reserved.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; decoder table and tile-specifier validity

statement: vtzero mtd writes 0 to each element of the tm x tn submatrix of the destination tile (outside is tail-agnostic); supports all SEW-derived TEWs; encoding opcode 1010111, funct6 010000, vs2=11110, vs1=00000, funct3 110, rd = tttt0.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; the only architectural way to clear tile contents (relevant to the AIVHAI tenant-isolation story: residual tile state across a context switch is otherwise only bounded by MS-driven save/restore)

statement: The mtype CSR is part of the vector context and its accessibility is controlled by the VS fields; the MS fields do not affect accessibility of mtype.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; CSR access-control rule

statement: A Zvt context status field MS is added at mstatus[30:29] and shadowed in sstatus[30:29], defined analogously to FS. Any instruction that accesses the matrix tile state raises an illegal-instruction exception when mstatus.MS is Off; vset* and mset* do not access the tile state.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; mstatus[30:29] was previously reserved
map_note: G-c; the privileged gate the CF must use to deny a compartment the matrix unit, and the one the RTL must enforce on every tile-touching instruction

statement: When mstatus.MS is Initial or Clean, executing any instruction that changes tile state changes mstatus.MS to Dirty; implementations may also change MS from Initial/Clean to Dirty at any time even without a change in tile state. If mstatus.MS is Dirty then mstatus.SD is 1, otherwise SD follows existing rules.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft; the spurious-Dirty allowance is nondeterminism the model must expose
map_note: A-1; dirty-tracking contract

statement: With the hypervisor extension, vsstatus[30:29] carries a second MS field; when V=1 both vsstatus.MS and mstatus.MS are in effect (illegal-instruction if either is Off), any tile-state change sets both to Dirty (with the same spurious-Dirty allowance), and vsstatus.SD is 1 when vsstatus.MS is Dirty.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; virtualisation of the enable/dirty state

statement: For the purposes of mstatus.VS and vsstatus.VS, all Zvt instructions (including configuration instructions) are considered to modify vector state; for the purposes of FS, the Zvt instructions that implicitly access fcsr are considered to modify floating-point state.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: A-1; cross-extension dirty-bit side effects

statement: vtdiscard (opcode 1010111, funct6 010000, vs2=11100, vs1=00000, funct3 110, rd=00000) raises illegal-instruction if mstatus.MS=Off (or V=1 and vsstatus.MS=Off), otherwise sets mstatus.MS (and vsstatus.MS when V=1) to Initial; it raises illegal-instruction if vtype.vill=1 but not because mtype.mtwiden is zero; it does not write the tile state, and for ABI purposes the tile state becomes UNSPECIFIED.
assumptions: Zvt v0.4 draft
map_note: G-c; after vtdiscard the runtime may skip saving the tiles, so the previous tenant's tile contents can survive into the next context unless the CF zeroes them: a confidentiality consideration for the isolation argument, stated only as an ABI matter here

statement: Cr (the VME accumulator array) is architectural state of mr x nr x c bits; it can only be read a row at a time and written either a row or a column at a time; writing by columns then reading by rows effects a transpose.
assumptions: Author's opinion, draft 0.1.1 (2025-08-31), explicitly 'not official nor authoritative'; written before the TG fixed names; uses BLIS Cr for what Zvt calls tiles
source: Killian-25 §Basics of VME ISA l.1218; §Bc Packing ll.540-549
map_note: A-1; a read-row/write-row-or-column asymmetry that Zvt v0.4 does not adopt (Zvt reads and writes both rows and columns)

statement: VME should stick with a square Cr (mr = nr) because the BLIS inner loop needs the same VL for the Va and Vb loads; non-square Cr would require two VL registers for which there is no 32-bit opcode space.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1, author's recommendation; Zvt v0.4 adopted square tiles
map_note: none; design rationale, realised in Zvt by TExTE tiles

statement: VME should have the usual lazy context-switch optimisations as for FPRs and VRs, plus a way to zero all accumulators quickly and a bit indicating whether Cr is all zeros, read on context save and written to thread saved state; four save/restore cases are enumerated (00, 01, 10, 11); two mstatus bits analogous to FS/VS/XS are needed.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; Zvt v0.4 adopted MS[1:0] in mstatus plus vtzero and vtdiscard but not an all-zero bit
map_note: G-c; context-switch state the CF must save/restore for compartment isolation; the 'all-zero bit' is a proposal only

statement: Base VME should have exactly one Cr accumulator set (m0); the assembler should still carry an m0 specifier to leave room for extensions; adding a second Cr would significantly increase minimum area and power (accumulators are at least 20% of a MAC unit in some designs).
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; superseded by Zvt v0.4's four TEW=32 tiles
source: Killian-25 §Number of Cr Tiles ll.1194-1198; §BLIS l.345
map_note: none; superseded design preference

statement: It is critical that the accumulators be co-located with the MACs that use them; centralising the accumulators in a large MAC array would introduce significant wiring and bandwidth challenges and ruin energy efficiency.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; microarchitectural guidance, not an ISA property
map_note: none; microarchitectural placement advice

statement: The VME ISA deals only in logical rows and columns; the mapping from a logical mr x nr Cr to a physical ur x uc MAC array with local accumulators is not architectural (an illustrative mapping: Cr[i,j] lives in MAC (i mod e, j mod f) at local accumulator index derived from i/e and j/f, e.g. a 128x128 Cr on a 64x64 array uses local accumulator {i[6],j[6]} of MAC (i[5:0],j[5:0])).
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1
map_note: G-c; the refinement map between architectural tile state and the physical accumulator SRAM is implementation-private, so a CVA6-CHERI-VME refinement proof must supply its own abstraction function

statement: Rank-k updates (k > 1 products summed per accumulate) change results relative to rank-1 because floating-point addition is not associative; this would not be tolerated for HPC but may be acceptable for quantised AI.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; Zvt v0.4 answers this by fixing KMAX and specifying the RVBNA fixed-point bulk-normalised accumulation (P-B-G059)
map_note: A-1; motivates why the reduction order must be pinned in the ISA model rather than left to the implementation

statement: Background Cr load/store (an optional extension) would copy accumulators to a non-architectural shadow copy in a 1RW SRAM and stream it to/from memory while the inner loop runs; 'issues regarding errors during background load/store would of course have to be addressed' (left open).
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; not in Zvt v0.4
map_note: G-c4; an asynchronous accelerator-initiated memory stream whose fault model is explicitly unaddressed, exactly the DMA-like path AIVHAI's non-bypass claim must cover if such an extension is ever adopted

statement: Remote (shared between multiple processors) VME MAC arrays may require Cr load/store instructions direct to memory that bypass the VRF, as in the Zvma proposal of 2024-12-18; whether that is base or extension is for the TG (and Zvt v0.4 did add vtle/vtse).
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1
source: Killian-25 §Local vs. Remote MAC Array ll.1188-1190; l.1297-1299
map_note: G-c4; memory paths that originate at the matrix unit rather than the scalar/vector LSU are the ones the per-access check must not miss

statement: Proposed instruction set: read a logical row of Cr to vd; write a logical row or column of Cr from vs1 (SEW-wide, in integer, floating-point and raw forms); vsetvli-like instructions mapping application m, n, k to implementation values; Cr <- vs1 x vs2 and Cr <- Cr + vs1 x vs2 in SEWfmt x SEWfmt, SEWaltfmt x SEWaltfmt and SEWfmt x SEWaltfmt flavours; INT4/FP4 handled by special SEW=8 instructions; scaling instructions (mxfp8.vv, vfp45.vv, vfint4.vv) applying a vector of scale factors to every N elements; gemv instructions vmacc.avx/vfmacc.avx m0, vs1, rs2/fs2, imm with imm an offset into Cr in units of VLEN*LMUL/SEW.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; placeholders, 'the TG is likely to change the details'; the raw form, the non-accumulating Cr <- vs1 x vs2, the scaling and the gemv instructions are not in Zvt v0.4
source: Killian-25 §Basics of VME ISA ll.1247-1291; §OCP MX Scaling ll.861-869; §FP4.5 Scaling ll.891-907
map_note: none; proposals not adopted in the v0.4 text in this share

statement: A 'raw' accumulator format may be needed: the accumulator might have an internal representation (e.g. FP22/E8M13 as on Hopper, or 16- or 20-bit formats) that must be saved and restored on context switch and differs from the integer and floating-point read-out forms.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; Zvt v0.4 instead fixes TEW=32 (or 64) IEEE/integer accumulators with a mandated punning layout
map_note: A-1; if an implementation holds accumulators in a non-architectural internal format, the ISA-level observation (vtse at TEW=32) must still equal the specified IEEE value, which is a refinement obligation

statement: Integer accumulation width analysis: for symmetric OCP INT8 (E0M7) products accumulated over k <= 2^16 terms, 30 bits (sign + x1 + x2 + 15) are required; for E0M3 products 22 bits; for UINT8 x UINT8 products 31 bits; limiting kc to 4096 reduces these to 27 and 19 bits.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; analysis under the author's assumed k bound; Zvt v0.4 mandates Int32 accumulators for int8, which satisfies these bounds with margin
map_note: A-1; an overflow-freedom argument for the int32 accumulator that a model could state as a lemma under a k bound (the Zvt text itself specifies wraparound semantics only implicitly, via Int32)

statement: Mixed-FP8 product range analysis: the product Ex1My1 x Ex2My2 requires at most ExaMya with xa = max(x1,x2)+1 and ya = 1+y1+y2 to be exact, and accumulating the maximum product over k = 2^16 terms requires accumulator formats from E6M7 to E7M7 depending on the pair (Table 8); whether E7 is really needed in practice is uncertain.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; the table's exponents are garbled by transliteration and must be checked against the PDF
map_note: none; motivates accumulator-width choice, not a property of Zvt as specified

statement: Block scaling for OCP MX (E8M0 over 32 elements) and NVFP4/FP4.5 (E4M3 over 16 elements) must be applied before forming the product (unlike per-tensor/per-axis scaling, which can be applied after); OCP scaling needs 2x widening to BF16 (4x for MXFP4, which RVV lacks); exponent-addition overflow would produce Infinity but is argued never to occur given how scale factors are computed.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; scaled formats are not in Zvt v0.4 (which supports OCP FP8 E4M3/E5M2 unscaled)
source: Killian-25 §Scaled Formats ll.849-857; §OCP MXFP4 l.883; §FP4.5 Scaling l.891; Glossary l.1561
map_note: none; outside the v0.4 instruction set

statement: In the BLIS inner loop the vector loads for Va and Vb must use the same VL, and the Va/Vb loads should be a multiple of W (the RVV load/store bandwidth in bits per cycle) so as not to waste the limiting resource; the Ac and Bc packing areas should be page-aligned and therefore cache-block aligned so vector loads do not cross cache lines and DTLB/D-cache misses are reduced.
assumptions: Killian draft 0.1.1; software/performance guidance on how the vector loads feeding VME are laid out, not a hardware requirement
source: Killian-25 §BLIS l.353; l.476; §GEMM Microarchitecture l.687; §Basics of VME ISA l.1233
map_note: none; software-side locality advice; note that under Zvt v0.4 all operand loads are ordinary RVV unit-stride loads, so they inherit RVV's (not VME's) memory-access checking

statement: Any CHERI RISC-V implementation must support one of the RVY bases (RV32Y/RV64Y); every RVY base requires a capability-encoding format (e.g. RV64LYA, XLEN=64) that gives full details of how capabilities are represented in memory and registers, including bounds precision and the available combinations of permissions.
assumptions: RV64LYA is the only format defined in this document; RV32Y formats are future work
map_note: G-c; fixes which base (RV64Y + RV64LYA) CVA6-CHERI must refine

statement: RVY widens every register that can hold an address (GPRs, pc, address-holding CSRs) from XLEN to YLEN=2*XLEN bits and adds a one-bit capability tag to each; the memory representation is always YLEN bits, little-endian only, with the address in the lower XLEN bits and the metadata in the upper XLEN bits.
assumptions: little-endian layouts only in this version
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 2.3 Capability Registers and Format, lines 553-566
map_note: G-c; register-file and memory layout the RTL must match

statement: When an instruction writes non-capability data to an extended register, the metadata fields and capability tag of the destination are set to 0 unless that instruction's definition explicitly states otherwise.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; register write-back invariant

statement: The capability tag is a single out-of-band, hardware-managed bit associated with each YLEN-bit register and each naturally aligned YLEN-bit memory location; it cannot be directly set by software and indicates that the capability was derived correctly (provenance, integrity, monotonicity).
assumptions: not all memory supports tags; the EEI defines which regions do
map_note: G-c5; tag storage must be hidden and hardware-managed

statement: Whenever an instruction writes a capability with tag=1 to a register or memory: at least one input operand had tag=1 (provenance), the operation was legal and did not increase bounds or permissions (monotonicity), and the instruction may have checked that no input was corrupted (integrity; not all instructions check all operands).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; the core monotonicity/provenance invariant AIVHAI's capability-monotonicity proof targets

statement: Storing a capability preserves its tag only if the store is performed via a valid capability that authorizes storing capabilities to that location (every stored byte within bounds, suitable write permissions); loading a capability preserves the tag in the destination only if the load is authorized likewise (every byte in bounds, suitable read permissions).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; provenance across memory

statement: Using an invalid capability (tag=0) to dereference memory or authorize any operation raises an exception; all capabilities derived from invalid capabilities are themselves invalid; writing non-capability data into a register or memory location sets the tag to 0.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; fail-closed dereference

statement: Every naturally aligned YLEN-bit memory region has a non-addressable one-bit tag that the hardware manages atomically with the data; the implementation must set the tag to zero if any byte in the region is ever written by an operation other than the successful store of a capability operand (e.g. SW always clears it); a failed SC leaves the tag unmodified.
assumptions: none
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 2.3.4 Capability tags in Memory, lines 634-640
map_note: G-c5; tag-clearing on any non-capability write

statement: All system memory and caches that store capabilities must preserve the tagged-memory abstraction, handling the capability tags atomically with the data.
assumptions: applies to the whole memory hierarchy, not just the hart
map_note: G-c5; cache/memory tag atomicity

statement: Bounds are a half-open byte range [base, top); checking is byte-by-byte so an access may be fully in-bounds, partially out-of-bounds, or fully out-of-bounds; a partially or fully out-of-bounds data access or instruction fetch raises an exception; base is XLEN bits inclusive, top is XLEN+1 bits exclusive, length = top - base is XLEN+1 bits.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; bounds-check semantics every load/store/fetch must implement

statement: YLENR and YTOPR saturate their (XLEN+1)-bit result to 2^XLEN-1 when it overflows an XLEN-bit register; YBASER returns the base.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; instruction semantics

statement: Bounds are only ever reduced: YBNDSW/YBNDSWI set base=rs1.address and length from rs2/imm and clear the tag if the bounds cannot be encoded exactly; YBNDSRW uses the smallest representable bounds that contain the requested range and remain within the initial bounds.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; monotonic bounds derivation

statement: Any address within a capability's bounds is always representable and preserves the tag; all instructions that derive a capability with a new address (YADDRW, YADD, YADDI, ...) must check that the new address does not change the decoding of the bounds, and if it moves outside the representable range the hardware sets the tag to zero.
assumptions: formats other than RV64LYA may specify an alternative check but must still support one-past-the-end pointers
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 2.3.7 Representability and Updating the Address, lines 718-741
map_note: G-c; representability check on every address update

statement: A hart has a single byte-addressable 2^XLEN address space; each memory region capable of holding a capability stores a tag for each naturally aligned YLEN bits (16 bytes in RV64), so tagged capabilities can only be stored at naturally aligned addresses; tags must be atomically bound to the data they protect.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c5; tag granule is one per aligned 16 bytes on RV64

statement: Address arithmetic is modulo 2^XLEN and the representable range is circular, but the decoded top is XLEN+1 bits and does not wrap; a capability with architectural top > 2^XLEN cannot be generated by any valid derivation and is only possible by a logic or memory fault; unlike malformed bounds it is not special-cased in decoding and normal bounds-check rules apply (fail-closed).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; the top>2^XLEN corner the RTL must handle by ordinary comparison

statement: Capabilities with CT!=0 are sealed: they cannot be dereferenced to access memory, and instructions that would alter address, bounds, or permissions of a sealed source produce an invalid capability; CT=0 is unsealed, CT=1 is a sealed entry point (sentry), all other CT values are reserved.
assumptions: RV64LYA has a 1-bit CT field
map_note: G-c; sealing semantics

statement: A sealed entry point capability may be passed as rs1 to JALR; an unsealed version is written to pc; if rd is not x0 the link capability written to rd is a sealed entry point capability.
assumptions: none
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 2.3.9 Sealed entry point capability, lines 783-789
map_note: G-c; sentry control-flow integrity in the fetch/branch unit

statement: Permissions grant access subject to the capability being valid, unsealed, and bounds checks passing; any memory operation is also contingent on virtual memory, PMP, and PMAs even if the capability grants sufficient permissions; all encoding formats must support at least R, W, X, C, LM, ASR; permissions can be cleared (YPERMC) but never added.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; permission monotonicity and PMP/PMA composition

statement: C-permission allows reading tags if R is also granted and writing tags if W is also granted; if C is missing, the tags for capability loads and stores are read and written as zero.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; tag-gating of LY/SY

statement: If the authorizing capability grants R and C but not LM, a capability loaded through it has W and LM removed; this stripping applies only to valid loaded capabilities that are not sealed, after all other checks, so non-capability data and sealed capabilities are not modified.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; load-path metadata modification

statement: ASR-permission only has effect when installed in pc; it does not bypass privilege checks; lacking ASR in pc prevents access to privileged CSRs and restricted instructions even if the privilege mode would permit it; writing xtidc requires ASR but reading does not; CBO.INVAL, MRET and SRET require ASR; all other privileged CSRs require ASR for any access.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; privileged-state gating by pc

statement: Permission dependency rules (Table 6): C valid only if R or W; LM valid only if C and R; ASR valid only if X; clearing a permission may therefore clear dependents; encoding formats and extensions (Zyhybrid Table 51, Zylg Section 13.3.1) may add constraints.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; legal-permission-combination invariant

statement: SDP bits are not interpreted by the CPU but follow the same rules as permissions: they can only be cleared and never set on valid capabilities.
assumptions: RV64LYA has 4 SDP bits
map_note: G-c; monotonicity extends to SDP

statement: Root Executable = unsealed, infinite bounds, at least X, R, C, LM, ASR; Root Data = unsealed, infinite bounds, at least R, W, C, LM; these are the maximum encodable values, and harts may specify implementation-defined initial values with reduced bounds and/or permissions.
assumptions: implementation-defined initial capability values
map_note: G-c; reset-state capability values

statement: The NULL capability is an invalid capability with all-zero metadata and address; it grants no permissions and any dereference raises an exception; x0 is the NULL capability with tag 0.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; x0 semantics

statement: RV64LYA encoding parameters: MW=14, EW=6, CAP_MAX_E=52, enableL8=0, REP_RANGE=rc1 (one extra bit, centered out-of-bounds region), AP_MAX=all ones, AP_ENC=full1 (all permission combinations representable), AUIPC_SHIFT=12.
assumptions: XLEN=64; RV32Y formats will differ
map_note: G-c; constants of the CVA6-CHERI format

statement: Integrity check rules: (1) the bounds are not malformed; (2) the metadata has no bits or fields set to a value not valid for the implemented extensions (e.g. ASR without X). Failure on a tagged capability indicates state corruption or incompatible/defective CHERI IP.
assumptions: checks are less rigorous than parity or ECC
map_note: G-c; integrity predicate

statement: Valid capabilities are guaranteed to satisfy all integrity rules unless corruption or incompatible IP is present, because valid derivation preserves integrity; integrity checks on operands expected to be valid are therefore optional; instructions that can produce a valid capability from an invalid input must perform the check (in RVY only the rs2 input of YBLD).
assumptions: implementation choice whether to enforce optional checks
map_note: G-c; integrity-preservation invariant and the single mandatory check

statement: A capability whose decoded bounds exceed 2^XLEN is a loss of integrity but is deliberately not included in the integrity checks (requires full bounds decoding); hardware relies on fail-closed bounds checking and YBLD subset enforcement instead; detection is deferred to future reliability extensions.
assumptions: out of scope for this version
map_note: G-c; documents what the RTL need not detect

statement: Table 9 capability states: Valid (tag 1, passes integrity, top <= 2^XLEN); Invalid (tag 0, arbitrary payload, cannot authorize unless as YBLD rs2); Corrupted valid with integrity failure (tag 1, not legal, detected by optional checks); Corrupted valid with top > 2^XLEN (tag 1, not legal, not detected, handled by bounds-check logic).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; state partition for refinement

statement: All state that can hold addresses is extended to YLEN bits and carries a hardware-managed tag; mconfigptr is the only documented exception and is not widened.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; CSR widening set

statement: For each instruction executed the hardware checks pc: tag set, not sealed, grants X, all bytes of the instruction in bounds, all integrity checks pass; a failing check raises a CHERI exception; the EEI must initialize pc bounds and permissions so the program can run.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; fetch-stage check

statement: utidc: any write raises an exception unless ASR is set in pc; the EEI sets its tag to zero and its metadata and address are UNSPECIFIED.
assumptions: UNSPECIFIED reset metadata/address
map_note: G-c; CSR semantics

statement: When a WARL CSR is widened its metadata and tag also become WARL; if the final written capability cannot be written unmodified due to WARL behavior it is considered invalid and must be written with tag 0.
assumptions: WARL restriction set is implementation-defined (e.g. fixing permissions or requiring non-reserved fields)
map_note: G-c; CSR WARL invalidation

statement: CSRRW on a YLEN-bit CSR reads and writes YLEN bits and invalidates the written capability if it fails integrity or cannot be written unmodified; CSRRS/CSRRC/immediate forms compute an XLEN-bit address value and write it with YADDRW semantics (Table 11 widths); suppressed accesses have no side effects.
assumptions: none
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 2.6.4 and Table 11, lines 1213-1255; Chapter 15, lines 6115-6200
map_note: G-c; CSR access datapath

statement: Every memory access must be authorized by a valid capability; fetches and data accesses raise a CHERI exception if: tag is 0 (all memory-access encodings with rs1=x0 are reserved), capability is sealed, any integrity check fails, any byte is out of bounds, the virtual address is invalid when VM is enabled, or the required permission (X for fetch via pc, R for loads, W for stores, R and W for AMOs, via rs1) is absent.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; master list of checks every access path must implement

statement: Opcode allocation: RVY-A inst[6:2]=11110, RVY-B 10110, RVY-C 01010 (formerly custom-3/2/1), leaving custom inst[6:2]=00010 for vendor use.
assumptions: several instruction encodings are marked not final
map_note: G-c; decoder

statement: YADD/YADDI/YADDRW copy rs1 to rd and set a new address; rd.tag=0 if rs1 is sealed, if the result cannot be represented exactly, or if rs1 fails integrity checks (Sail: incCapAddrChecked / setCapAddrChecked).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; address-update instructions

statement: cap2 is a capability subset of cap1 iff all AP and SDP permissions of cap2 are granted by cap1, cap2.top <= cap1.top, cap2.base >= cap1.base, and both pass all integrity checks (Zylg adds: cap2.GL=0 or cap1.GL=1).
assumptions: integrity clause only material for YBLD rs2 and YSS
map_note: G-c; subset relation used by YBLD/YUNSEALS/YSS

statement: YPERMC clears permission bits per an rs2 mask; hardwired-one bits are not cleared; the result is re-encoded applying the dependency rules; if the format cannot represent the requested set a minimal set (possibly none) is returned but permissions are never added; rd.tag=0 if rs1 is sealed and any AP/SDP bit was affected; if rs1 fails integrity, rd.tag, AP, SDP and P are all zeroed.
assumptions: the Operation listing is manually maintained rather than extracted from the Sail model
map_note: G-c; permission-clearing datapath

statement: Dependent permissions added by future extensions must be allocated to bits currently reported as 1 and must be cleared when the permission they depend on is cleared (forward compatibility of YPERMC).
assumptions: constraint on future extensions
map_note: none; design rule for extensions

statement: YMV copies rs1 to rd unchanged and can propagate valid capabilities that fail integrity checks; YHIW writes rs2 into the metadata and sets rd.tag=0.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; copy and metadata-write semantics

statement: YBNDSW/YBNDSWI: rd.tag=0 if rs1.tag=0, rs1 sealed, rd bounds exceed rs1 bounds, requested bounds not exactly encodable, or rs1 fails integrity; Sail cond also clears if the new capability has malformed bounds or invalid reserved fields; YBNDSWI decodes a 9-bit immediate into byte/8-byte/16-byte/page-granular lengths (imm=0 means 4096).
assumptions: YBNDSWI listing manually maintained
map_note: G-c; bounds-setting datapath

statement: YBNDSRW rounds base down and top up by the smallest amounts needed to form a representable capability; rd.tag=0 if rs1.tag=0, rs1 sealed, rd bounds exceed rs1 bounds, or integrity fails.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; rounding bounds derivation

statement: YUNSEALS copies rs2 to rd with CT=0 and tag=1 iff rs1.tag=1, rs1 unsealed, rs2.tag=1, rs2 sealed, and rs2 is a subset of rs1; otherwise tag=0.
assumptions: listing manually maintained; rs1=x0 is not guaranteed to remain a tag/type-clearing pseudo-instruction
map_note: G-c; unseal authorization

statement: YBLD copies rs2 to rd with tag=1 iff rs1.tag=1, rs1 unsealed, rs2 subset of rs1, and rs2 passes a mandatory integrity check (malformed bounds, perms, reserved bits); otherwise tag=0; this is the only RVY instruction that can set a tag on an arbitrary bit pattern.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; the one path that re-tags data, critical for monotonicity

statement: YSEALE copies rs2 to rd and sets CT=1; rd.tag=0 if rs2 is sealed or fails integrity; rs1!=x0 is reserved; if the format does not support CT=1 the instruction is reserved.
assumptions: listing manually maintained; encoding not final
map_note: G-c; sentry creation

statement: YBASER, YLENR and YTOPR return zero if rs1's bounds cannot be decoded or rs1 fails integrity; YLENR returns 2^XLEN-1 for length 2^XLEN; YTOPR saturates to 2^XLEN-1; rs1.tag does not affect the result.
assumptions: YTOPR listing manually maintained
map_note: G-c; bounds decode outputs

statement: YTAGR zero-extends the tag; YPERMR returns the AP/SDP bit field with reserved and unimplemented-extension bits in [23:0] hardwired to 1, and reports all allocated permission bits as 0 if rs1 fails integrity; YTYPER returns the CT field (the Sail model stores RV64LYA's 1-bit CT as boolean sealed; wider formats must return the full field); YHIR returns the metadata; none depend on rs1.tag.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; field-extraction instructions

statement: YEQ compares all YLEN bits and the tag; YSS sets rd=1 iff the tags are equal and rs2 is a subset of rs1 (capIsSubset returns false if either input has malformed bounds, perms, or non-zero reserved bits); YAMASK returns the alignment mask for the nearest representable length (getRepresentableAlignmentMask).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; comparison and mask instructions
