statement: LY and SY atomically access YLEN bits of data and the associated tag; they additionally check C-permission; all capability data accesses require naturally aligned addresses and raise an access fault (not a misaligned fault) otherwise, because misaligned capability accesses cannot be emulated (one hidden tag per aligned YLEN region).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; atomic tag+data access and alignment rule

statement: LY result: write loaded data and tag to rd; if rs1 lacks C then rd.tag=0; if rd.tag=1, rs1 lacks LM and rd is unsealed, perform an implicit YPERMC clearing W and LM; the loaded capability may also be invalidated by platform-specified conditions (use-after-free schemes), PMA settings, or PTE configuration; trace interfaces report the final rd value; LY can propagate valid capabilities that fail integrity checks.
assumptions: platform-specified invalidation conditions are open
map_note: G-c; load-capability datapath

statement: LY/LR.Y exceptions: load access fault if misaligned; CHERI Load Access Fault if the authorizing capability has tag 0, is sealed, lacks R, any byte is out of bounds or the bounds could not be decoded, or any integrity check fails.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; load fault conditions

statement: SY stores rs2 with its tag to the naturally aligned location; the stored tag is zero if rs2.tag=0, rs1 lacks C, or platform/privileged configuration (PMAs, PTEs) requires it; exceptions: store/AMO access fault if misaligned, CHERI Store/AMO Access Fault for tag 0, sealed, missing W, out-of-bounds/undecodable bounds, integrity failure.
assumptions: extensions (Zylg) may add further tag-clearing circumstances
map_note: G-c; store-capability datapath

statement: Changes to base ISA: whenever an operand is used as an address all capability bits are fed in; any instruction writing back an address writes a full capability using YADDRW semantics; all other results zero the high bits and tag; ADD/ADDI are not affected and YADD/YADDI must be used for capability address incrementing.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; integer-pipeline write-back rule

statement: All load and store instructions use the full rs1 capability for authorization; all loads except LY set the result tag and metadata to zero; all stores except SY write zero to the tag(s) of the locations written, so a misaligned store may clear up to two tags; this applies to floating-point, vector, and atomic accesses.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c4; the general rule that vector loads/stores are authorized and tag-clearing exactly as scalar ones

statement: Whenever the pc address is modified it is always updated with YADDRW semantics (branches, direct jumps, link register); JALR computes new_pc = YADDRW(Unseal(rs1), offset); this can clear the target pc tag and then raise a CHERI Instruction Access Fault at the target (a future extension may fault at the branch instead).
assumptions: exception is raised at the target, not the branch
map_note: G-c; branch/jump pc update

statement: AUIPC (RVY) adds the shifted immediate (AUIPC_SHIFT, default 12) to pc with YADDRW semantics and clears rd.tag if the result cannot be represented exactly.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; pc-relative derivation

statement: JAL: target = YADDRW(pc, pc.address + imm); the pc of the next instruction is sealed as a sentry and written to rd. JALR: rs1 is written to the target pc; target address = (rs1.address + imm) with bit 0 cleared; the target pc is unsealed only if rs1 is a sentry, rs1.address[0]=0 and the immediate is zero; the address is set with YADDRW semantics; the link is sealed as a sentry.
assumptions: both listings are manually maintained rather than extracted from the Sail model
map_note: G-c; control-transfer semantics and sentry CFI

statement: RV64LYA metadata layout (bits of the upper 64): SDP 63:60, AP 52:45, P 44 (Zyhybrid only), GL 43 (Zylg only), CT 27, EF 26, T[11:3] 25:17, TE 16:14, B[13:3] 13:3, BE 2:0; all other bits are reserved and must be 0 in valid capabilities; T[13:12], T[2:0], B[2:0] are computed, not stored.
assumptions: XLEN=64; P and GL are reserved-zero when their extension is absent
map_note: G-c; bit-exact register/memory format

statement: RV64LYA AP field is 8 bits, one bit per permission (bit0 C, 1 W, 2 R, 3 X, 4 ASR, 5 LM, 6 LG, 7 SL); patterns encoding illegal combinations are reserved; with the P-bit there are 90 valid combinations in 9 bits (18 data-permission combinations x 5 X/ASR/P combinations).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; legal-AP-value set for integrity checks

statement: An invalid capability is produced when attempting to construct a capability whose bounds cannot be encoded (not representable); the address and bounds must be representable in valid capabilities; CAP_MAX_E = XLEN - MW + 2.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; representability invariant

statement: Normative bounds-decoding pseudocode: if EF=1 then E=0, T[EW/2-1:0]=TE, B[EW/2-1:0]=BE, LCout=(T[MW-3:0] < B[MW-3:0]), LMSB=enableL8?L8:0; else E=CAP_MAX_E-{L8?,TE,BE}, low bits of T and B are 0, LCout=(T[MW-3:EW/2] < B[MW-3:EW/2]), LMSB=1; and T[MW-1:MW-2] = B[MW-1:MW-2] + LCout + LMSB (relying on T = B + L and top >= base).
assumptions: the pseudocode is stated to be normative but intentionally simpler than the equivalent Sail definitions
map_note: A-1; the prose decoder and the Sail decoder must agree, and CVA6-CHERI must match both (G-c)

statement: Base and top are derived from address a by substituting a[E+MW-1:E] with B and T, clearing the lower E bits, and adding correction factors cb/ct; if E=0 the lower section is absent; if E+MW=XLEN the top section of top is only the lsb of ct and absent for base; if E+MW>XLEN neither top section exists and bounds do not depend on the address; the address can roam at least 2^(E+MW)/4 below base and above top while bounds decode correctly.
assumptions: none
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 3.1.5.3 Format of the Bounds, lines 3477-3519
map_note: G-c; decoder structure

statement: Correction factors cb, ct each take values -1, 0, +1, computed from unsigned comparisons A<R, T<R, B<R with A=a[E+MW-1:E] and R=B-2^(MW-2) (Table 27); the combinations (A<R=false,T<R=false,B<R=true) and (A<R=true,T<R=false,B<R=true) are impossible because B<R implies T<R; only six combinations are reachable.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; a provable decoder lemma (impossible cases) the RTL may exploit

statement: Top MSB correction: if E < CAP_MAX_E-1 and (top[XLEN:XLEN-1] - {0,base[XLEN-1]}) >= 2 (unsigned) then top[XLEN] is inverted; a capability has infinite bounds iff E=CAP_MAX_E and it is not malformed, equivalent to base=0 and top>=2^XLEN.
assumptions: none
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 3.1.5.5 Top Bound Address MSB Correction, lines 3611-3629
map_note: G-c; decoder edge rule

statement: Malformed bounds: malformedMSB = (E==CAP_MAX_E and B!=0) or (E==CAP_MAX_E-1 and B[MW-1]!=0); malformedLSB = (E<0) or (E==0 and enableL8); malformed = !EF and (malformedMSB or malformedLSB); malformed capabilities return base and top as zero (affecting YBASER etc.) and cause manipulation instructions such as YADDI to always clear the result tag.
assumptions: enableL8=0 for RV64LYA so the E==0 case does not apply
map_note: G-c; malformed predicate and its fail-closed consequences

statement: Representable range check: with source (a, m) decoding to (base, top) and derived (a', m) decoding to (base', top'), a' is representable iff base==base' and top==top'; otherwise the derived capability is invalidated.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; definitional form of the check

statement: Encoding artifact: top != top' iff base != base', so checking either top==top' or base==base' suffices; top[XLEN] need not be checked because output_top[XLEN] = ({input_top[XLEN-1], base[XLEN-1]} == 01); for E > CAP_MAX_E-3 the representability check always passes even though bounds are infinite only at E=CAP_MAX_E; the gap between bounds and representable-range edge is at least s/4, so if an instruction is in pc bounds the next linear instruction is representable.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; implementation simplifications of the representability comparator that an RTL proof must justify

statement: NULL encoding is zero in all fields (tag, SDP, AP, CT, EF, L8, T, TE, B, BE, address, reserved), implying E=CAP_MAX_E (52) so bounds cover the address space but no permissions are granted; Zylg permissions are presumed absent.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; reset/zero value

statement: Infinite Capability encoding: tag 1, SDP all ones, AP=AP_MAX, CT 0, EF 0, L8 0, T/TE/B/BE zeros, reserved zeros, any address; it is both Root Executable and Root Data and authorizes all memory accesses regardless of address field; Zylg permissions presumed present (may redefine AP_MAX).
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; root value installed at reset

statement: Zcd (RV64) is incompatible with RVY because its 16-bit encodings are reused for C.LY/C.SY/C.LYSP/C.SYSP (Table 34); Zcd, Zcmp and Zcmt are incompatible with RV64Y; on Zyhybrid harts these encodings revert to Zcd in Integral Pointer Mode; the compressed forms behave as LY/SY/JALR/YADDI after expansion.
assumptions: Zca present
map_note: G-c; compressed decoder

statement: In RVY, C.ADDI with rd!=x0 and imm=0, C.SLLI with rd!=x0 and shamt=0, C.SRLI with shamt=0, C.SRAI with shamt=0 are reserved rather than HINTs, because integer arithmetic writing rd!=x0 zeroes the metadata and tag.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; decoder reserved set

statement: LR.Y loads an aligned YLEN value with its tag, sets the reservation as LR.W/D, and forms rd per the LY rules; SC.Y conditionally stores rs2 with its tag following SC.W rules, the written tag may be cleared per the SY rules; both raise access faults on misalignment and the same CHERI fault set as LY/SY; both can propagate valid capabilities that fail integrity (the Sail model currently reserves physical addresses).
assumptions: Zalrsc
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, Chapter 5, lines 4279-4475, Sail note at 4401
map_note: G-c; atomic capability accesses

statement: AMOSWAP.Y is equivalent to an atomically executed LY rd,0(rs1); SY rs2,0(rs1); rd is updated only if no exception is raised; the stored value is the original rs2 even if rd=rs1 or rd=rs2; requires R and W; if C is absent the tag is stored as zero; misaligned raises a store/AMO access fault.
assumptions: Zaamo
map_note: G-c; atomic swap with tag

statement: YSHnADD and YSHnADD.UW increment rs2.address by rs1 (or its unsigned word) shifted by n and clear rd.tag if rs2 is sealed, the result is not exactly representable, or rs2 fails integrity.
assumptions: Zba; listings manually maintained
map_note: G-c; address-generation variants

statement: CBO.CLEAN and CBO.FLUSH require R and W and only that at least one byte of the cache block is within bounds (none-in-bounds faults); CBO.INVAL and CBO.ZERO require every byte of the block within bounds; CBO.INVAL additionally raises Illegal instruction if pc lacks ASR, and a sensible CHERI implementation choice is to always execute CBO.INVAL as CBO.FLUSH because invalidation can re-expose previously stored capabilities.
assumptions: Zicbom
map_note: G-c; cache-maintenance checks

statement: CBO.ZERO stores zeros to the full cache block; an implementation may or may not update the entire block atomically, but each individual write must atomically set the tag of the corresponding naturally aligned YLEN-bit location to zero; requires W, every byte in bounds, tag, unsealed, integrity.
assumptions: Zicboz
map_note: G-c5; tag clearing on block zeroing

statement: PREFETCH.I/R/W never raise exceptions; they are performed only if rs1.tag=1, rs1 unsealed, at least one byte of the block within bounds, the matching permission (X/R/W) is granted and integrity passes; otherwise they execute as nop with no prefetch (rs1=x0 is a nop); in Integral Pointer Mode they are checked against ddc (R/W) or pc (I).
assumptions: Zicbop
map_note: G-c; prefetch must not touch cache state without authorization (side-channel rationale)

statement: Vector extension (RVY): vector registers do not support capability tags, consequently vector stores always set the associated tags in memory to zero; vector load/store must not be used for generic memory copying that must preserve capabilities.
assumptions: V extension; a future extension may allow tags in vector registers
map_note: G-c4; vector stores are tag-clearing, so the VME datapath must clear tags on every store
correction: Codex review of PR #246, Cycle 2: the RVY vector access rules are the stated precedent for the VME ISA goals G-a2 and G-a3 as well as for G-c4.

statement: Vector memory access instructions require capability operands and check permissions and bounds; only active elements are subject to CHERI exception checks; on fault-only-first loads a CHERI exception is raised only if element 0 is active and fails; the x0-base reserved rule applies to all vector memory instructions.
assumptions: V extension; nothing is said about per-element bounds granularity beyond 'active elements', nor about VLEN, strided/indexed element-wise checks, or vector AMOs
map_note: G-c4; this is the entire normative statement on vector checking that AIVHAI's VME proof must refine
correction: Codex review of PR #246, Cycle 2: the RVY vector access rules are the stated precedent for the VME ISA goals G-a2 and G-a3 as well as for G-c4.

statement: Zylg: the GL flag can be cleared when deriving but never set to 1 unless derived from a superset with GL=1; a Root Executable must grant LG and be global; a Root Data must grant LG and SL and be global.
assumptions: Zylg
map_note: G-c; monotonicity of the GL label (if CVA6-CHERI implements Zylg)

statement: Zylg loads: if the authorizing capability lacks LG and the loaded capability is unsealed, both GL and LG are cleared; if sealed, only GL is cleared; applies to LY and every instruction that can load valid capabilities (Table 46).
assumptions: Zylg
map_note: G-c; load-path label stripping

statement: Zylg stores: a valid capability is stored with its tag only if it is global or the authorizing capability grants SL; otherwise it is invalidated (tag cleared) before being stored; applies to SY and all capability-storing instructions (Table 47).
assumptions: Zylg
map_note: G-c; store-path tag filtering

statement: Zylg YPERMC rules: LG valid only if C and R; SL valid only if C and W; GL is treated as a permission by YPERMC/YPERMR but is not subject to the sealed check, so YPERMC can clear GL even on a sealed capability.
assumptions: Zylg
map_note: G-c; permission rules extension

statement: Zyhybrid: the P-bit in pc selects Capability Pointer Mode (P=0) or Integral Pointer Mode (P=1); in Integral mode all data accesses (including LY/SY) are implicitly authorized by ddc with only the address from rs1, fetches by pc, rs1=x0 is permitted, RVC capability encodings revert to Zcd, modified instructions revert to RVI behavior, and non-RVY YLEN CSRs are accessed XLEN-bit with YADDRW semantics.
assumptions: Zyhybrid; implementations without it are always in Capability Pointer Mode
map_note: G-c; hybrid-mode authorization source selection

statement: The P-bit is only valid in capabilities granting X (rule Zyhybrid-1); YPERMC clearing X while P=1 must set P=0; mode changes only when a capability is installed in pc (JALR, YMODESWI, YMODESWY, trap entry/return); YMODEW copies rs1 to rd, clears tag if sealed or integrity fails, and updates P only if rs1 grants X, propagating rs1.tag unchanged; YMODER returns 0 if no X or integrity fails; YMODESW* flip pc.P only if in the other mode.
assumptions: Zyhybrid; YMODESW listing manually maintained
map_note: G-c; mode-bit handling

statement: ddc is a U-mode read-write YLEN CSR that does not require ASR, implicitly checked for all data accesses in Integral Pointer Mode; the EEI initializes it so the program can run (e.g. Root Data); on write it is subject to Invalid address conversion and YADDRW rules (Table 43).
assumptions: Zyhybrid
map_note: G-c; default data capability

statement: Smy is mandatory for all RVY implementations; mtvec is widened, its reset value is nominally Root Executable, and every read (implicit on trap or explicit) forms the observed address with YADDRW semantics (MODE bits, vectored offset up to 4*HICAUSE), so all observable addresses must be exactly representable or the hardware clears the tag; a sealed capability written to mtvec reads back with tag cleared; mtvec is not unsealed when installed in pc.
assumptions: implementations may use WARL to restrict metadata to code-pointer-valid values
map_note: G-c; trap-vector capability

statement: mepc is widened with nominal reset Root Executable; mepc.address[0]=0 and address[1] rules follow IALIGN; software must ensure all possible read values are exactly representable or the tag is cleared on write; sealed capabilities may be written; the capability is invalidated on write if address[0]=1 or address[1]=1 with IALIGN=32; the observable tag of a sealed mepc with address[1]=1 depends on IALIGN; on trap the full pc (tag and metadata) is written to mepc; MRET unseals a sentry mepc into pc.
assumptions: implementations with writable misa.C must legalize xepc on read
map_note: G-c; exception pc save/restore

statement: mscratch, mtidc, sscratch, stidc reset/start with tag=0 and UNSPECIFIED (platform-specified) metadata and address; XLEN writes update them with YADDRW, YLEN writes are direct.
assumptions: UNSPECIFIED reset payload
map_note: G-c; scratch CSR reset

statement: misa.Y is 1 when the base is RVY and is WARL; zero is a legal value only if the metadata of pc, xtvec, xepc (and ddc with Zyhybrid) are at their reset values, so M-mode cannot drop CHERI checks after configuring them; a simpler conforming implementation may refuse to clear misa.Y if any of these were ever written.
assumptions: Smyhybrid makes misa.Y writable
map_note: G-c; CHERI cannot be silently disabled

statement: mstatus restrictions: MXL, SXL, UXL must be read-only (SXL=UXL=MXL, only values 1 and 2) and MBE, SBE, UBE must be read-only (SBE=UBE=MBE or read-only zero) when the base is RVY, because changing XLEN or endianness would change the interpretation of all in-memory capabilities; MXR has no effect on CHERI permission checking.
assumptions: may be relaxed by a future extension
map_note: G-c; fixed XLEN/endianness invariant

statement: New synchronous exception codes: 32 CHERI Instruction Access Fault, 33 CHERI Load Access Fault, 34 CHERI Store/AMO Access Fault, 35 CHERI Load Capability Fault (Svyrg), 36 CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault (Svyrg); medeleg bits 32-36 may delegate them; scause mirrors mcause.
assumptions: 35 and 36 are RV64Y/Svyrg only
map_note: G-c; cause codes

statement: Exception priority (Table 55, decreasing): instruction address breakpoint; CHERI Instruction Access Fault from pc checks (prior to instruction address translation); instruction page/access fault during translation; instruction access fault with physical address; illegal instruction, misaligned, ecall, ebreak, load/store breakpoint; CHERI Load/Store/AMO Access Fault from capability checks (prior to data address translation); capability address misaligned (as access fault); optional misaligned; CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault, page fault or access fault during translation; access fault with physical address; misaligned if not higher; lowest: CHERI Load Capability Fault.
assumptions: pc bounds are checked against all bytes of the fetched instruction; if length cannot be determined the check uses the minimum supported instruction size
map_note: G-c; ordering of checks in the pipeline

statement: Table 56 detailed check set: all instructions first check pc (tag, sealed, X, any byte out of bounds including undecodable bounds, integrity) -> cause 32; CSR*/MRET/SRET/CBO.INVAL -> Illegal instruction if pc lacks ASR; all loads check auth_cap tag/sealed/R/bounds/integrity -> 33 and misaligned capability load -> 5; all stores, atomics and CBOs check tag/sealed/integrity -> 34; stores and CBO.ZERO need W, atomics and CBO.CLEAN/FLUSH/INVAL need R and W; stores/atomics any byte out of bounds, CBO.ZERO/INVAL any block byte out, CBO.CLEAN/FLUSH all block bytes out -> 34; misaligned capability store -> 7; auth_cap is rs1, or ddc in Integral Pointer Mode.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; the exception-check matrix the CVA6-CHERI LSU and fetch unit refine

statement: Speculative execution (non-normative, ARC-NOTE marked): programmers should be able to rely on instructions that fail CHERI permission checks not updating microarchitectural state (e.g. no cache update for a load that fails a bounds check); micro-architects must consider late exception raising, speculation windows, and resulting side channels.
assumptions: explicitly advisory; placement in the spec is under review
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 17.5 CHERI Exceptions and Speculative Execution, lines 6595-6611
map_note: none; the spec does not make this a requirement, and AIVHAI's claims exclude side channels

statement: CHERI PMAs define three levels: CHERI Capability Tag (load and store tags), CHERI Capability Tag Strip (load zero tag, ignore stored tag), CHERI Capability Tag Store Fault (load zero tag, Store/AMO Access Fault when C and W are granted and the to-be-stored capability is valid; for SC.Y the fault is raised if rs2 is valid regardless of reservation outcome); only regions with the CHERI Capability Tag PMA require tag storage.
assumptions: which regions carry which PMA is platform/EEI-defined
map_note: G-c5; tag storage coverage and behaviour on untagged regions

statement: Ssy is mandatory with S-mode; stvec and sepc are handled identically to mtvec and mepc (sepc applying to SRET); SRET reads the full YLEN sepc and unseals a sentry before return; MRET/SRET raise Illegal instruction if pc lacks ASR.
assumptions: S-mode present
map_note: G-c; supervisor trap state

statement: CHERI checks are made on the effective address of the current translation scheme (virtual if translation enabled, physical otherwise); implicit page-table-walker accesses are not subject to CHERI checks; SFENCE.* and SINVAL.* are unmodified and ignore metadata and tag of their address operands.
assumptions: future extensions may add checks to the PTW and to SFENCE
map_note: G-c; which accesses are outside the capability check boundary (PTW)

statement: Sv39/Sv48/Sv57 (RVY) allocate the 4-bit pte.rvy field; with pte.y (rvy[3]) = 0 all capability loads return tag zero and all capability stores of valid capabilities raise CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault; with pte.y=1 they operate normally; rvy[2:0] are reserved; translation step 7 checks whether the capability store is allowed by pte.rvy.
assumptions: RV64Y only; RV32Y has no PTE field
map_note: G-c; MMU capability-flow control

statement: Invalid virtual addresses: CSRs and pc need not hold all invalid addresses, but because bounds depend on the address, if the bounds are not infinite implementations must not convert an invalid address to a different invalid address; if bounds cannot be decoded due to an invalid address a CHERI Instruction/Load/Store-AMO Access Fault is raised; on a CSR update with an invalid address and non-infinite bounds the capability is invalidated before writing (implementation-defined whether to invalidate when the invalid address happens to be holdable); jumps to invalid targets with non-infinite bounds clear the target pc tag; data accesses at invalid effective addresses with non-infinite bounds raise CHERI Load/Store faults.
assumptions: implementation-defined invalidation choice in 19.3.1; bounds comparators may be narrowed to the supported VA width
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, 19.3 Invalid Virtual Address Handling, lines 7001-7049
map_note: G-c; canonical-address handling in the comparator

statement: Smyhybrid/Ssyhybrid: effective CHERI enable is M always, S = menvcfg.Y, U = menvcfg.Y & senvcfg.Y; reset values menvcfg.Y=0, senvcfg.Y=0, pc.P=1, ddc at most Root Data, pc/xtvec/xepc at most Root Executable; with CHERI disabled RVY encodings revert to custom, RVY CSRs are unavailable and CSR accesses are XLEN-bit, but implicit accesses and security checks are unaffected: the last pc and ddc written continue to authorize fetch and data accesses, and traps use the full xtvec/xepc capabilities (Table 65).
assumptions: Zyhybrid; the hart is fully RVI-compatible when Y=0 only if pc, xtvec, xepc, ddc remain at reset
map_note: G-c; bounds enforcement persists while CHERI is disabled

statement: Svyrg (optional, RV64Y, implies Sv39) is enabled by sstatus.YRGE and redefines pte.rvy as yr (rvy[0]), yrg (rvy[1]), yw (rvy[2]), yd (rvy[3]); after changing YRGE an SFENCE.VMA x0,x0 suffices to synchronize; Load Capability Faults and Capability Dirty Tracking apply only when YRGE=1, the authorizing capability grants C, and the PMA is CHERI Capability Tag.
assumptions: Svyrg
map_note: G-c; revocation support in the MMU, if implemented

statement: CHERI Load Capability Fault: with pte.yr=0, pte.yrg=0 clears the loaded tag and pte.yrg=1 loads normally; with pte.yr=1 a fault is raised when pte.yrg differs from sstatus.UYRG (pte.u=1) or SYRG (pte.u=0) and the loaded capability is valid, unless the implementation traps conservatively (implementation-defined choice to fault even when the loaded tag is 0); AMOs that would raise both a CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault and a Load Capability Fault take the former.
assumptions: Svyrg; precise vs conservative trapping is implementation-defined; software must tolerate spurious traps
map_note: G-c; data-dependent load trap

statement: Capability Dirty Tracking: with pte.yw=0, stores/AMOs of valid capabilities raise CHERI Store/AMO Page Fault; with pte.yw=1 and pte.yd=0 and a valid to-be-stored capability, Svade raises the page fault and Svadu performs an atomic hardware PTE update setting pte.yd (and pte.a, pte.d); tracking must be triggered in that case and may be triggered when the stored tag is unknown at translation time (SC.Y triggers if rs2 is valid even if the store fails); pte.yd must always be set when a tagged capability is written to the page.
assumptions: Svyrg; Svade or Svadu
map_note: G-c; PTE dirty-bit update atomicity

statement: System-level fundamental rule: the tag and data of every naturally aligned YLEN-bit location are always accessed atomically; it must never be possible to update any data byte without also writing the tag (so a non-CHERI-aware bus master overwriting a capability clears its tag), to read a tag with mismatched stale or newer data, or to set a tag to one without atomically writing the data; clearing a tag without changing the data is permitted provided stale tagged data can never be observed.
assumptions: Appendix C is marked by an ARC-NOTE as possibly moving to supporting documentation
map_note: G-c5; the tag-integrity invariant AIVHAI's DMA/MMU shim and tag storage must satisfy

statement: Bus rules: tag-aware buses carry the tag with the data on reads and writes; non-tag-aware buses do not read tags, and their writes to tagged memory must set the tag of any naturally aligned YLEN-bit location to zero where any byte is overwritten; in the small-system example all writes from the (non-tag-aware, e.g. DMA) system port must clear tags.
assumptions: SoC interconnect design, outside the hart
source: AirdAlmataryAmayaGarciaEtAl-26b, Appendix C and C.1, lines 8009-8017, 8036-8049
map_note: G-c5; NPU/DMA writes must clear tags unless tag-aware

statement: Large-system tag cache: all memory cached and visible to CHERI CPUs must support tags; a DRAM region reserved for tag storage must only be written by the tag cache, so no bus initiator (GPU, peripherals) may write the tag-storage region or the tagged data region without passing through the tag cache (a network-on-chip constraint), though they may read; direct DMA to the tagged region would require root-of-trust authentication, encryption and anti-rollback.
assumptions: example architecture, not a hart requirement
map_note: G-c5; tag-storage write-path exclusivity

statement: Not all memory in a real system supports tags; the EEI defines which regions of the address space support them.
assumptions: implementation/EEI-defined
map_note: G-c5; tag coverage is a platform parameter

statement: Model status: Operation listings are Sail excerpts except those explicitly marked 'manually maintained rather than extracted from the Sail model' (YPERMC, YBNDSWI, YUNSEALS, YSEALE, YTOPR, JAL, JALR, YSHxADD, YSHxADD.UW, CBO.CLEAN/FLUSH/INVAL/ZERO, YMODESW*); the normative bounds pseudocode is 'intentionally simpler than the equivalent definitions in the SAIL model'; the Sail model stores RV64LYA's CT as a boolean and 'currently reserves physical addresses' for LR.Y.
assumptions: the document nowhere declares the Sail model authoritative over the prose, and no test suite, ACT, riscv-arch-test, or proof is mentioned
map_note: A-1; the prose/Sail divergence points that the ISA-model-agrees-with-specification task must reconcile

statement: Document status: v0.9.10 Intermediate Release, 'Stable' state ('assume anything could still change, but limited change should be expected'); several instruction encodings (YBNDSRW, YSEALE, YTOPR, ...) are 'not final and highly likely to change prior to v1.0'; sections 17.5, Appendix A and Appendix C carry open ARC-NOTEs.
assumptions: none
map_note: A-1; version pinning risk for any model AIVHAI builds against

statement: Alternative encoding formats (e.g. for accelerators or micro-controllers) may specify a different representable-range check but must still support one-past-the-end pointers; the ISA therefore uses the phrase 'represented exactly' for the check; RV64Y is expected to have few custom formats.
assumptions: implementation-defined for non-RV64LYA formats
map_note: G-c4; an accelerator (NPU) using its own format is explicitly contemplated but must keep one-past-the-end representability

statement: Integer-add and capability-add have separate encodings so that high-performance implementations with multiple ADD units need not carry the upper operand halves or capability-check logic on integer ADD results.
assumptions: rationale, non-normative
map_note: none; microarchitectural rationale

statement: Bounds expansion from rs1 and bounds checking are expected to run in parallel with address calculation, translation and PMA/PMP checking in a typical load/store unit; metadata modification of loaded capabilities is on naturally aligned data and typically happens in parallel with the alignment multiplexers on the cache read path.
assumptions: implementation guidance, non-normative
map_note: G-c; where in the CVA6 LSU the checks are expected to sit

statement: Implementations may choose to enforce optional integrity checks for instruction-level verification simplicity (deterministic behaviour for all 2^(YLEN+1) input values, analogous to NaN-boxing), resilience with mixed CHERI IP, or reliability reporting.
assumptions: implementation choice
map_note: G-c; determines whether CVA6-CHERI's behaviour on corrupted tagged inputs is fully specified

statement: xepc WARL behaviour allows implementations not to maintain invalid metadata fields in microarchitectural pc copies (JALR may jump to a target with invalid metadata, faulting at the target), with the caveat that fixing too many fields hinders debugging.
assumptions: implementation-defined WARL set
map_note: G-c; permitted abstraction in the fetch-pc datapath

statement: Zylg capability subset extension and YSS/YBLD/YUNSEALS are affected by the GL rule; Zylg's LY/SY constraints apply to every instruction that can load or store valid capabilities (LR.Y, SC.Y, AMOSWAP.Y, compressed forms).
assumptions: Zylg
map_note: G-c; coverage of label rules across all capability memory ops

statement: YLEN-bit CSRs that are code or data pointers (ddc, mtvec, mepc, stvec, sepc) are WARL, need not store full 64-bit addresses on RV64 and may be subject to Invalid address conversion on writing; xtvec writes always apply YADDRW including the MODE field and a vector range check when vectored; xepc YLEN writes are direct if the address did not change.
assumptions: none
map_note: G-c; CSR write legalization

statement: Design-goal statement: CHERI aims at 'formal grounding' and 'strong, non-probabilistic protection' rather than random numbers or truncated hashes; the stated protection properties are provenance, integrity, and monotonicity, with the explicit caveat that not all corrupted states are detected.
assumptions: no formal statement or proof of these properties appears in the document
map_note: RP1; the top-level properties AIVHAI's monotonicity and isolation proofs must formalize

statement: Memory safety, Unforgeable: 'A reference to memory (in particular, the authority to access memory) can be constructed only from other references.'
assumptions: Definitional; realised by tags (§7.7) and roots (§7.13.1)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.1 The CHERIoT RTOS Model, approx line 494
map_note: RP4: this is the tag-unforgeability goal RP4 discharges at the ISA level

statement: Memory safety, Monotonic: 'A constructed reference will have no more authority than its progenitor reference(s) (and may have less).'
assumptions: Definitional; the only mechanised fragment is setCapBounds monotonicity (A26-063)
map_note: RP1: the top-level monotonicity goal; spec gives no instruction-sequence proof

statement: Memory safety, Spatially Safe: 'References to memory authorize access to a set of memory locations determined when the reference is constructed.'
assumptions: Relies on compiler/allocator inserting bounds (§1.2.1, §1.2.4)
map_note: RP2: bounds fixed at derivation and never widened

statement: Memory safety, Temporally Safe: 'References to a region of memory will not remain usable across reuse of memory for a different allocation.'
assumptions: Holds for heap only (allocator + load barrier + revocation sweep); stack allocations 'are not guaranteed to be temporally safe' (L544)
map_note: G-CF: allocator-owned property, outside the ISA-level RP set

statement: TCB for confidentiality and integrity is exactly the loader, the switcher (~300 hand-written assembly instructions) and the memory allocator; compartments 'are not part of the TCB and are assumed to have a mutual distrust relationship with each other'; any code running with interrupts disabled is in the TCB for availability.
assumptions: 'The code in these components must be carefully audited' (no verification claimed)
map_note: G-CF: defines the firmware self-protection boundary AIVHAI's CF proof must cover

statement: Heap spatial safety: 'The allocator ensures that the capabilities it gives out have bounds that do not overlap any other allocation, and so the CHERI bounds checks enforce spatial memory safety.'
assumptions: Allocator correctness is assumed, not verified; a compromised allocator 'can violate safety properties of the heap only' (L540)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.1 Heap memory safety, approx lines 530-540
map_note: G-CF: allocator obligation

statement: Hardware guarantee for heap temporal safety: 'no capability can be loaded if the memory allocator has marked the memory it points to as deallocated' — CLC reads the revocation bit of the capability's base granule and clears the tag if set.
assumptions: Platform defines which address ranges have revocation bits; bases outside them 'will not be revoked'; revocation bits undefined at reset; sealing-format caps excluded
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.1 and §7.8 Temporal safety, CLC semantics, approx lines 530, 1204-1210, 3225-3231
map_note: G-CF: the load-barrier is the ISA half of the allocator's revocation contract; not one of RP1-RP5

statement: Blast-radius bound on the allocator: 'even a completely compromised memory allocator can violate safety properties of the heap only; it cannot directly violate memory safety for non-heap memory' because it 'does not hold capabilities to normal compartment memory'.
assumptions: Loader grants allocator only heap-region capabilities
map_note: G-CF: least-authority structure of the firmware TCB

statement: Stack-derived capabilities 'can not be stored anywhere other than on the stack to which they point'; §1.2.2 says storing to heap or a global 'will deliver a trap'. NOTE: contradicted by v1.0 change Issue 20/PR 26 which makes store-local violations clear the stored tag instead of trapping (L4106).
assumptions: Only stacks, register save areas and trusted stacks carry PERMIT_STORE_LOCAL_CAPABILITY (loader policy); stale 'trap' wording in §1.2.2
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.2 Local stack memory safety, approx line 546; Appendix A, line 4106
map_note: G-c: cross-thread stack isolation; enforcement is RP4-style tag clearing on CSC

statement: Cross-compartment stack safety: 'The stack bounds are restricted so that the callee has no access to the caller's stack, except via capabilities that are explicitly passed as arguments'; the callee-visible stack suffix 'is zeroed both on call and on return'; the stack pointer and stack-derived arguments 'are the only pointers that are both held by a compartment and capable of storing other stack-derived pointers'.
assumptions: Switcher correctness; nested stack pointers inside argument structures are NOT checked by the switcher (§6.1)
map_note: G-c: compartment-switch isolation obligation on the switcher

statement: Lexically-scoped delegation: a caller 'may, for any capability it holds, construct a variant that can only be stored to the stack and can load only capabilities that can be stored only to the stack'; passing it 'ensures that the callee compartment cannot capture either the passed capability or any loaded through it in memory not visible to (and mutable by) the caller after return'.
assumptions: Relies on transitive LG attenuation on CLC (A26-046) and SL store rule (A26-044); the tools 'provide a security benefit only if they are used' (§6.2)
map_note: G-c: delegation/no-capture guarantee built from RP3 (transitive permission attenuation) and RP4

statement: Immutable globals: 'Immutable objects with static storage duration are derived from PCC (with the execute permission removed) and so cannot be written to.'
assumptions: Executable format has no SD permission (Appendix C, ¬(EX∧SD)); memory safety for globals is otherwise 'advisory'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.4 Global memory safety, approx line 564
map_note: RP3: relies on the permission lattice forbidding EX∧SD

statement: High-level security goals: 'No compartment should be able to access another compartment's data, except where explicitly shared' and 'No thread should be able to access another thread's data, except where explicitly shared.'
assumptions: Threat model of mutually distrusting compartments; explicit sharing via capabilities across exposed interfaces
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.5 Higher-level security properties, approx lines 568-572; §2, line 590
map_note: G-c: the two isolation goals AIVHAI's compartment/thread isolation proof targets

statement: Availability goal (qualified): 'Compartments that have not been explicitly granted the rights to run with interrupts disabled should also not be able to impact availability.'
assumptions: 'should'; the scheduler and any interrupts-disabled path are in the availability TCB and must be audited (§6.3)
map_note: none: availability is outside AIVHAI's formal boundary (SL-AIVHAI-P04 keeps it distinct from isolation)

statement: Threat model: 'code running in a compartment is untrusted ... an attacker is assumed to have the ability to execute arbitrary code within a compartment'; all code within a compartment trusts all other code within that compartment (§2.1).
assumptions: Attacker model is arbitrary code inside one compartment; no intra-compartment protection
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §1.2.6 Threat model, approx line 578; §2.1, line 638
map_note: G-c: fixes the adversary AIVHAI's isolation claims are stated against

statement: A compartment is 'defined by the memory that is transitively reachable from the capability registers in the running code' (including memory reachable by any number of capability loads).
assumptions: Definitional
map_note: G-c: the reachability definition the isolation property quantifies over

statement: Interrupts-disabled execution requires explicit grant: 'For a compartment to run code with interrupts disabled, the linker and loader must have explicitly granted it these rights'; the loader must explicitly grant every MMIO region, entry point (with interrupt status), interrupts-disabled internal function, cross-compartment call and library routine, so 'a complete graph of cross-compartment communication' is auditable.
assumptions: Loader and linker correctness; auditing is a firmware-integrator duty
map_note: G-CF: loader-established authority graph; also the auditability premise of the CF model

statement: Two-bit information flow: 'Capabilities without the global bit can be stored only via capabilities that have the store-local permission'; only stacks, register save areas and trusted stacks have store-local; the latter two are 'reachable only from a special capability register'.
assumptions: Loader allocates SL only to these three memory kinds
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §2.2 Threads define temporal ownership, approx lines 644-652
map_note: G-c: thread isolation mechanism; ISA half is RP4 (tag cleared on store-local violation)

statement: Cross-thread isolation: because CGP-derived globals lack store-local, 'it is not possible to construct a capability that is reachable from a global and which points to a stack allocation'; a compromised compartment 'cannot tamper with the victim thread's stack or register file and must use data-oriented attacks from data reachable from globals'.
assumptions: Globals derived from CGP without SL; stacks local
map_note: G-c: thread isolation claim

statement: Sentry opacity: 'A CHERI sentry is a capability that can be jumped to but cannot be used for any other operations'; the switcher sentry 'implicitly disables interrupts on entry'.
assumptions: Sentries are sealed executables (otypes 1-5); all forward sentries 'must have been built by the RTOS loader' (L1488)
map_note: RP5: sentry opacity stated verbatim

statement: Compartment-switch post-condition: at the end of a transition the callee has access only to 'Its own code (PCC)', 'Its own globals (CGP)', 'A portion of the thread's stack, excluding any frames owned by the caller, and full of zeroes', and 'Any memory pointed to by argument capability registers, passed explicitly'; 'On return, any temporary state is cleared and the caller has access only to explicit return capabilities.' Switcher zeroes all non-argument registers except CGP/CSP and saves callee-saves on the trusted stack.
assumptions: Switcher correctness; stack high-water-mark used to reduce zeroing (A26-065); does not prevent deliberate sharing of a global via a read-only capability
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §2.4 Compartment switches enforce compartment isolation, approx lines 678-694
map_note: G-c: the switcher contract AIVHAI's compartment-isolation proof must refine

statement: Context-switch isolation: the context switcher 'is the only code that is able to violate thread isolation'; it seals the register-save-area capability before passing it to the scheduler; 'The loader guarantees that nothing except the switcher has a permit-seal capability for that type and so the scheduler is able only to provide register save areas that were previously provided by the loader or the switcher'; the scheduler 'is therefore in the TCB for availability but, crucially, not for confidentiality or integrity'.
assumptions: Loader sealing-type policy; scheduler 'does not have access to the stacks, trusted stacks, or register-save areas' (L750)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §2.5 Context switches enforce thread isolation, approx lines 704-714; §3, line 750
map_note: G-CF: scheduler is de-privileged by sealing; relies on RP5-style seal unforgeability

statement: Shared-library entry control: 'This is enforced by the loader providing callers with a sentry capability to the jump target. This prevents the caller from being able to jump to arbitrary points in a shared library.'
assumptions: Library runs with caller's CGP, so this is control-flow integrity not data isolation
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §2.6 Adding shared libraries, approx line 730
map_note: RP5: sentry as call gate

statement: Privilege confinement: 'only the loader and the switch routines run with access to the trusted stack and register save areas (that is, with the access-system-registers permission on their PCC) ... these are the only two that can completely compromise all of the security properties'; the loader 'runs once on system start and then erases itself'.
assumptions: Loader not needed where persistent storage holds tags
map_note: G-CF: minimal SR-bearing TCB

statement: Loader derivation discipline: 'Each capability that is derived from a root is derived via a mechanism that validates (at compile time) that the requested permissions are less than the permissions of the root'; on exit the loader stub 'zeroes all of the memory used by the loader (stack, code, and globals) and almost all of the register file, ensuring that no capabilities are leaked'.
assumptions: C++ template typing, not a verified check; 'almost all' of the register file
map_note: G-CF: loader self-protection and no-leak obligation

statement: Import table confinement: the import table 'is the only piece of state reachable from a compartment that is allowed to contain capabilities that point outside of the compartment's PCC and CGP on system start'; it 'is mutable only by the loader. After the loader finishes it is reachable only by the read-execute PCC for the compartment, not by any capabilities with store permission'.
assumptions: Loader-established; relies on ¬(EX∧SD)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §5.4 Import table layout, approx line 971
map_note: G-c: single audit point for the compartment graph; immutability rests on RP3's lattice

statement: Explicit interrupt posture across security contexts: 'Exports from compartments must set either the interrupts-enabled or interrupts-disabled bit. Code running in a different security context always runs with an explicit interrupt status'; cross-compartment calls default to enabled.
assumptions: Compiler/linker fill export flags; shared-library exports may inherit
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §5.3 Export table layout, approx line 963; §4.3, line 888
map_note: G-CF: interrupt-posture invariant of the switcher

statement: Relocation representability: auipcc and the following 12-bit-immediate instruction 'must both displace the PCC in the same direction, keeping the intermediate capability in bounds and hence representable'; the auipcc shift is reduced by one so immediates always have matching signs.
assumptions: Linker enforces sign matching; relocation range < 2^31
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §5.2 Access to globals and §7.12, approx lines 924-926, 1308
map_note: none: toolchain correctness (avoids spurious tag loss), not an authority property

statement: Instruction fetch gating: 'If PCC becomes untagged or the instruction is not entirely within the bounds of PCC, then an exception is raised', accounting for 2- vs 4-byte instructions; jumps and branches themselves perform no bounds check (v1.0, Issue 23/18, PR 37).
assumptions: Bounds error surfaces at the fetch after the jump, not at the jump
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.5, approx line 1164; CJALR Notes, line 3107; Appendix A, line 4110
map_note: RP1: PCC authority is checked on every fetch so a jump cannot escape bounds

statement: MEPCC tag cleared on instruction-fetch bounds violation 'to avoid violating capability monotonicity' because the faulting PC 'might be unrepresentable'; MEPCC.address still holds the faulting address, its bounds are undefined.
assumptions: Chosen 'to simplify hardware while preserving capability monotonicity'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.5, §7.11, §7.13.5, approx lines 1164-1170, 1269, 1594; Appendix A line 4110
map_note: RP2/RP1: exception path must not synthesise a widened PCC

statement: CJALR target rules: 'It checks that the target capability is tagged and executable before it is installed in PCC. If the target is sealed with one of the reserved sentry types then it is unsealed before jumping to it ... If it is sealed with a non-sentry type an exception is raised'; a sealed target with non-zero immediate raises a seal violation.
assumptions: None stated
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.5, approx line 1172; CJALR semantics/exceptions, lines 2956-2967, 3083-3101
map_note: RP5: sentries unsealed only by jump; non-sentry seals cannot be entered

statement: PCC integrity: 'The checks on CJALR and special capability writes (Section 7.10) prevent execution with a PCC that is sealed or lacks PERMIT_EXECUTE. The only ways for PCC to become untagged is by MRET with an untagged MEPCC or exception with untagged MTCC. The latter will result in an unrecoverable exception loop.'
assumptions: Relies on MTCC/MEPCC write validation (A26-037)
map_note: RP1/G-c: PCC is always a tagged, unsealed, executable capability

statement: Memory access gating: every load/store raises an exception if the base capability 'has the tag unset', 'is sealed', 'does not have the appropriate memory permissions', or 'has bounds that do not cover the entire region being accessed'.
assumptions: Region check is on the full access width (CLC/CSC: address+imm ≥ base and address+imm+CLEN/8 ≤ top)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.6, approx lines 1180-1188; CLC/CSC exceptions, lines 3269-3281, 3476-3488
map_note: RP2/G-c: spatial-safety enforcement point

statement: Tag unforgeability in memory: 'The tag bits are not accessible directly and may be set to one only by a store of a tagged capability using CSC. To prevent tampering with valid capabilities in memory, non-capability stores (e.g. CSW) clear the tag bits for the capability-aligned region(s) they touch. If an unaligned store crosses a capability alignment boundary then two tag bits need to be cleared.'
assumptions: Platform defines tag-supporting regions; elsewhere 'capability stores will silently drop the tag, and capability loads will always return untagged values'; tag bits undefined at reset so software should zero memory
map_note: RP4: data writes clear tags, stated verbatim

statement: Register-file tag discipline: instructions that produce integers 'write a NULL capability (Section 7.13.6) with the address set to the integer result'; 'At reset the registers are initialized to the NULL capability'; CClearTag and CSetHigh always yield an untagged result.
assumptions: None
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.3, approx line 1156; CClearTag line 2502; CSetHigh line 3839
map_note: RP4: no integer-producing instruction can mint a tag

statement: System-register gating: with PERMIT_ACCESS_SYSTEM_REGISTERS unset on PCC, access to any CSR outside the allowlist (cycle/time/instret/hmpcounter read-only; fflags/frm/fcsr), to any SCR via CSpecialRW, to mshwm/mshwmb, or executing MRET 'will cause a PERMIT_ACCESS_SYSTEM_REGISTERS exception'.
assumptions: Machine mode only; no S/U modes
map_note: G-CF: SR permission is the privilege boundary of the switcher/loader

statement: MTCC/MEPCC write validation: 'If the capability being written is sealed or does not have PERMIT_EXECUTE then its tag is cleared'; misaligned low address bits are cleared and the tag is cleared; 'These rules avoid potential problems due to legalisation where capabilities might become unrepresentable or sealed capabilities modified'; vectored mode unsupported.
assumptions: Direct trap mode only
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.10, approx lines 1257-1263; §7.13.5 line 1596; CSpecialRW semantics lines 3911-3930; Appendix A line 4112
map_note: RP1: legalisation can never widen or unseal; supports A26-032

statement: Reserved bit: 'This is zero in the root capabilities (and hence all tagged capabilities), but may be set if untagged data is loaded into a register. In this case its value must be preserved' so that CLC/CSC 'faithfully copy arbitrary untagged data'.
assumptions: prop_decEnc: bits→Capability→bits preserves bits and tag, 'vital ... to ensure that memcpy works'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, Figure 7.2, approx line 1321; B.1 line 4787
map_note: none: data-fidelity invariant, not an authority property (though needed for RP4 bit-exactness arguments)

statement: USER_PERM0 'may be cleared by CAndPerm and cannot be set after being cleared'.
assumptions: Software-defined meaning
map_note: RP3: a permission bit, once dropped, is unrecoverable

statement: Store-local rule: GLOBAL-lacking (local) capabilities 'may be stored only via capabilities with the PERMIT_STORE_LOCAL_CAPABILITY permission. Otherwise, attempting to store a local capability (with GL unset) will store the capability with the tag cleared' (CSC: stored tag 'forcibly cleared' when authority lacks SL and cs2 lacks GL).
assumptions: v1.0 changed this from a trap to tag clearing (Issue 20/PR 26) 'because it removes the possibility of a trap when copying untrusted inputs'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1 GL/SL, approx lines 1354-1356; CSC lines 3382, 3436; Appendix A line 4106
map_note: RP4/G-c: silent tag-clear is the thread-isolation enforcement point

statement: Transitive read-only (LM): 'If PERMIT_LOAD_MUTABLE is not set then any tagged capabilities loaded via this capability will have SD and LM cleared. Thus, if SD and LM are cleared on a capability then it, and any capability loaded via it (including via indirection), will be read-only.' Untagged or sealed loaded capabilities 'are unaffected and retain their existing SD and LM bits'.
assumptions: Sealing 'stops this transitivity' (CLC comment)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1 LM, approx line 1358; CLC semantics lines 3200-3217; F.2.2 line 5108
map_note: RP3: loads can only attenuate permissions, never add

statement: Transitive locality (LG): 'If PERMIT_LOAD_GLOBAL is not set then any tagged capabilities loaded via this capability will have LG and GL cleared'; for loaded sealed capabilities 'GL, but not LG, is cleared, making this an exception to the immutability of sealed capabilities'; untagged unaffected.
assumptions: 'Software accepting sealed capabilities must be prepared to receive local (that is, GLOBAL-lacking) variants, even if none were ever explicitly constructed' (Issue 14)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1 LG, approx line 1360; CLC lines 3169-3195; Appendix A line 4128
map_note: RP3: attenuation-only; RP5 caveat: sealed immutability has exactly this GL exception

statement: Capability-load/store permission (MC): 'The CLC instruction logically ANDs the tag of the loaded capability with MC from the capability base operand, so only capabilities with MC and LD set can be used to load tagged capabilities. The CSC instruction raises an exception if the stored capability has the tag set and the capability base operand lacks either MC or SD permission.' When the tag is cleared for lack of MC the loaded value is not further attenuated (Issue 13).
assumptions: None
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1 MC, approx lines 1362-1368; CLC lines 3126, 3165; CSC line 3400; Appendix A line 4126
map_note: RP4: tags propagate only through MC-bearing authority

statement: Compressed-permission encoding invariants: each format has fixed bits that 'unambiguously identify the format'; 'it is not possible to have a single capability with all permissions'; exactly three roots ⊤M (memory), ⊤X (executable), ⊤S (sealing) with whole-address-space bounds; Appendix C constraints MC→(LD∨SD), LG→(MC∧LD), LM→(MC∧LD), SL→(MC∧SD), SR→EX, EX→(MC∧LD), ¬(EX∧SD), ¬((SE∨US∨U0)∧(LD∨SD)); 33 useful combinations, write-only+store-local dropped to fit 5 bits.
assumptions: Figure 7.5 lattice 'ordered by inclusion' with edges labelled by the dropped permission; GL orthogonal
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1, approx lines 1374-1406; Appendix C lines 5007-5011
map_note: RP3: the permission lattice; W^X (¬(EX∧SD)) and memory/sealing disjointness are structural

statement: CAndPerm attenuation: the result 'will have a (possibly empty) subset of the requested permissions'; 'Any permissions that cannot be encoded using the chosen format are dropped'; SMT prop_andperms: for any capability and mask, new permissions ⊆ original ∧ mask after encode/decode.
assumptions: Checked on untagged bit patterns (capBitsToCapability(false, b)); six-step encoding procedure L1414-1424
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1, approx lines 1412-1426; CAndPerm line 2422; B.1 line 4798
map_note: RP3: the one permission-monotonicity lemma that is machine-checked

statement: Permission-legalisation consistency: 'legalization of permissions must happen at all points where permissions can change (CAndPerm and CLC) ... the result of CAndPerm followed by CGetPerm should be consistent regardless of whether the register file stores the permissions in the compressed or decompressed form. Similarly, storing then loading a capability should not change the permissions except possibly GL, LG, LM and SD as specified by CLC.'
assumptions: Clearing SD may switch format and clear SL 'as a side-effect'
map_note: RP3: implementation obligation that no path observes un-legalised permissions

statement: Sealed immutability: 'A sealed capability cannot be modified or used as authority for operations except special unsealing ones, but can be passed as a token and later unsealed.' Mechanised per-instruction: CIncAddr/CSetAddr/CSetBounds*/CSeal on a sealed cs1 clear the tag (clearTagIfSealed); CAndPerm on a sealed cs1 clears the tag unless the mask clears only GL; loads/stores via a sealed authority trap.
assumptions: Two sanctioned exceptions: CAndPerm clearing only GL (Issue 70/PR 83) and CLC clearing GL via an LG-lacking authority (Issue 14)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.2, approx line 1432; CAndPerm lines 2422-2470; CIncAddr 2766; CSetAddr 3588; CSetBounds 3625; CSeal 3507; Appendix A line 4144
map_note: RP5: sentries/sealed tokens are opaque; RP1: no sealed-cap mutation path

statement: CSeal authority: result tagged only if cs2 is tagged, unsealed, has PERMIT_SEAL, cs2.address ∈ [cs2.base, cs2.top), and the otype is permitted for cs1's format; otherwise 'the tag field of cd is cleared'; sealing 'allows pointers to be made ... unforgeable by anyone who lacks the matching permit-seal capability'.
assumptions: Sealing root ⊤S bounds cover the full space though only otypes 1-7/9-15 are usable (out-of-range sealed sealing-format caps serve as software tokens)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.2, approx line 1434; CSeal lines 3507-3567; §6.2 line 1092; §7.13.1 line 1384
map_note: RP5/RP4: seal unforgeability

statement: CUnseal authority: result tagged only if cs2 tagged, unsealed, has PERMIT_UNSEAL, and cs1.otype lies within cs2's bounds (v1.0: no longer exact address equality); 'If cs2.perms does not grant GLOBAL then cd.perms is stripped of GLOBAL'.
assumptions: Issue 71/PR 87: 'The address of a sealing-root capability is now meaningful only to CSeal'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.2 line 1434; CUnseal lines 4053-4083; Appendix A line 4136
map_note: RP5: unsealing requires matching authority and cannot add GL

statement: otype applicability: 'The otypes 1-7 can only be applied to executable capabilities, while memory and sealing format capabilities can only be sealed with otypes 9-15 ... An attempt to use CSeal or CUnseal with a reserved otype, or with an otype not applicable to the capability format, will clear the capability tag.'
assumptions: otype 8 reserved; 3-bit field with implicit bit 3 for non-executables
map_note: RP5: sentry otypes exist only on executables

statement: CJALR register-selector rules (anti recursive-return attack): function return (cd=$cnull, cs1=$cra) only to backward sentries (4,5); tail call (cd=$cnull, cs1≠$cra) and outlined call (cd∉{$cnull,$cra}) only to unsealed or IRQ-inheriting forward sentry (0,1); call with cd=$cra to unsealed or any forward sentry (0-3); CJAL/CJALR generate a backward sentry (4/5 per current MIE) iff cd=$cra, otherwise an unsealed link; hence 'all forward sentries in the system must have been built by the RTOS loader'.
assumptions: Motivated by the availability attack where 'the callee will call itself on return all the while operating with interrupts disabled' (PR 54, Issue 85/PR 86); compilers 'must be careful to use matching entry and exit CJALRs'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.2, approx lines 1464-1490; CJALR semantics lines 2934-2952, 2995-3020; Appendix A lines 4132-4134
map_note: RP5: forward sentries cannot be minted by untrusted code; backward sentries only by jump

statement: Interrupt posture via sentries: jumping to an interrupt-disabling sentry (otype 2 or 4) clears mstatus.MIE, to an enabling sentry (3 or 5) sets it, inheriting (1) leaves it; the link register written to $cra 'is sealed as a sentry of the type corresponding to the current value of mstatus.MIE'.
assumptions: None
map_note: G-CF/RP5: interrupt state is restored on return by construction of the backward sentry

statement: Bounds-encoding invariant: 'The ISA is constructed to ensure that, for valid capabilities, a and t are in the representable range and b ≤ t'; the top-bit corrections 'ensure that the decoded bounds remain the same provided the address is in [b, b + 2^(e+9))'; root memory cap decodes to [0, 2^32); 'no valid capability will ever exceed this length'.
assumptions: Decoded top is 33 bits; E=15 maps to effective e=24
map_note: RP2: the well-formedness invariant every bounds-mutating instruction must preserve

statement: Representability-check invariant: 'We also wish to maintain the monotonicity invariant that the bounds of a valid capability must be a subset of the bounds of the valid capability from which it is derived. Therefore, whenever the address of a capability changes the hardware must check whether the new address remains within the representable range'; AUIPCC, AUICGP, CSetAddr, CIncAddr clear the tag when the new address is outside it.
assumptions: prop_setaddr: representable-flag ⇒ bounds unchanged (converse not required: 'a conservative implementation ... may return false even though the bounds are unchanged'); prop_repbounds: flag ⇔ (E max ∨ b ≤ a < b+2^(e+9)) for caps produced by setCapBounds from the root
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.3 line 1513; §7.13.5 approx lines 1578-1590; CIncAddr 2766; CSetAddr 3588; B.1 lines 4880-4970
map_note: RP2/RP1: address mutation cannot widen bounds; the stated 'monotonicity invariant'

statement: Minimum representable range: 'The representable range always includes top ... Therefore the representation meets the C-language requirement that pointers may range within object bounds or one byte past the end'; 'if e is 24 then all addresses are representable'.
assumptions: Quantified over caps derived from the root by setCapBounds with sane top
map_note: none: usability guarantee (no spurious tag loss), not an authority bound

statement: Link-capability representability: for CJAL/CJALR the link register 'is guaranteed to be representable because its address can be at most equal to PCC.top given that the jump itself is in bounds. Therefore no representability check is required'; the Sail asserts 'Link cap should always be representable' and 'should always be unsealed'.
assumptions: Sail assert, not an SMT property; relies on A26-029 (fetch in bounds) and A26-032 (PCC unsealed)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.5, approx line 1592; CJAL lines 2858-2863; CJALR lines 2985-2991
map_note: RP2: return capabilities never widen beyond PCC

statement: CSetBounds/CSetBoundsImm rounding: 'If the resulting capability cannot be represented exactly the base will be rounded down and the length will be rounded up by the smallest amount needed to form a representable capability covering the requested bounds. The tag field of the result is cleared if the bounds of the result exceed the bounds of cs1, or if cs1 was sealed.' SMT prop_setbounds: result encodable, address = requested base, and (exact ∧ bounds equal) ∨ (¬exact ∧ b2 ≤ reqBase ∧ reqTop ≤ t2).
assumptions: Restricted to reqTop ≤ 2^32 ('saneTop'); exponent selection e = 23 − clz(l) with +1 retry when T−B overflows 2^9−1 (§7.13.4)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.4, approx lines 1523-1568; CSetBounds line 3625; CSetBoundsImm line 3766; B.1 lines 4830-4851
map_note: RP2: the bounds-setting rounding guarantee

statement: CSetBounds monotonicity under rounding: SMT prop_setbounds_monotonic — for any two successive setCapBounds requests from the memory root, if the second request lies within the first result's bounds then the second result's bounds lie within the first result's bounds. The spec states this 'is really only the inductive step of a monotonicity proof that relies on the fact that setCapBounds only produces canonical encodings ... This also requires that nothing else produces capabilities with non-canonical bounds encodings'; base case prop_setbounds_monotonic_root and prop_setboundsrounddown_canonical are referenced but not listed.
artifact: SMT (prop_setbounds_monotonic; prop_setbounds_monotonic_root and prop_setboundsrounddown_canonical referenced only)
assumptions: Canonical-encoding hypothesis on all other producers; 'some encodings are invalid and won't be generated by setCapBounds, in particular when the exponent is at the maximum and T > B'
map_note: RP2: the closest the spec comes to a bounds-monotonicity proof; AIVHAI must supply the global canonicity invariant

statement: CSetBounds checks the requested, not rounded, bounds: 'the resulting bounds may be larger than the requested bounds, which could potentially lead to non-monotonic behaviour. However, providing that setCapBounds always returns the most precise encodable bounds it is safe to do the check on the requested bounds because, in the worst case, it would return the existing bounds.'
assumptions: 'most precise encodable bounds' is asserted, not SMT-checked as such; applies to CSetBounds, CSetBoundsImm, CSetBoundsExact
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, CSetBounds Notes, approx lines 3653-3661; CSetBoundsExact line 3704; CSetBoundsImm line 3792
map_note: RP2: a hand argument AIVHAI should discharge mechanically

statement: CSetBoundsExact: 'If the resulting capability cannot be represented exactly, the tag field will be cleared (unlike CSetBounds)'; tag also cleared if result exceeds cs1 or cs1 sealed.
assumptions: Exact flag from setCapBounds (checked in prop_setbounds)
map_note: RP2: exact variant never silently widens

statement: CSetBoundsRoundDown: length replaced 'with a representable value no larger than the value in the integer register rs2. That length will be nonzero if rs2 is nonzero'; 'the results of setCapBoundsRoundDown are always a subset of the requested range'; largest representable span capped at exponent 14; 'software should depend only on the result being representable and of non-zero length'.
assumptions: Exponent-14 cap 'may revisit'
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, CSetBoundsRoundDown, approx lines 3723-3746; Appendix A line 4142
map_note: RP2: shrink-only bounds derivation

statement: CRRL/CRAM soundness: for any requested length, rounding base down by the CRAM mask and length up by CRRL yields an exact setCapBounds with newLen ≥ reqLen (SMT prop_crrl_cram); CRRL may round to 2^xlen and return zero.
assumptions: saneTop and (reqLen=0 ∨ newLen≠0)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, CRAM/CRRL, approx lines 3323, 3353; B.1 lines 4972-5001
map_note: none: allocator-support correctness, feeds the allocator's non-overlap obligation (A26-006)

statement: NULL capability: 'an untagged capability with an address of zero and an encoding of all zeroes'; decodes as 'untagged, unsealed capability, with no permissions, base 0 and length 0'; 'NULL-derived capabilities with a non-zero address may have non-zero base and top, but will be untagged'. SMT prop_nullzero and prop_null_noperms.
assumptions: Nullary properties
map_note: RP4: integers are untagged, permissionless bit patterns

statement: Root capabilities are encodable: prop_mem_root, prop_exe_root, prop_seal_root (validateRootCap) hold; roots have whole-address-space bounds; SCRs reset to the roots (MTCC=⊤X, MTDC=⊤M, MScratchC=⊤S, MEPCC=⊤X) and PCC resets to ⊤X.
assumptions: Nullary
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.1 lines 1380-1397; Table 7.2 line 1242; B.1 lines 4777-4783
map_note: G-CF: all initial authority sits in SR-gated SCRs held by the loader

statement: Stack high-water mark invariant: the RTOS maintains 'an invariant that the stack between mshwmb and mshwm for each thread is always zeroed'; hardware updates mshwm on every write with mshwmb ≤ addr < mshwm; the unaligned-store-spanning-mshwmb corner case is NOT handled by hardware because 'the RTOS will never issue a capability to untrusted code that crosses the stack base'.
assumptions: Only the store address, not width, is tracked; relies on loader never creating a capability crossing the stack base
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.15 Stack high water mark, approx lines 1644-1650; Appendix A line 4130
map_note: G-CF: switcher zeroing optimisation rests on a loader invariant

statement: Sealing-type separation from revocation: 'The base of sealing capabilities refers to a distinct namespace to that of memory capabilities, therefore they are not revoked'; CLC excludes caps with SE/US/U0 from the revocation check.
assumptions: 'Software should take care not to reallocate sealing capabilities unless there is some other mechanism to revoke previously issued ones'
map_note: G-CF: allocator/loader must never reuse sealing types

statement: Zero-length capability caveat: 'zero length capabilities can be derived with base equal to the top of an existing capability, even though that capability does not authorize access to top' so an allocator 'has no way to tell which of the two ranges it was derived from' and revocation sweeps cannot revoke them; use is 'strongly discourage[d]'.
assumptions: inCapBounds(cap, top, 0) returns true by definition (L2273)
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §7.13.7 Zero length capabilities, approx line 1608; §9.3 line 2273
map_note: RP4: a stated unforgeability weakness for zero-length tokens AIVHAI must exclude or model

statement: Zero-permission capability caveat: 'the ability to derive the same capability from either a memory or a sealing root may break the expected unforgeability property'; such caps are not revoked; 'support may be removed in future revisions'.
assumptions: Encoded in sealing format regardless of origin root
map_note: RP4: a stated unforgeability weakness

statement: Compartment error handling: a fault in a compartment invokes that compartment's error handler, which may resume with an amended register context 'or ... unwind the trusted stack, returning an error to the calling compartment'; the export table carries the handler offset.
assumptions: Details and 'special security considerations' deferred to RTOS documentation
source: AmarAndersonChenEtAl-26, §3.6 Error handling, approx line 818; §5.3 line 945
map_note: G-CF: fault-path self-protection of the switcher

statement: Argument validation at compartment entry: 'The compartment switcher will check that these are not passed as direct arguments' (stack capabilities into the callee's region), but pointers reached through argument structures are not checked and 'The victim must check this' with check_pointer (tagged, unsealed, sufficient permissions, not on the current compartment's stack).
assumptions: Shared-stack design: 'The caller has access to all of the callee's stack prior to a call'
map_note: G-c: a stated gap in switcher enforcement, left to compartment code

statement: A compartment is a black box whose code may be malicious or arbitrarily buggy; security must come from CHERI and the trusted compartment machinery, not from trusting the compartment.
assumptions: Threat-model premise; first version; availability excluded
map_note: G-CF: adversary model under which the goal is stated

statement: Main guarantee: a compromised compartment can only exercise the non-I/O authority assigned to it during bootstrap plus the I/O buffers supplied for its current invocation.
assumptions: Availability out of scope; synchronous invocation; purecap workloads
map_note: G-CF: this is the firmware-layer statement of G-CF

statement: After bootstrap a compartment cannot acquire new non-I/O authority; non-I/O authority is closed and cannot increase (rule 6).
assumptions: No general runtime capability-transfer mechanism exists
map_note: GAP-4: closure holds only because runtime delegation is absent by design

statement: A compartment cannot cause its capabilities to escape into arbitrary system state; capabilities cannot escape through ordinary I/O (rule 9).
assumptions: I/O buffers carry no valid capabilities
map_note: G-CF: no other compartment or the OS obtains this compartment's capabilities

statement: Availability is out of scope for the first version; once invoked a compartment runs until it returns and may loop forever; timeout, preemption, forced termination and availability isolation are future requirements (rule 11).
assumptions: Single synchronous invocation model
map_note: GAP-1: preemption and shared compartments explicitly deferred

statement: A compartment is statically defined at build time: code, globals and static data, stack, captable/GOT storage, optional heap or scratch (rule 2).
assumptions: Static linking; concrete capabilities may be created at bootstrap
map_note: G-CF: fixes the set of private resources the goal protects

statement: Permitted non-I/O authority is statically declared: MMIO, auxv capabilities, device capabilities, ASR only if explicitly required.
assumptions: Watson asks that 'architectural privilege' (get/set of key CSRs) be named explicitly; Almatary says it is covered under declared authority policy
map_note: G-CF4: ASR is a declared, default-off privilege

statement: Compartments use CHERI purecap; there is no DDC-based ambient authority (rule 4).
assumptions: Davis asks whether this holds if the compartment is untrusted; Almatary: workloads assumed recompiled purecap, and even a non-purecap or malicious blob can reach only its bootstrap caps and I/O buffer caps
map_note: G-CF4: no DDC at entry

statement: PCC restricts executable code; other capabilities installed in compartment memory or passed via argument registers provide private data and explicitly granted authority.
assumptions: Capabilities passed indirectly after bootstrap are prohibited
map_note: G-CF4: PCC bounded at entry

statement: The compartment CRT may construct or corrupt its own captable/GOT; this is acceptable because it can manipulate only capabilities it already has and cannot manufacture authority not available during bootstrap (rule 5).
assumptions: Watson: captable entries are probably sealed, so they can be replaced but not directly manipulated; clarified as init_globals population
map_note: G-CF: captable is linkage state, not a source of externally granted authority

statement: There is no general runtime capability-transfer mechanism; the only new capabilities after bootstrap are invocation-time input/output buffer capabilities (rule 7).
assumptions: Watson: temporary delegation of authority for I/O buffers will eventually be needed to avoid copies; signposted, not adopted
map_note: GAP-4: runtime delegation is the signposted future change

statement: Compartments have no ASR permission by default; privileged system-register access must be explicitly declared and granted (rule 10).
assumptions: Watson wants ASR for an eventual OpenSBI compartment; not in first two red-team exercises
map_note: G-CF4: no ASR at entry

statement: I/O buffers carry data, not capabilities: no valid capabilities in either input or output buffers, so an input buffer cannot introduce arbitrary capabilities and an output buffer cannot be used to leak capabilities (rule 8).
assumptions: Enforced by stripping the capability permission from buffer capabilities
map_note: G-CF4: data-only I/O buffers

statement: Calling convention: apart from the explicit caller's argument capabilities, no registers may hold any other capabilities from previous code execution or state at entry, and the same on return.
assumptions: 'Will need to be thoroughly defined and implemented'; added after Watson's register-scrubbing comment
map_note: G-CF4: registers scrubbed at entry and return

statement: No stack or memory clearing is anticipated during the lifetime of a compartment.
assumptions: Almatary's own comment: unless a compartment is invoked by different OSes or processes, where caller A could corrupt state that caller B then inherits; whether this is a threat is undecided
map_note: GAP-1: shared compartments across callers is the unresolved case

statement: Capability containment: a compartment may copy and derive capabilities within capability-bearing state it is authorised to use (stack, globals, captable/GOT, heap/scratch); persistent compartment capabilities remain inside known capability-bearing state or explicitly granted regions.
assumptions: Isolation should hold by construction, not by audit
map_note: G-CF: bounds the reachable capability graph

statement: Lifecycle: build, bootstrap, authority closed, ready, (+I/O caps) running, return, ready, destroy, destroyed.
assumptions: Destruction appendix marked optional
map_note: GAP-9: destruction state exists but is not part of the core design

statement: Once quiescent, compartment-owned capability-bearing state can be erased (rule 12).
assumptions: Quiescence means it cannot be invoked again
map_note: GAP-9: reuse after erasure not specified

statement: Because capabilities cannot escape, destruction does not require general system-wide capability revocation (rule 13).
assumptions: Davis: the precondition is hard to prove (no instruction executed while holding a cap-writable capability to outside memory); Almatary: globally forbid cap-writable capabilities to anything outside, provable for bootstrapping, and the trampoline strips cap-write (or capability) permission on invocation
map_note: A-5: the cap-writable-to-outside prohibition is exactly the bootstrap invariant A-5 demands

statement: Destruction procedure: disable invocation, optional authority audit, clear owned memory, clear saved CPU state, discard current I/O caps, discard trusted roots.
assumptions: Owned mutable state = globals, stack, captable/GOT, heap, scratch; device MMIO regions are not compartment-owned RAM and are not zeroed; device reset is separate
map_note: GAP-9: destruction and reuse procedure, optional and unreviewed

statement: Open question: the core rules should say something specifically about exceptions and safe handling.
assumptions: Raised by Watson; no text added
map_note: G-CF4: trap path is a boundary crossing with no stated invariant

statement: OpenSBI is not itself a compartment at first; it creates the compartments for workloads; OpenSBI as a privileged compartment may come later; a future requirement for compartments to call OpenSBI or Linux services is a similar worry to rule 13.
assumptions: Decision was to keep the design as easy and static as possible
map_note: GAP-4: any service call path reopens runtime authority flow

statement: Demo protection BOUNDS: the compartment PCC is bounded (weakened variant leaves PCC bounds covering all memory).
